body.translated_text: <s>Ratnatrayaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Three Jewels)
Composed by <s>Śrīkaṇṭhasūri</s>
Together with the <s>Ratnatrayollekhinī</s> (Illumination of the Three Jewels) composed by <s>Aghoraśivācārya</s>

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Śiva</s>, the auspicious one who illuminates the meaning of the <s>Siddhānta</s>,
the purpose of the <s>Ratnatrayaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Three Jewels) is briefly illuminated.
By some through the perspective of the <s>Vedas</s>, by others through the intellect of tradition, by yet others following <s>Nyāya</s> (logic),
and by still others through their own reasoning, the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>) have been tainted by delusion.
Therefore, for the adornment of the ears of the learned, once again through proper exposition,
polished on the whetstone of correct analysis, I now make them radiant.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya śaktyai ca bindave śāśvatāya ca |
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Śakti</s>, to <s>Bindu</s>, and to the Eternal One,
to the Guru, to <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and to the wise <s>Kārtikeya</s>. || 1 ||

children.text: atra ca pūrvārddhena prakaraṇapratipādyaṃ ratnatrayaṃ prastāvayan praṇamati |
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half [of the verse], introducing the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>) as the subject of the treatise, he offers salutation.
In the second half, to the Guru, the blessed Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s>, who is the revealer of all the <s>Saṃhitās</s>,
and to <s>Gaṇapati</s> who removes all obstacles, and to
<s>Kārtikeya</s> whose knowledge is distinguished by hearing the <s>Siddhānta</s> scriptures—he pays homage for the unobstructed completion of this [work]. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: He declares that very triad of substances as the subject to be expounded—

children.translated_text: The three [jewels] called <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>, drawn from the ocean of <s>Siddhānta</s>,
[are presented] for the virtuous to hold always in heart, throat, and ears. || 2 ||

children.text: karṇayoḥ śravaṇena, kaṇṭhopalakṣitavāgindriye pāṭhena, hṛdyavadhānena satāṃ
children.translated_text: By 'hearing' in the ears, by 'recitation' in the organ of speech indicated by 'throat,' and by 'attention' in the heart—for the virtuous
to hold—the jewels beginning with <s>Bindu</s> are drawn up from the ocean of <s>Siddhānta</s>. || 2 ||
These jewels are strung by me with verbal threads; therefore,
may the virtuous forgive [any faults], for there should be no reproach toward a servant. || 3 ||

children.text: vāṅmayaiḥ sūtrairmayā nibaddhyante | loke hi karṇādyavayaveṣu dhāraṇārthaṃ
children.translated_text: They are strung by me with verbal threads. For in the world, jewels are strung on threads for wearing on ears and other limbs. Therefore, no reproach should be directed at me who am engaged in serving the virtuous. || 3 ||

children.text: ratnāni sūtrairbaddhyante | tasmāt sadārādhanapravṛtte mayyasūyā na kartavyeti || 3 ||
children.translated_text: And the reason these [substances] beginning with <s>Bindu</s> are called by the word 'jewels' due to their similarity with jewels—he states:

body.translated_text: And the reason these [substances] beginning with <s>Bindu</s> are designated by the word 'jewel' due to similarity with jewels—he states—

children.translated_text: Because of their radiance among all <s>tattvas</s> (principles), from attachment to the two who have authority,
the Lords, the <s>Śivas</s>, and because they are to be held by the intellect, || 4 ||
and because of their unobstructed and noble array of rays for souls,
and because they accomplish what is desired—<s>Bindu</s> and the rest [are jewels] in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>. || 5 ||

children.text: ratnāni yathā loke rājante mahārghatayā prakāśante, samīpavartināṃ ca
children.translated_text: Just as jewels in the world shine (<s>rājante</s>) with great value and brilliance, generate

children.text: rāgamutpādayanti, puruṣaiścāvayavairdhāryante, dīptimantīṣṭavidhāyīni ca bhavanti; yathā
children.translated_text: attachment (<s>rāga</s>) in those nearby, are worn by people on their limbs, and are luminous and productive of desired results; so too

children.text: bindvādayaḥ padārthāḥ sarveṣu śaktyādiṣu tattveṣūpādānatayā'dhiṣṭhātṛtvena ca
children.translated_text: the entities beginning with <s>Bindu</s> shine among all <s>tattvas</s> such as <s>Śakti</s> etc. as material cause and as presiding [principle],
and for the Lords such as <s>Ananta</s> and the <s>Śivas</s> stationed at levels such as <s>Sadāśiva</s>, who are souls—from these
[jewels] which are the causes, there is always attachment (<s>rāga</s>) toward the two kinds of authority, namely the relation of grace-giver and grace-receiver,

children.text: puruṣāṇāṃ caite dhiyā dhyeyatayā dhāryante, apratihatavilakṣaṇatejaso
children.translated_text: and these are held by souls through the intellect as objects of meditation, and they possess unobstructed and extraordinary brilliance

children.text: bhuktimuktyākhyābhīṣṭapradāyinaśca bhavanti | tasmādete'pi śivaśāstre ratnāni, procyanta
children.translated_text: and bestow desired results called enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) and liberation (<s>mukti</s>). Therefore, in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>, these too are 'jewels'—the word 'are called' is
to be supplied. And by their possessing unobstructed extraordinary brilliance, their superiority is shown. || 4–5 ||
Dependent upon the Three Jewels, the aggregate of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) exists,
and the sixfold path (<s>adhvan</s>) for attaining them is taught by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameṣṭhin</s>). || 6 ||

children.text: tatra śuddhatattvasaṃhatirbindumupādānatvena, śivaṃ kartṛtayā, śaktiṃ ca
children.translated_text: There, the aggregate of pure <s>tattvas</s> exists depending upon <s>Bindu</s> as material cause, upon <s>Śiva</s> as agent, and upon <s>Śakti</s>

children.text: tatkaraṇatayā saṃśritya vartate, upādānādi vinā kāryotpattyasaṃbhavāt | aśuddhāyāṃ ca
children.translated_text: as His instrument, since the arising of an effect is impossible without a material cause, etc. And in the impure [realm],

children.text: śivaśakto eva paramparayā kartṛkaraṇe, binduśca nivṛttyādikalādvāreṇādhāra iti vakṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> alone are agent and instrument successively, and <s>Bindu</s> is the substratum through the <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>—this we shall explain [later].
Here, for those who seek enjoyment (<s>bubhukṣus</s>), who are recipients of the elemental initiation (<s>bhautikadīkṣā</s>), the practitioners (<s>sādhakas</s>),

children.text: pariṇato binduḥ prāpyaḥ, śivastu śaktyavinābhūto naiṣṭhikadīkṣābhājāṃ mumukṣūṇām |
children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s> transformed into the form of manifold world-enjoyments is what is to be attained; while <s>Śiva</s>, inseparable from <s>Śakti</s>, [is to be attained] by those who seek liberation (<s>mumukṣus</s>) who are recipients of the final initiation (<s>naiṣṭhikadīkṣā</s>).

children.text: tatprāptaye ca kalādiṣatprakāro'dhvā śivena śāstreṣu varṇyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: And for attaining that, the sixfold path (<s>adhvan</s>) consisting of <s>kalā</s> etc. is described by <s>Śiva</s> in the scriptures. || 6 ||

body.text: eṣāṃ cādhvatvamupariṣṭāt sādhayiṣyati, idānīmasya dīkṣādāvupayogaṃ darśayati-
body.translated_text: He will establish their nature as 'paths' (<s>adhvan</s>) later; now he shows their utility in initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and consecration (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>)—
This very triad is the seed of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and consecration (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>).

children.translated_text: Since without knowledge of this [triad], initiation and consecration cannot be performed, this alone is their root—that is the meaning. ||

body.translated_text: He clarifies this very point—

children.translated_text: Various <s>yogas</s>, rituals both regular (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), || 7 ||
[various] knowledges, supernatural powers (<s>siddhis</s>), and liberations—all arise from the understanding of that [triad].
This alone is the supreme limit of that which is called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), upon reflection. || 8 ||

children.text: yogāḥ sālambanādayaḥ | nityaṃ pūjādi | naimittikaṃ dīkṣādi | jñānāni
children.translated_text: <s>Yogas</s> [mean those] with support (<s>sālambana</s>) and so forth. 'Regular' (<s>nitya</s>) means worship (<s>pūjā</s>) etc. 'Occasional' (<s>naimittika</s>) means initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) etc. 'Knowledges' means

children.text: tadviṣayāṇi paśupāśapativiṣayāṇi ca | siddhayaḥ aṇimādyāḥ | mokṣaḥ śivasāmyaṃ
children.translated_text: those pertaining to that subject, concerning <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), <s>pāśa</s> (bond), and <s>pati</s> (lord). '<s>Siddhis</s>' means <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the rest. '<s>Mokṣa</s>' means equality with <s>Śiva</s>

children.text: sadāśivādipadaprāptiśca | yaduktaṃ śrīmanmataṅge- mokṣaḥ saptaprakāro'yam, (yo0 5|67) iti
children.translated_text: and the attainment of stations such as <s>Sadāśiva</s> etc. As stated in the blessed <s>Mataṅga</s>: 'This liberation is of seven kinds' (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 5.67).

children.text: | etatsarvaṃ tajjñānāt siddhyatīti | kiñca, etatprāptirevāṇoḥ parā kāṣṭhā, paramokṣa
children.translated_text: All this is accomplished through the knowledge of that [triad]. Moreover, the attainment of this alone is the supreme limit (<s>parā kāṣṭhā</s>) for the soul—the highest liberation,
that is the meaning. || 7–8 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: This is to be heard through the statements of the authoritative (<s>āpta</s>), to be reflected upon with reasoning,
and to be meditated upon through the path of <s>yoga</s>, by those whose selves have been awakened through the descent of <s>Śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>). || 9 ||

By those whose selves have been awakened by the descent of <s>Śakti</s>, which is inseparable from the maturation of <s>mala</s> (impurity)—that is, by those whose minds are turned upward. And by this,
he indicates that these [truths] are established by scripture (<s>āgama</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>). || 9 ||

body.translated_text: Now what is the authoritative statement here? Therefore he says—

children.translated_text: The authoritative statement here is the <s>Siddhānta</s>, for <s>Śiva</s> alone is the [truly] authoritative one (<s>āptimān</s>).
There is no one equal to those two [Śiva and Siddhānta] who is a bestower of the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>). || 10 ||
The word '<s>Siddhānta</s>,' like words such as '<s>paṅkaja</s>' (lotus), is established through conventional usage (<s>yogarūḍhi</s>) as referring to the

children.text: daśāṣṭādaśasu tantreṣu prasiddhaḥ | tatastānyevābādhitatvāt pramāṇānīti bhāvaḥ | kuta
children.translated_text: ten or eighteen <s>tantras</s> such as <s>Kāmika</s> etc. composed by <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore, those alone, being uncontradicted, are valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)—that is the import. Why

children.text: ityatrāha- śiva evāptimān yata iti | nanu kaṇādapatañjaliprabhṛtayo'pyāptā evetyata āha- na
children.translated_text: so? To this he says: 'For <s>Śiva</s> alone is the authoritative one.' But are not <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Patañjali</s> and others also authoritative? To this he says: 'No one equal to those two.'

children.text: tābhyāmiti | satyam, te'pi svaviṣaye vastunyāptā eva, kintvasarvajñatvāt teṣāṃ tatpraṇītāni
children.translated_text: True, they too are indeed authoritative regarding their own subject matter. However, since they are not omniscient, the scriptures composed by them

children.text: ca śāstrāṇi tadaviṣayeṣu bindvādiṣu vastuṣu na pramāṇībhavitumarhanti, śivastu
children.translated_text: cannot be valid means of knowledge regarding matters outside their scope, such as <s>Bindu</s> and other realities. But <s>Śiva</s>,
being possessed of unsurpassed knowledge of all things and capacity for all actions, is the supreme authority (<s>paramāpta</s>), and the scriptures composed by Him,
since they reveal the realities unreachable by all other scriptures, and since they lead to the knowledge of things not known through other means, and since they are uncontradicted,

children.text: pramāṇānyeva | yadāhuḥ- anadhigatārthagantṛ pramāṇam iti | tatastena śivena tadāgamena
children.translated_text: are indeed valid means of knowledge. As they say: 'That which leads to the knowledge of things not otherwise known is a valid means of knowledge.' Therefore, nothing equal to that <s>Śiva</s> and His <s>Āgama</s>

children.text: ca sadṛśaṃ na kiñcicchreyasaḥ sādhakamasti | nanu nityatvādevāgamānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ
children.translated_text: exists as an instrument for attaining the highest good. But the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> [say]: 'The validity of the <s>Āgamas</s> rests on their eternality alone,

children.text: nāptapraṇītatayeti mīmāṃsakāḥ, tadayuktam, racanāyāḥ kartāraṃ vinā
children.translated_text: not on their being composed by an authoritative person'—that is unjust, because no origination is observed
of a composition without an author, just as with pots and the like. This and more has been established at length by us in the <s>Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā</s>; therefore,
let it be ascertained from there. || 10 ||

children.text: yadyevaṃ vāmādayo'pi śaivatvena prasiddhāḥ śivakṛtā eva, tanna,
children.translated_text: If so, then the <s>Vāma</s> and other [tantras] too, being well-known as Śaiva, are made by <s>Śiva</s> Himself? No,
because they teach mutually contradictory meanings, they are not made by <s>Śiva</s>. As they say: (See the first footnote on page 135 of the

children.text: pṛṣṭhasthā prathamā ṭippaṇī draṣṭavyā |) sugato yadi sarvajñaḥ kapilo neti kā pramā |
children.translated_text: earlier <s>Tantra</s>.) 'If the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) is omniscient, then <s>Kapila</s> is not—what is the proof?

children.text: athobhāvapi sarvajñau matibhedaḥ kathaṃ tayoḥ || iti | prasiddhistu teṣāṃ
children.translated_text: Or if both are omniscient, how can there be a difference of views between them?' And their being well-known [as Śaiva] is because
they were composed by other souls presided over by <s>Śiva</s>—thus there is no contradiction. He states this very point—
The <s>Siddhānta</s> alone is the [true] <s>Siddhānta</s>; the others are [merely] the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

children.text: āptastu śiva evaikaḥ śivānye tvaśivā matāḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: The [truly] authoritative one is <s>Śiva</s> alone; others besides <s>Śiva</s> are considered non-<s>Śiva</s> (inauspicious). || 11 ||
And '<s>Śivatva</s>' (the nature of <s>Śiva</s>) here means omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) and omnipotence (<s>sarvakartṛtva</s>). || 11 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: The <s>Siddhānta</s> is followed by the virtuous who have been purified by the descent of <s>Śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>),
but is condemned by others who act arbitrarily, as if it were a scripture for beasts (<s>paśuśāstra</s>). || 12 ||

body.text:
etadeva śaktipātacihnatvenoktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendre- yeṣāṃ śarīriṇāṃ śaktiḥ 
patatyavinivṛttaye |
body.translated_text: This very thing is stated as the mark of <s>śaktipāta</s> in the blessed <s>Mṛgendra</s>: 'Those embodied beings upon whom <s>Śakti</s> descends for the sake of cessation [of bondage],

children.text: vinivṛttaye | teṣāṃ talliṅgamautsukyaṃ muktau dveṣo bhavasthitau || bhaktiśca
children.translated_text: the sign of that [descent] in them is eagerness for liberation, aversion to worldly existence,

children.text: śivabhakteṣu śraddhā tacchāsake vidhau | (vi0 5|4-5) iti | tataśca śaktipātānantarabhāvinyā
children.translated_text: devotion to the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, and faith in the rituals prescribed by His scripture' (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 5.4–5). And therefore, by initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) which follows immediately after <s>śaktipāta</s>,

children.text: dīkṣayā pavitritaiḥ śodhitaiḥ siddhāntaḥ sevyate | yaduktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe- tīvraśaktinipātena
children.translated_text: [they are] purified, i.e., cleansed, and the <s>Siddhānta</s> is followed [by them]. As stated in the blessed <s>Kiraṇa</s>: 'When one is initiated by a guru through intense descent of <s>Śakti</s>,

children.text: guruṇā dīkṣito yadā | sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvat (vi0 1|21) iti || 12 ||
children.translated_text: he becomes omniscient, like <s>Śiva</s> Himself' (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 1.21). || 12 ||

body.text: asya ca paśujananindayā na prāmāṇyavyāhatirastīti dṛṣṭāntenāha-
body.translated_text: And that there is no impairment of [the Siddhānta's] validity due to the censure of those who are [still] bound souls (<s>paśu</s>)—he illustrates with an example—

children.translated_text: Surely the fragrance of musk is not destroyed by [the criticism of] people.
It is not established by arguments, but is always smelled by the fortunate. || 13 ||
For its utility in initiation etc., knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> and other [realities] must be acquired by those who desire enjoyment and liberation. That knowledge

children.text: ca siddhāntābhyāsena, tadabhyāsaśca śaktipātāvinābhāvinyā dīkṣayā siddhyatītyuktam ||
children.translated_text: is accomplished through study of the <s>Siddhānta</s>, and that study is accomplished through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) which is inseparable from <s>śaktipāta</s>—thus it has been stated.
Here some say: 'By this false account of <s>Śiva</s> and other realities,

children.text: tatparijñānasādhanakathanena vā, sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma (chā0 u0 3|14|1), eko vaśī
children.translated_text: or by this account of the means of knowing them—[rather, according to Vedānta:] "All this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>" (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 3.14.1), "The one controller,

children.text: sarvabhūtāntarātmā (kaṭho0 5|12) ityādiśrutibhiḥ paramātmaiva cidākāraḥ satyabhūtaḥ | sa
children.translated_text: the inner Self of all beings" (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 5.12)—by such <s>Śrutis</s>, the Supreme Self alone, of the nature of consciousness, is real.

children.text: eva śivādiśabdavācyo nānyatkiñcidasti | tataḥ paramānandasvarūpasya tasya
children.translated_text: It alone is denoted by words like '<s>Śiva</s>' etc.; nothing else exists. Therefore, the true understanding
of that [Supreme Self] whose nature is supreme bliss is alone the cause of liberation.' To them he replies—
By the <s>Vedānta</s> texts and the <s>Kula</s> scriptures, and likewise by other [texts], what is taught is:
consciousness (<s>citi</s>) endowed with bliss, [as understood] by those who are deluded by [the concept of] bliss. || 14 ||
That which is taught by the <s>Vedānta</s> and other scriptures such as <s>Śākta</s> etc.—that the reality of the nature of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) alone
is ultimately real, and that understanding of that consciousness (<s>citi</s>) endowed with bliss, whose nature is supreme bliss,

children.text: mokṣaheturiti pratipādyate; tadānandavipralabdhānām ānandaṃ brahma (bṛ0 u0 3|9|34) iti
children.translated_text: is alone the cause of liberation—this appeals only to those who are deluded by bliss, who, regarding the Upaniṣadic statement '<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.34),
are deluded by the error of taking the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss), which [actually] means fullness/completeness,
to mean [mere] pleasure—[this appeals] only to those whose <s>mala</s> (impurity) is not yet matured, not to others such as us who have received the grace of <s>Śiva</s>—

children.text: bhāvaḥ | tathā hyātmaikatvaṃ tāvat sādhayitumaśakyam, anekatvapratipādakānāṃ
children.translated_text: that is the import. For indeed, the oneness of the Self is impossible to establish, since there exist
<s>Śrutis</s> that teach multiplicity; since the <s>Śrutis</s> of oneness have a different purport; and since the directly perceived
regularity of birth, death, etc. which indicates multiplicity cannot be denied. And since the lack of independence of those selves is observed,

children.text: baddhatve sati teṣāṃ bhogamokṣakartā śivaḥ, tadupādānādayaścāgamenānumānena siddhā
children.translated_text: when they are bound, <s>Śiva</s> is the agent of their enjoyment and liberation, and His material causes etc. are established by scripture (<s>Āgama</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>)—
this and more has been shown by us at length in the <s>Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā</s>, and has been established
by <s>Rāmakaṇṭha</s> and others in the <s>Mataṅgavṛtti</s> etc.; therefore let it be ascertained from there. It is not elaborated here for fear of expanding the text.

body.text:
ata evātmaviṣayaṃ vijñānamapi tattacchāstraprasaktānāṃ yathāvanna 
saṃbhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: For that very reason, even knowledge pertaining to the Self does not truly arise for those attached to those [other] scriptures—he says—

children.translated_text: The depth of the great ocean of consciousness could be fathomed by the wise,
if the wave of supreme bliss did not cast them up [to the surface]. || 15 ||

body.text:
yadi hi proktavatparamānandabhrāntikallolastānnotkṣipati, tato 
vidvadbhiścinmahodadherātmavargasamudrasya gāmbhīryaṃ sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvātmasvarūpaṃ 
nityatvavyāpakatvānekatvādi
body.translated_text: If indeed the surging wave of the delusion of supreme bliss, as described, does not cast them up, then by the learned, the depth of the great ocean of consciousness—i.e., the ocean of the collective of selves—[meaning] the essential nature consisting of omniscience and omnipotence,

children.translated_text: as well as eternality, pervasiveness, multiplicity, etc.—having fathomed [it], i.e., having made it the object of valid means of knowledge, could be ascertained; not otherwise. Since the authors of those [other] scriptures are not omniscient,
from their statements alone this [complete knowledge] is not possible—that is the meaning. || 15 ||

body.translated_text: Now, from what source is this [truth] known? Therefore he says—

children.translated_text: That is stated here, in the greatest of all streams, by the Lord;
By the upward-facing mouth of the north, one should ascertain that. || 16 ||
And that nature of the self (<s>ātmasvarūpa</s>) is taught in the most excellent stream called <s>Siddhānta</s>, from among all the streams of scripture beginning with <s>Vāma</s>,

children.text: srotasi kathitamiti tata evāvadhāryam | śivakṛtatvena jyāyastvamevāsya sādhayati-
children.translated_text: therefore it should be ascertained from that alone. He establishes its superiority by virtue of being created by <s>Śiva</s>—
'By the upward-facing mouth of the north of the Lord' — 'taught' — by the word 'mouth' (<s>vaktra</s>) is meant the power (<s>śakti</s>) whose nature is protective speech,
since in ultimate reality <s>Śiva</s> has no body. Therefore, by the northward-facing mouth, meaning that which is inclined toward grace and situated above,

children.text: ca śaktyātmanā vaktreṇa | binduśakternādādikrameṇotpādite śāstre prakāśitamityarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: by the mouth that is of the nature of <s>Śakti</s>. The meaning is: it was revealed in the scripture produced through the sequence beginning with <s>Nāda</s> from <s>Bindu-śakti</s>.
Objection: for one without a body, scriptural instruction is impossible? That is not so, because just as in the creation of the world and so forth, merely by will (<s>saṅkalpa</s>),
the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others are made to comprehend the scripture. || 16 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover—

children.translated_text: One should examine the reasons (<s>hetus</s>) too for the investigation of that, from the scripture;
For herein even vast and pure intellect does not dare to proceed. || 17 ||

children.text: tasyātmasvarūpasya parīkṣaṇamapi siddhāntoktaireva hetubhiḥ kāryamiti bhāvaḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the examination of that nature of the self (<s>ātmasvarūpa</s>) should also be done only through the reasons stated in <s>Siddhānta</s>. || 17 ||

body.text:
itthaṃ prasaṅgādātmasvarūpasya siddhāntaikagamyatvaṃ prasādhya prakṛtānāṃ 
śivādiratnānāṃ śravaṇamanananididhyāsanāni siddhāntādeveti prāguktaṃ prapañcayati-
body.translated_text: Having thus incidentally established that the nature of the self is knowable only through <s>Siddhānta</s>, he elaborates on what was said earlier — that the hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>manana</s>, <s>nididhyāsana</s>) on the jewels beginning with <s>Śiva</s>, which are the topic at hand, are from <s>Siddhānta</s> alone—

children.translated_text: Supramundane, subtle, and concealed by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: trīṇi ratnāni ko vetti siddhānteta vinā svayam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: who knows the three jewels (<s>ratnāni</s>) by oneself without <s>Siddhānta</s>? || 18 ||
And likewise the reasons (<s>hetus</s>) which are engulfed in the darkness of false reasoning, even with intellect,

children.text: tadvad yogaṃ ca ko vetti sabījābījalakṣaṇam || 19 ||
children.translated_text: who knows <s>Yoga</s> characterized as with-seed (<s>sabīja</s>) and without-seed (<s>abīja</s>)? || 19 ||

children.text: tatra sabījayogaḥ sadāśivādyākāraḥ sakalaviṣayaḥ, nirbījastu niṣkalaviṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: There, <s>sabīja-yoga</s> (with-seed yoga) has the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s> and others and pertains to the <s>sakala</s> domain, while <s>nirbīja</s> (without-seed) pertains to the <s>niṣkala</s> domain.
By this he also shows that these are knowable through scripture (<s>āgama</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and yogic perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>). || 18-19 ||

body.translated_text: Furthermore—

children.translated_text: <s>Siddhānta</s>, when served by the virtuous, grants whatever desires,
like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) obtained, fulfilling all that is in the mind of the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>). || 20 ||
The meaning is that from <s>Siddhānta</s> alone comes the knowledge of the respective means of accomplishment for practitioners (<s>sādhakas</s>),
and from its practice comes the attainment of results. || 20 ||

body.text:
itthaṃ siddhāntajñānaphalaṃ pradarśya tadabhidheyārtha-prakāśakatvādasyāpi 
prakaraṇasya tadeva prayojanamiti sūcayan abhidheyaparīkṣāṃ pratijānīte-
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the fruit of <s>Siddhānta</s> knowledge, indicating that since this section too illuminates the subject matter to be expressed, its purpose is the same, he undertakes the examination of the subject matter—

children.translated_text: Having resorted to that, by me too this examination, which rests on <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>, is undertaken;
therein <s>Bindu</s> is ascertained first. || 21 ||

body.translated_text: There he states the establishment of <s>Bindu</s>—

children.text: jāyate'dhvā yataḥ śuddho vartate yatra līyate |
children.translated_text: The pure path (<s>adhvan</s>) arises from which, exists in which, and dissolves in which,
that is <s>Bindu</s>, called <s>Paranāda</s>, the cause of <s>Nāda</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, and <s>Varṇa</s>. || 22 ||
Because the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>) is an effect, having the form of diverse worlds and so forth as will be described, <s>Bindu</s> is established as its material cause (<s>upādāna</s>).

children.text: binduḥ siddhyati | kiñca, śabdopādānatayāpi tasya siddhirityāha- nādavindvarṇakāraṇamiti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, its establishment is also as the material cause of sound — hence 'the cause of <s>Nāda</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, and <s>Varṇa</s>'.

children.text: tatra nādo nāmābhidheyabuddhiheturbindoḥ prathamaprasararūpaḥ sūkṣmo nādaścintayā
children.translated_text: There, <s>Nāda</s> is the first emanation of <s>Bindu</s>, a subtle sound that is the cause of the cognition of name and referent,
being devoid of deliberate thought, as stated in the glorious <s>Kālottara</s> and other texts. And <s>Bindu</s> is its effect, like a drop of essence in a peacock's egg, indesignatable,
the imperishable <s>Bindu</s> (<s>akṣara-bindu</s>) whose nature is reflective knowledge, described there as subtle. And <s>Varṇa</s> is the letter-sound,

children.text: ākāśavāyupra-bhavaḥ śrotragrāhyaḥ sthūlaśabdaḥ | taduktaṃ tatra- sthūlaṃ śabda iti
children.translated_text: arising from space and air, perceptible by the ear, the gross sound. As stated there: 'The gross is called sound,

children.text: proktaṃ sūkṣmaṃ cintāmayaṃ bhavet | cintayā rahitaṃ yattu tatparaṃ parikīrtitam || (1|8) ||
children.translated_text: the subtle is that which consists of thought; that which is devoid of thought is declared to be the supreme.' (1.8) ||

body.translated_text: There, to show that the pure path is the substratum of worlds and so forth, he says—

children.translated_text: Those who have crossed the ocean of <s>Māyā</s>, who have broken the great bolt of <s>karma</s>,
but have not attained the abode of <s>Śiva</s> — these are the <s>Vijñānakevalas</s> of three kinds. || 23 ||

children.text: trividhā hi paśvātmānaḥ- tatra malakarmamāyāyuktāḥ sakalāḥ,
children.translated_text: The bound souls (<s>paśu-ātmānas</s>) are indeed of three kinds: among them, those endowed with <s>mala</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>māyā</s> are <s>sakalas</s>;

those whose <s>kalā</s> and other [fetters] have been withdrawn at the time of dissolution, who are endowed with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>, are <s>pralayākalas</s>; and those for whom <s>karma</s> too has been exhausted beyond the <s>vijñāna</s> [stage],

children.text: kṣayānmalamātrayuktā vijñānakalāḥ | te punaḥ malaparipākatāratamyāt śivaprasādena
children.translated_text: who are endowed with <s>mala</s> alone, are <s>vijñānakalas</s>. They again, by the grace of <s>Śiva</s> according to the degree of ripening of <s>mala</s>,
have broken the great obstruction called <s>karma</s> and <s>mala</s>, but because of some residual <s>mala</s> in the form of functional authority (<s>adhikāra</s>), have not attained
equality with <s>Śiva</s> — they become <s>Vijñānakevalins</s> of three kinds indeed. || 23 ||

body.translated_text: What are those divisions? He says—

children.translated_text: The lords of <s>Vidyā</s> and <s>Avidyā</s>, preceded by the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>), are <s>Sadāśivas</s>;

children.text: tatra vidyābhujaḥ pūrve mantrā vidyāśca nāmataḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: among them, the first, who partake of <s>Vidyā</s>, are called <s>Mantras</s> and <s>Vidyās</s> by name. || 24 ||

children.text: tatra prathame vidyātattvanivāsina ityāha- tatra vidyābhuja iti || 24 ||
children.translated_text: That the first ones reside in the <s>Vidyā-tattva</s>, he states: 'among them, those who partake of <s>Vidyā</s>.' || 24 ||
They are appointed by the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, numbering seventy million;
their cities in <s>Vidyā</s> are <s>Vāma</s> and others, in succession. || 25 ||
Their appointment by the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> is because they perform the function of grace (<s>anugraha</s>), while the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>
have authority over the five types of divine activity (<s>pañcavidhakṛtya</s>). || 25 ||

body.translated_text: Nine [cities] have arisen, flourishing with bodies, enjoyments, senses, and so forth;

children.translated_text: the meaning is that these worlds possess progressively superior enjoyments and so forth.

body.translated_text: Now he says that the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> are superior to these—

children.translated_text: The middle ones, whose impurities are pacified, are the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, radiant with the splendor of <s>Śiva</s>. || 26 ||
Endowed with <s>mala</s> only in the form of functional authority (<s>adhikāra</s>), they have resorted to the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>,
their powers blossoming through contact with the rays of the sun that is <s>Śiva</s>. || 27 ||
The pacification of <s>mala</s>, the association with functional <s>mala</s> (<s>adhikāramala</s>), and being graced by <s>Śiva</s> are
common to the <s>Mantras</s> as well. 'Radiant with the splendor of <s>Śiva</s>' means they perform the five types of divine activity. As stated in the glorious <s>Raurava</s>:
'They perform creation, preservation, giving, destruction, and grace' (1.15). || 26-27 ||
They are eight, beginning with <s>Ananta</s>, each progressively superior in qualities;
likewise their cities are there, and <s>Ananta</s> among them is the supreme lord. || 28 ||

children.text: aṣṭāvanantapūrvā iti | ananta-sūkṣma- śivottama- ekanetra- ekarudra- trimūrti-
children.translated_text: 'Eight, beginning with <s>Ananta</s>' — they are named <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Śivottama</s>, <s>Ekanetra</s>, <s>Ekarudra</s>, <s>Trimūrti</s>,

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhaśikhaṇḍisaṃjñāḥ | tatreśvaratattve teṣāmaṣṭau bhuvanāni prāgvadeva | ata
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>. In the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>, their eight worlds are as described before. Therefore,
<s>Ananta</s> alone among them is the supreme lord. || 28 ||
There, the atomic souls (<s>āṇavas</s>) were in the cities, and no others; their powers are [limited];
the higher ones, equal to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, have authority over the lord's activities. || 29 ||

children.text: tattadbhuvaneśvarārādhanādinā dīkṣayā vā teṣu bhuvaneṣu yojitā ātmānaśca
children.translated_text: Souls who have been placed in those worlds through worship of the respective lords of the worlds, or through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>),

children.text: vidyante | ayaṃ ca nyāyo vidyābhuvaneṣu sadāśivādibhuvaneṣu ca vijñeyaḥ | yaduktaṃ
children.translated_text: are found there. And this principle should be understood for the worlds of <s>Vidyā</s> as well as for the worlds of <s>Sadāśiva</s> and others. As stated

children.text: sūkṣmasvāyambhuve- yo yatrābhilaṣed bhogān sa tatraiva niyojitaḥ |
children.translated_text: in the <s>Sūkṣma-svāyambhuva</s>: 'He who desires enjoyments in a particular [world] is appointed there itself,

children.text: siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyāt (39|2) iti | atha paśusadāśivānāha- pare sadāśivasamā iti || 29
children.translated_text: by the power of <s>Siddhi</s>, speech, and <s>Mantra</s>' (39.2). Now he speaks of the bound-soul <s>Sadāśivas</s>: 'The higher ones, equal to <s>Sadāśiva</s>.' || 29 ||

body.translated_text: Having reached the summit of the path, when the supreme Lord is gracious,

body.text:
sadāśivaścātrādhikārāvasthaḥ śiva eva | tasya ca adhikārādayo'vasthā 
aupacārikā ityuktam- adhikārī sa bhogī ca layī syādupacārataḥ  iti | 
saṃskāryasadāśivādīnāṃ tu bhedo vāstava eva |
body.translated_text: And <s>Sadāśiva</s> here is in the state of functional authority — he is <s>Śiva</s> himself. And his states of authority and so forth are figurative, as stated: 'He is called one with authority, one with enjoyment, and one in dissolution — figuratively.' But the distinction of the <s>Sadāśivas</s> who are to be consecrated is real indeed.
He says that these reside in the <s>Sadāśiva</s> world within the <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s>—

children.translated_text: Their <s>tattva</s> is adorned with unthreaded limbs, cities, enjoyments, and so forth. || 30 ||
<s>Sadāśiva</s> by the name of the presiding deity — they too are <s>Sadāśivas</s>.

children.text: ata evaiṣāṃ dehādayo'vāstavā eva, adhiṣṭhātustasya śivasya na pāramārthikā
children.translated_text: Therefore their bodies and so forth are indeed unreal; for the presiding deity, that <s>Śiva</s>, they are not ultimately real,

children.text: ityuktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare- sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam iti || 30 ||
children.translated_text: as stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s>: 'This form of his is considered to be for the purpose of visualization by the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>).' || 30 ||

body.translated_text: He summarizes the stated meaning—

children.translated_text: This path, together with its eighteen worlds and their enjoyers, || 31 ||
and three <s>tattvas</s>, has been declared as the pure [path], created by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: eṣa cādhvā kāryatvāt śivakartṛka ityarthaḥ | atra ca nivṛttyādibhuvanānāṃ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that this path is created by <s>Śiva</s> because it is an effect. And here it should be understood that the worlds of <s>Nivṛtti</s> and others
and the <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s> tattvas are included within the <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s> itself. || 31 ||

body.text:
kāryatvādevāsya śuddhādhvanaḥ kenāpi nityena kāraṇena bhavitavyam, tacca 
bindvākhyamityāha-
body.translated_text: Since this pure path is an effect, there must be some eternal cause for it, and that is called <s>Bindu</s> — he says—

children.translated_text: The aggregate of <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> has an eternal material cause (<s>nityopādānakāraṇa</s>). || 32 ||
Just as a pot is a modification, so too is this [path]; therefore, likewise.

children.text: eṣo'pi sadāśivādiradhvā vikārī, tato nityopādānakāraṇa iti || 32 ||
children.translated_text: This path beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> is also a modification (<s>vikārin</s>), therefore [it must have] an eternal material cause. || 32 ||

body.text:
nanu ghaṭopādānakāraṇasya mṛtpiṇḍasyānityatvādanenāpi 
śuddhādhvopādānenānityena bhavitavyamiti dharmisvarūpaviparīta-sādhakatvād viruddho'yaṃ 
vikāritvāditi hetuḥ ? ata āha-
body.translated_text: Objection: since the material cause of a pot, namely a lump of clay, is non-eternal, this material cause of the pure path too should be non-eternal — thus this reason 'because of being a modification' proves the opposite of the property to be established (<s>dharmi-svarūpa-viparīta-sādhaka</s>), making it a contradictory reason? To this he says—

children.translated_text: Even though a pot is made of earth, <s>Māyā</s> is [its] material cause. || 33 ||
Even though clay is the direct material cause of a pot, indirectly <s>Māyā</s> alone is the material cause. || 33 ||

body.translated_text: How so? He says—
By virtue of [its] possessing origination and destruction, and likewise by way of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>),

children.translated_text: This is the intention: for things that are characterized by origination and destruction,
even though there may be intermediate cause-effect relations through intermediate transformations such as pot-sherds and so forth, ultimately for the <s>tattvas</s> such as earth and the rest,
one must accept that which is called <s>Māyā</s>, the eternal supreme cause, as the indirect material cause,
otherwise there would be the fallacy of infinite regress. And it is stated in the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s>: 'The <s>Māyā-tattva</s>
is the seed of the world, imperishable and immutable.'

body.translated_text: He establishes this same point in detail—

children.translated_text: Whatever entity arises, that is of <s>Māyā</s>, just as <s>Kalā</s> [is]. || 34 ||
The Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) declared that origination and destruction are properties of <s>Māyā</s>;
the purport is that this is also established by authoritative testimony (<s>āptavākya</s>). || 34 ||

body.text:
idānīṃ satkāryavādadṛṣṭyā kalādyavasthābhedenotpatti-vināśavyapadeśaṃ bhajantī 
māyaiva kalādikāryadvāreṇa pariṇamata iti darśayituṃ pariṇāmaśabdārthamāha-
body.translated_text: Now, to show that <s>Māyā</s> itself, which receives the designation of origination and destruction through the differentiation of states such as <s>Kalā</s> and others from the perspective of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (the doctrine that the effect pre-exists in the cause), transforms through the medium of effects such as <s>Kalā</s> and others, he explains the meaning of the word <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation)—

children.translated_text: Transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of things is indeed the departure from a prior state || 35 ||
and the attainment of another state, like milk becoming curd,
and curd becoming buttermilk; there the state of buttermilk is examined. || 36 ||
To explain the nature of the example, he says: 'there.' || 35-36 ||

body.translated_text: For that [state]—

body.text: na dadhno nāpi dugdhasya pūrvāvasthe hi te mate |
body.translated_text: is neither of curd nor of milk, for those are considered prior states.

body.text:
dadhyavasthāyāṃ kṣīrāvasthāyāṃ vā takrāvasthā nāstītyarthaḥ | tathā hi 
kṣīrameva dadhyādirūpeṇa pariṇamate, kṣīraṃ naṣṭaṃ dadhyutpannamityādivyapadeśaśca 
dṛśyate |
	etadevāha-
body.translated_text: The meaning is that the state of buttermilk does not exist in the state of curd or in the state of milk. For indeed, milk itself transforms into the form of curd and so forth, yet the designation 'milk is destroyed, curd has arisen' and so on is observed. He states this very point—

children.text: sadavasthaṃ hi vastvekaṃ pūrvaṃ kṣīraṃ tato dadhi || 37 ||
children.translated_text: For a single substance always exists — first as milk, then as curd. || 37 ||

children.text: asata utpattyasaṃbhavāt sadeva dadhi kṣīrādabhivyajyate, sadeva takraṃ
children.translated_text: Since the origination of something from non-existence is impossible, curd is manifested from milk as something that already exists; likewise buttermilk

is manifested from curd as already existent — this is the purport. And this <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of the pre-existence of the effect) has been demonstrated by us in detail in the <s>Mṛgendra-vṛtti-dīpikā</s>. || 37 ||

body.text:
yathā caiṣāṃ dadhinavanītādyavasthāpariṇāmabhedena vicitrārthakriyāṇāṃ 
kāryāṇāṃ kṣīramevopādānam, evaṃ tattvabhuvanādibhedena vicitrapariṇāmavatāṃ 
vicitrārthakriyāṇāṃ ca kalādikāryāṇāṃ sākṣāt paramparayā ca māyaiva 
paramakāraṇamityāha-
body.translated_text: Just as milk alone is the material cause of effects such as the states of curd, butter and so forth, which have diverse transformations and diverse functional capacities, similarly <s>Māyā</s> alone is the supreme cause — directly and indirectly — of effects such as <s>Kalā</s> and others, which have diverse transformations in the form of <s>tattvas</s>, worlds and so forth, and diverse functional capacities. He says—

children.translated_text: Afterwards buttermilk; similarly <s>Māyā</s>, through its diverse transformations,
is the imperishable material cause of <s>tattvas</s> and their derivative states. || 38 ||

children.text: yadyevaṃ kṣīravat satvātmanā pariṇāmādanityatvaṃ māyāyāḥ, tanna, sarvathā
children.translated_text: If so, then like milk, <s>Māyā</s> would be non-eternal since it transforms with something existing [as its nature]. That is not so, because the example cannot apply in all respects;
its exemplary status pertains only to the aspect of being transformable. And therefore,
by the maxim of the worm in the ghee (<s>ghṛtakīṭanyāya</s>), <s>Māyā</s> transforms only in one part [of itself] — hence there is no fault. || 38 ||

body.translated_text: Having thus established that even for a pot, indirectly, there is an eternal material cause, he summarizes—
Therefore the illustration is apt, with the qualifier that has been stated as well-established.

body.text: prakarṣeṇa siddhamuktaṃ nityopādānatvarūpaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ yasya tat tathāvidhamiti |
body.translated_text: The meaning is: that [illustration] is of such a nature that the qualifier — namely the nature of being an eternal material cause — has been thoroughly established.
He also states the establishment of <s>Bindu</s> through residual inference (<s>pāriśeṣikānumāna</s>)—

children.text: na māyā neśvaro nāṇurna śaktiḥ śuddhavartmanaḥ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Māyā</s>, nor <s>Īśvara</s>, nor the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul), nor <s>Śakti</s> [is the material cause] of the pure path. || 39 ||
Therefore <s>Bindu</s> is obtained as the material cause by the method of elimination.

body.translated_text: Here he establishes that <s>Māyā</s> is not the material cause—

children.translated_text: For that <s>Māyā</s> which, agitated by the infinite power [of <s>Ananta</s>], || 40 ||
produced the entire class of <s>tattvas</s> from water up to earth,

children.text: teṣāṃ madhyād yā māyā, sā hyacetanatvādanantasāmarthya-kṣobhitaiva
children.translated_text: that <s>Māyā</s> among them, being insentient, produces its own effect only when agitated by the infinite power [of <s>Ananta</s>]. As stated in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>: 'In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is declared the agent;

children.text: svakāryamutpādayati | yaduktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe- śuddhe'dhvani śivaḥ kartā prokto'nanto'site
children.translated_text: in the impure [path], <s>Ananta</s> is the lord'
(Vidyāpāda 3.27). || 40 ||

body.translated_text: There itself he states the reasons—

children.translated_text: Because of being impure and insentient, because of being the path of <s>Māyā</s>, || 41 ||
because of the connection with suffering, because of the association with <s>māyīya</s>, <s>kārma</s>, and <s>āṇava</s> impurities,
because of being the object of experience for all bound souls, and because of the arising of transformations. || 42 ||

children.text: yato'syā aśuddhādhvano'śuddhatve sati jaḍatvam, yataśca māyāmārgatvaṃ
children.translated_text: Since this impure path, being impure, is insentient, and since it is the path of <s>Māyā</s>,
the cause of delusion, and since there is connection with suffering, and since through the <s>māyīya</s> [impurities]—
the impurities such as false self-identification with the non-self—and through the <s>kārma</s> [impurity] which is the cause of pleasure, pain, and delusion,

whose nature consists of states such as erroneous attachment, and through the <s>āṇava</s> [impurity] which is the beginningless veil of the <s>aṇu</s> called the state of a bound soul (<s>paśutva</s>),

children.text: saṃbandhaḥ, bandhatrayayogināmeva dehendriyādijanakatvāt | ata eva yataśca
children.translated_text: there is connection [with bondage], since only those possessed of the triple bondage generate bodies, senses, and so forth. Therefore, since
there is the quality of being the object of experience for all bound souls through the medium of worlds and so forth, and since there are manifold

children.text: anekavidhāḥ pariṇāmodayāḥ pariṇāmavṛddhayaḥ, tasmādanantena kṣobhitā māyā
children.translated_text: transformations—increases of transformation serving as means for the experience of various fruits of <s>karma</s>—therefore <s>Māyā</s>, agitated by <s>Ananta</s>,

children.text: tādṛśaṃ kāryaṃ janayati, śuddhasya śivasya aśuddhaviṣaye kartṛtvāyogāt | yadyevaṃ
children.translated_text: produces such an effect, since pure <s>Śiva</s> cannot be the agent in the impure domain. If so,

children.text: śivasyāsarvakartṛtvaprasaṅgaḥ ? tanna, sākṣātkartṛtvamatra niṣiddhaṃ na tu prayojakakartṛtvam,
children.translated_text: would there not be the unwanted consequence that <s>Śiva</s> is not the agent of all? No, for what is denied here is direct agency, not prompting agency (<s>prayojakakartṛtva</s>),
since even <s>Ananta</s> and others cannot have agency without <s>Śiva's</s> superintendence. || 41-42 ||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very point—

children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, pervaded by insentient [substance], and being subject to transformation,
in the production of <s>kalā</s> and the other [tattvas], || 43 ||
would surely lead the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul), endowed with body and the rest, to a state of dependence,
just as gold [leads] the goldsmith in the work of producing a crown. || 44 ||

children.text: yadyevaṃ śivasyāpi śuddhaviṣaye kartṛtvāt śarīrendriyayogādi-prasaṅgaḥ ? tanna, tasya
children.translated_text: If so, would there not be the unwanted consequence that even <s>Śiva</s>, being the agent in the pure domain, would be subject to connection with body and senses? No, because he
eternally possesses pure, unsurpassed knowledge and action regarding all objects, and because agency in the movement of one's own body is observed even for the bodiless self.
But for <s>Ananta</s>, due to his connection with the impurity of [limited] authority, dependence on body and the rest is required—thus there is no contradiction. || 43-44 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: This very [<s>Māyā</s>], being within the range of determinate cognition (<s>vikalpa-vijñāna</s>),
is agitated by <s>Ananta</s>, the lord, just as clay [is shaped] by a potter. || 45 ||

children.text: savikalpajñānaviṣaya eva śarīriṇāṃ kartṛtvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti bhāvaḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that agency for embodied beings is observed only in the domain of determinate cognition. || 45 ||

body.translated_text: What follows from this? To this he says—
Determinate cognition (<s>savikalpa-vijñāna</s>) [arises] from the penetration of word (<s>śabda</s>) into consciousness (<s>cit</s>).

children.text: savikalpakavijñānamayaṃ ghaṭa iti parāmarśarūpāt śabdollekhādevāt-mano dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Determinate cognition has the form of the apprehension 'this is a pot'—it is seen to arise from the impression of word (<s>śabdollekha</s>).

body.translated_text: What further [follows] from this? To this he says—

children.translated_text: That word (<s>śabda</s>) is fourfold, by the division into <s>Vaikharī</s> and the others. || 46 ||
It arises from the agitation of <s>Bindu</s> when <s>Ananta</s> perceives objects.
For the arising of <s>Ananta's</s> determinate cognition, word is necessarily required. And at that time,
since the impure path has not yet arisen, the manifestation of word through gross space is not possible;

children.text: śivakṣubhitabindujanya eva śabdo'bhyupagantavyaḥ | tasya ca vaikharyādyāścatasro vṛttīrvakṣyati
children.translated_text: therefore word must be accepted as born from <s>Bindu</s> agitated by <s>Śiva</s>. And its four modes beginning with <s>Vaikharī</s> will be explained.
Here, the establishment of <s>Bindu</s> as the material cause of word is also achieved. || 46 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover—

children.translated_text: The Lord <s>Ananta</s>, whose body is <s>Vidyā</s>, is regarded as the agitator || 47 ||
of <s>Māyā</s>; and that [body] is called by the learned the <s>Baindava</s> <s>tattva</s> (the principle pertaining to <s>Bindu</s>).

children.text: anantasya baindavaśarīrayogaḥ śrūyate, tadupādānatayā binduḥ siddhyatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The connection of <s>Ananta</s> with a <s>Baindava</s> body is heard [in scripture]; the purport is that <s>Bindu</s> is established as its material cause.

body.translated_text: Here is the conclusion—

children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Māyā</s> is not the material cause; likewise this <s>Maheśvara</s> [is not either]. || 48 ||
<s>Bindu</s> alone is the material cause in the pure path—this is the meaning. Why [posit] this unfamiliar thing called <s>Bindu</s>,

children.text: kalpitena, īśvara ātmā tacchaktirvā śuddhādhvanyupādānamastu, ata āha- tathaivāyamiti || 48
children.translated_text: an invented [concept]? Let <s>Īśvara</s>, the self, or his <s>Śakti</s> be the material cause of the pure path. To this he says: 'Likewise this'— || 48
Because of being conscious, because of not undergoing modification (<s>vṛtti</s>), and because of transformation—therefore,
the self (<s>Ātman</s>) and <s>Śakti</s> should be understood [as not being the material cause]. The elaboration of this will be stated here itself. || 49 ||
For insentience is observed in material causes such as clay and the like. But <s>Śiva</s>, the self, and <s>Śakti</s> are conscious.

children.text: tataste nopādānaṃ bhavitumarhanti | kiñca, upādānaṃ hi pariṇāmena vā kāryamutpādayati,
children.translated_text: Therefore they cannot be the material cause. Moreover, a material cause produces its effect either through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>),

children.text: yathā kṣīrasya dadhibhāvaḥ, vṛttirūpeṇa vā, yathā paṭasya gṛhādibhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: as milk [transforms] into curd, or through modification (<s>vṛtti</s>), as cloth [is modified] into a house-covering and so forth.

children.text: śivādīnāmeṣāṃ tu vṛttipariṇāmau na saṃbhavataḥ, avikāritvāt, vikāritve
children.translated_text: But for <s>Śiva</s> and the others, neither modification nor transformation is possible, because they are unchangeable; if they were changeable,
there would be the unwanted consequence of defects such as insentience and non-eternality. The elaboration of this will come here itself. And this has been stated
by us in the commentary on the <s>Tattvaprakāśa</s>. || 49 ||

body.translated_text: He states another proof of <s>Bindu</s>—
<s>Bindu</s> is also inferred from the observation of inequality among souls (<s>aṇu-vaiṣamya</s>).

children.translated_text: From where? To this he says: 'from the observation of inequality among souls.' From the observation of
inequality in knowledge and action among the <s>aṇus</s> (individual selves).

body.translated_text: He states the inequality—

children.translated_text: Some individuals are seen to possess little knowledge and action, || 50 ||
others superior to them, and yet others are omniscient and powerful.

body.text: etacca vaicitryaṃ teṣāṃ na svataḥ saṃbhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: And this diversity is not possible for them inherently—thus he says—

children.translated_text: The individual soul (<s>pudgala</s>) is considered to be conscious, eternal, and free from modification. || 51 ||
For the consciousness and eternality of the self are established through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), as it always has the capacity

children.text: svasaṃvedanasiddhatvād dehāntaraphalakarmabhoktṛtayā ca cetanatvaṃ nityatvaṃ ca
children.translated_text: to connect determinate cognitions of infinite pots, cloths, and so forth, and as the experiencer of <s>karma</s> whose fruit is [rebirth in] another body—

children.text: siddhamāgameṣu śrūyate | ityato'sya na vikāraḥ saṃbhavati || 51 ||
children.translated_text: this is heard in the <s>Āgamas</s>. Therefore no modification is possible for it. || 51 ||

body.translated_text: For otherwise—
If it were subject to modification, it would become insentient and non-eternal, like a pot or a wall.

body.text: ayaṃ ca nyāyaḥ śakterapi samānaḥ, dharmadharmiṇoravyatirekādityāha-
body.translated_text: And this reasoning applies equally to <s>Śakti</s>, since a property and its possessor are non-different—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Citi</s> (consciousness-power), which is <s>Śakti</s>—for both of these, which are free from modification— || 52 ||

children.text: idaṃ ca prāgeva darśitam | uktaṃ ca nādakārikāsu-
children.translated_text: This has already been shown. And it is stated in the <s>Nādakārikās</s>:

children.text: avikāryatrātmoktastacchaktiścāpyato na yogyau tau | bahudhā sthātuṃ yadvā caitanyavinākṛtau
children.translated_text: 'The self is declared here to be unmodifiable, and so is its <s>Śakti</s>; therefore these two are not fit to exist in manifold forms, or [if they did,] being devoid of consciousness,

children.text: vikāritvāt || (ślo0 19) iti | ata eva tayoraupādhikameva vaicitryamityāha- tayorapīti || 52 ||
children.translated_text: they would be subject to modification' (Śloka 19). Therefore, the diversity of these two is only due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>)—thus he says: 'for both of these.' || 52 ||

body.translated_text: The manifold state of existence is due to the influence of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>).
And therefore—

children.translated_text: That by which the consciousness-power (<s>cit</s>) of the soul, when conjoined, || 53 ||
engages in the perception of objects from <s>Māyā</s> onwards, and by whose diverse modes it becomes variegated—that is <s>Bindu</s>, having many modes.

Here, the consciousness-power (<s>cit-śakti</s>) of the selves, conjoined with that [<s>Bindu</s>] in the form of <s>Nāda</s>—the seed of conceptual cognition (<s>abhidheya-buddhi</s>) which has undergone transformation—
operates in the perception of determinate objects belonging to the domain of <s>Māyā</s>, and
being qualified by diverse mode-distinctions called <s>Nāda</s>, specific to each individual self, it manifests as variegated—that is <s>Bindu</s>. And this

children.text: vistareṇoktaṃ tatrabhavatā rāmakaṇṭhena nādakārikāsu | proktaṃ ca śrīmatkālottare-
children.translated_text: has been stated in detail by the revered <s>Rāmakaṇṭha</s> in the <s>Nādakārikās</s>. And it is declared in the venerable <s>Kālottara</s>:
'That supreme seed called <s>Nāda</s> is situated in all beings' (1.5). || 53 ||
But could not the diversity of knowledge and so forth among selves be [explained] by <s>karma</s> alone, specific to each individual, just as the diversity of experience [is explained by karma]?
To this he says—
<s>Karma</s> alone, without [<s>Bindu</s> as] a co-factor, does not produce diversity for the soul. || 54 ||
Even the diversity of experience is [produced] only by [<s>karma</s>] dependent [on co-factors].

children.text: karma hi kalāditattvabhuvanādisāpekṣameva bhogavaicitryaṃ karoti, anyathā
children.translated_text: For <s>karma</s> produces diversity of experience only in dependence on <s>tattvas</s> such as <s>Kalā</s> and worlds and so forth; otherwise,
even earth and the like would be purposeless. || 54 ||

children.text: evaṃ jñānavaicitryamapi nādasahakṛtameva karoti na kevalam | tadeva sāpekṣatvaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>karma</s> produces diversity of knowledge also only with the assistance of <s>Nāda</s>, not by itself alone. He shows this very dependence—
<s>Karma</s> brings about the experience [of its fruits]; sandal-paste and other [accessories] [bring about] its diversity. || 55 ||

children.text: tadeva yadi tatkuryāt kiṃ tairiti vilupyatām |
children.translated_text: If that [<s>karma</s>] alone could produce that [diversity], what would be the use of those [accessories]? Let them be dispensed with.

children.text: karma paraṃ phalajananameva karoti, tasya tu vaicitryaṃ sahakārivaicitryādeva bhavatīti
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> produces only the fruit as such; but its diversity comes from the diversity of co-operative causes—

children.text: bhāvaḥ | nanu karmataśca śarīrāṇi vividhāni (viṣayāḥ kārakāṇi ceti tatratyaḥ pāṭhaḥ |)
children.translated_text: this is the purport. But [one may object]: 'From <s>karma</s> arise the manifold bodies' (the reading there is: 'objects and instruments')

children.text: śarīriṇām (svā0 32|13) iti śrīmatsvāyambhuvaśruteḥ karmaiva sādhanavaicitryamapi karoti |
children.translated_text: 'of embodied beings' (<s>Svāyambhuva</s> 32.13)—thus from the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s> scripture, <s>karma</s> alone produces even the diversity of means.

children.text: satyam, sādhanavaicitryadvāreṇaiva karma phalavaicitryaṃ karoti na kevalamityavirodhaḥ || 55 ||
children.translated_text: True; but <s>karma</s> produces diversity of fruit only through the medium of diversity of means, not by itself alone—thus there is no contradiction. || 55 ||

body.translated_text: He reinforces this very point—

children.translated_text: The activity of all beings, which is the cause of renunciation and appropriation, || 56 ||

children.text: apekṣyavastusadbhāve hi heyānāṃ tyāgārtham upādeyānāṃ copādānārthaṃ
children.translated_text: is possible only when the objects to be depended upon exist—for the purpose of renouncing what is to be abandoned
and appropriating what is to be adopted, the activity of beings is possible, not otherwise. || 56 ||

body.translated_text: He states the proof of <s>Bindu</s> by yet another method—

children.translated_text: Moreover, [the sages] declare that which is supremely transcendent—that [supreme] space (<s>ambara</s>), imperishable (<s>anaśvara</s>),
for the <s>Śivas</s> of unequal sovereignty, in both experience and authority, || 57 ||
is the cause, like space for the luminaries, being the [ultimate] source of the elements and the rest.
Just as space (<s>ākāśa</s>), which is the [ultimate] source of the five elements and the rest, by providing room

children.text: sthūlaśabdābhivyañjakatvena ca sūryādīnāṃ jyotiṣāṃ bhogādhikārayoḥ kāraṇam, evaṃ
children.translated_text: and by manifesting gross sound, is the cause of the luminaries such as the sun in both their experience and authority, so too
<s>Bindu</s> is established as the cause in both experience and authority for the <s>Śivas</s> dwelling in the pure path—

children.text: vidyeśvarādīnāmava-kāśadānena śabdotpādanena ca bhogādhikārayoḥ kāraṇaṃ binduḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others who possess <s>Śivahood</s> characterized by omniscience and omnipotence—by providing room and by producing speech.
And the knowers of <s>Āgama</s> declare that [<s>Bindu</s>] to be supremely transcendent, imperishable, called the supreme void (<s>paramavyoman</s>), distinct from the other [ordinary] space,
since there is no dissolution of the other [space] in it. || 57 ||

body.translated_text: Now he concludes the previously stated usefulness of <s>Bindu</s> for determinate cognition—

children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s> alone, in determinate cognitions, || 58 ||
by the combinations of its own diverse modes, inscribing [the content of] conceptual determination (<s>vikalpa</s>), attains consciousness.
<s>Bindu</s> alone, being the material cause of speech, through the connection with its own mode-distinctions in the form of speech from the subtle up to <s>Vaikharī</s>,
by inscribing the conceptual determination such as 'this is a pot, it is red, it is round,' produces in determinate cognitions the consciousness-experience (<s>cit</s>)
of the self as determinate. For determinate cognition arises through the penetration of word, qualified by particulars such as genus (<s>jāti</s>).

children.text: savikalpajñānamutpadyate | yadāhuḥ- asti hyālocanaṃ jñānaṃ prathamaṃ nirvikalpakam |
children.translated_text: As they say: 'There is indeed a cognition called apprehension (<s>ālocana</s>), which is the first, indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>),

children.text: balamūkādivijñānasadṛśaṃ śuddhavastujam | tataḥ paraṃ punarvastu dharmairjātyādibhiryayā
children.translated_text: resembling the cognition of a child or a mute, born from the pure object. Then subsequently, that cognition by which the object is ascertained

children.text: | buddhyā'vasīyate sāpi pratyakṣatvena saṃmatā || (ślo0 vā0 pratyakṣa0 112, 120) iti || 58
children.translated_text: through properties such as genus is also accepted as perception' (<s>Ślokavārttika</s>, Pratyakṣa section, 112, 120). || 58
And this is not a mental impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) called a latent impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>), because it is of the nature of direct experience. || 59 ||
For mental impressions are inferred through their indicator, namely memory, and are not within the range of our direct perception.
This determinate experience should not be considered a mental impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the nature of the latent traces of previous experience,

children.text: tasyānumeyatvāt, asya ca pratyakṣānubhava-rūpatvāt | smṛtyanyathānupapattyā hi saṃskāraḥ
children.translated_text: because that [<s>saṃskāra</s>] is inferential, while this has the nature of direct perceptual experience. For a <s>saṃskāra</s> is postulated only because memory cannot be otherwise explained. || 59 ||

body.text:
nanvadhyavasāyasya buddhikāryatvād buddhipariṇāmabheda eva savikalpānubhavaḥ ? ata 
āha-
body.translated_text: But since determination is an effect of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), is not determinate experience merely a modification of <s>buddhi</s>? To this he says—

children.text: na buddheḥ pariṇāmo vā māyordhvamapi sambhavāt || 60 ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it a transformation of <s>Buddhi</s>, since [determinate cognition] occurs even above <s>Māyā</s>. || 60 ||
Even though <s>Buddhi</s> is the cause of determination, it has been stated that determinate cognition is produced only through the cooperation of speech, which is an effect of <s>Bindu</s>.

children.text: ityuktam | ata eva śuddhādhvano buddhyabhāve'pi vākśaktidvāreṇa vidyeśvarādīnāṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the pure path where <s>Buddhi</s> is absent, determinate experience for the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others is established through the power of speech (<s>vāk-śakti</s>). || 60 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: Thus <s>Vidyeśvara</s> <s>Ananta</s>, invading <s>Māyā</s> with [his] power,
then carries out creation, possessing determinate knowledge. || 61 ||
Being an <s>aṇu</s> (limited soul) yet having agency, like a servant commissioned by us.
Since <s>Ananta</s>, being of atomic nature, is impelled by the residual impurity of [his] authority, it is through the connection with <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) alone

children.text: māyākṣobhakatvam, na tu śivasya bindukṣobhavannirvikalpakamātreṇeti bhāvaḥ || 61 ||
children.translated_text: that he has the capacity to agitate <s>Māyā</s>, not merely through <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate knowledge) as is the case with <s>Śiva</s>'s agitation of <s>Bindu</s> — this is the intended meaning. ||61||
Thus, having stated that <s>Bindu</s> is established through <s>Ananta</s>'s agency by means of <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) through the medium of <s>śabda</s> (word),
with <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others being the instrumental cause thereof, he now states the view of others on this very matter —
Other teachers, skilled in the distinction between the doctrines of <s>vṛtti</s> (operation) and <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), ||62||
explain this matter, which has been described with [different] qualifications, in another way.
This matter — that <s>Ananta</s>'s agency is through the connection with <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) — described with qualifications, other
teachers establish in another way. ||62||
He is the agent of <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), not of <s>vṛtti</s> (operation); therefore, he is so [endowed]. ||63||
Since this <s>Ananta</s> is the agent of <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), therefore he possesses such <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) — this is the meaning. ||63||

body.translated_text: He establishes this very point —

children.translated_text: 'This has been agitated by me in this way; it should certainly bring about the desired [result]' —

children.text: iti jānāti yaḥ śaktaḥ sa kartā pariṇāminām || 64 ||
children.translated_text: one who knows thus and is capable, he is the agent of transformations. ||64||

body.translated_text: But for the agent of <s>vṛtti</s> (operation), that [determinate knowledge] is not required — he says —
In things subject to <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), this quality [exists]; in things subject to <s>vṛtti</s> (operation), it would be otherwise.
To elaborate on this, he states that <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) is preceded by <s>nirvikalpaka-jñāna</s> (indeterminate knowledge) —

children.translated_text: For indeed, everyone, first perceiving an object free from conceptual construction, ||65||
the world then knows it determinately; otherwise,
<s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) arises after <s>nirvikalpaka-jñāna</s> (indeterminate knowledge) — this has already been stated. Otherwise,
there would be an infinite regress of cognitions. If <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> is not accepted, since <s>nirvikalpaka</s> [knowledge], merely illuminating the object as such,
would be common to all objects, there would be an infinite regress of cognitions. The specific determination 'this is the cognition of a pot' and so forth would be unjustified —
this is the meaning. ||65||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: Even by <s>Ananta</s>, everything here, if it is known ||66||
preceded by cognition pervaded by <s>śabda</s> (word) — he acts thus;
from the self-awareness 'I know determinately.' ||67||
Since <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate) knowledge, being of the nature of awareness 'I know,'
arises pervaded by <s>śabda</s> (word) in the form of reflective thought, the inner dialogue,
therefore, having known <s>Māyā</s> and other realities preceded by <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> pervaded by <s>śabda</s>, <s>Ananta</s> performs agitation and the rest,
since action upon something unknown is never observed. ||66-67||

body.translated_text: But for <s>Śiva</s>, who is the agent of <s>vṛtti</s> (operation), that [knowledge] is required for the agitation of <s>Bindu</s> — he says —

children.text: vṛttireva matā bindoḥ paṭasyeva kuṭī tataḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s> (operation) alone is considered [to belong to] <s>Bindu</s>, like the folding of a cloth; therefore,
even in <s>nirvikalpaka-bodha</s> (indeterminate awareness), the Lord presides over <s>Bindu</s>. ||68||

body.translated_text: And for <s>Ananta</s>, the agent of <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation), the dependence on <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> indeed exists — he concludes —
Not so does <s>Vidyeśvara</s> [act upon] <s>Māyā</s>, for she is subject to <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).
Having thus presented the rival view, he refutes it —

children.translated_text: No distinction of agency is ascertained by [the distinction between] <s>vṛtti</s> (operation) and <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation). ||69||

children.text: kurvato'pi kuṭīṃ buddhiḥ savikalpā hi dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: Even one who makes a fold [in cloth] is seen to have <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate) cognition.

children.text: hīti yasmādarthe | etacca paramathābhyupagamanadūṣaṇamuktam, na tu siddhāntatayā,
children.translated_text: '<s>Hi</s>' [means] 'because.' And this is stated as a refutation by accepting the opponent's [position], not as the established doctrine,

because even <s>Bindu</s> is described as undergoing <s>pariṇāma</s> in the form of <s>tattva-bhuvanas</s> and the like, and because there is no absolute difference between <s>vṛtti</s> and <s>pariṇāma</s>. ||69||

body.translated_text: Now he states the synonymous names of <s>Bindu</s> —

children.translated_text: <s>Śabda-tattva</s> (word-principle), <s>Aghoṣā</s> (unvoiced), <s>Vāk</s> (speech), <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, the eternal, ||70||

children.text: vidyā śaktiḥ parā nādo mahāmāyeti deśikaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>Śakti</s> (power), <s>Parā</s> (supreme), <s>Nāda</s> (resonance), <s>Mahāmāyā</s> — thus by the teachers;
<s>Bindu</s> is thus designated, and also as <s>Vyoman</s> (space) and <s>Anāhata</s> (unstruck). ||71||

body.translated_text: Now he shows the functions of <s>Bindu</s> in the form of subtle and other levels of speech, in the order of dissolution —
Its four <s>vṛttis</s> (functions), by which the <s>aṇus</s> (souls) are pervaded in three ways;

children.translated_text: by which the <s>aṇus</s> (souls) are pervaded — they possess superior, middling, and inferior knowledge, and so forth, as previously stated. ||70-71||

body.translated_text: What are those? — to this he says —

children.translated_text: <s>Vaikharī</s>, that called <s>Madhyamā</s>, <s>Paśyantī</s>, and that named <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (subtle). ||72||

children.text: ata āsāṃ kāraṇatvena binduḥ siddha ityarthaḥ || 72 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Bindu</s> is established as the cause of these — this is the meaning. ||72||

body.translated_text: He describes the nature of <s>Vaikharī</s> —

body.text: tatra sā vaikharī śrotragrāhyā yā'rthasya vācikā |
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Vaikharī</s> is that which is grasped by the ear and is the verbal expression of meaning.
And that —

children.translated_text: with breath held at the [articulatory] positions, having assumed the form of phonemes, ||73||
this [speech], for speakers, is generally dependent on the activity of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).

body.translated_text: Thus they say —

children.translated_text: 'The sound that arises from space and air, issuing forth from the body, reaching the mouth,

children.text: sthānāntareṣu pravibhajyamāno varṇatvamāgacchati yaḥ sa śabdaḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: being differentiated at various [articulatory] positions, attains the state of phonemes — that is <s>śabda</s> (speech).'

body.translated_text: He describes <s>Madhyamā</s> —

children.translated_text: Having solely the intellect as its basis, following phonemes in sequence, ||74||
in the form of inner dialogue, it does not reach the ear.
Transcending the activity of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), it exists as that called <s>Madhyamā</s>. ||75||
And this, being of the nature of reflective knowledge, has been stated to be the cause of gross speech as well. ||74-75||
With phonemes undifferentiated, through the process of universal withdrawal,
self-luminous, <s>Paśyantī</s> is like the juice within a peacock's egg. ||76||
And this has been stated to be of the nature of <s>akṣara-bindu</s> (imperishable seed-point). ||76||

body.translated_text: Now he describes the subtle state, previously mentioned as a synonym of <s>Nāda</s>, as being the seed of the cognition of the signified —
The <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (subtle) speech is the inner light of one's own nature, imperishable.

children.text: anapāyinītvaṃ cāsyāḥ suṣuptyādyavasthāsvapi saṃbhavāt, na tu nityatvena | asyā
children.translated_text: Its imperishability is because it exists even in states such as deep sleep, but not in the sense of eternality. Because

children.text: api pratipuruṣaṃ bhedenānekatvādacetanatvācca kāryatvāt | tasyāśca kāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: it too is multiple by differing in each individual soul, and because it is insentient and therefore a product. And its cause
has been stated to be <s>Para-bindu</s> (supreme Bindu) itself.

body.translated_text: He further specifies that —

children.translated_text: When [the speech] whose nature has been seen [as distinct], authority ceases. ||77||

children.text: yasyāṃ puruṣasvarūpād vivekena dṛṣṭasvarūpāyāṃ puruṣasya bhogādhikāro
children.translated_text: When [the speech] whose nature has been seen as distinct from the nature of the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) through discrimination, the soul's authority over experience

children.text: nivartate | yadyevaṃ vivekajñānādeva mokṣasiddherdīkṣānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ ? tanna, malasya
children.translated_text: ceases. If so, then since liberation would be achieved by discriminative knowledge alone, there would be the undesirable consequence of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) being purposeless? No, because <s>mala</s> (impurity) is a substance,
just as the cataract of the eye [is removed] by the treatment of an eye-doctor, so too liberation is accomplished only through the Lord's intervention called <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation),
by the removal [of mala]. ||77||

body.text:
tataśca tadviṣayavivekavijñānābhāvādeva śabdabrahmavādinaḥ puruṣasamavāyinīṃ 
tāṃ manyanta ityāha-
body.translated_text: And therefore, due to the absence of discriminative knowledge regarding that [subtle speech], the proponents of <s>Śabda-brahman</s> (Word-Absolute) consider it to be inherent in the <s>puruṣa</s> — he says —
They call it '<s>Amṛtā</s>' (immortal) in the <s>puruṣa</s> of sixteen <s>kalās</s> (parts).
That this is indeed their error — he says —

children.translated_text: The <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) alone is the essence of speech — pure, supremely blissful, steadfast, eternally risen, the Lord. ||78||

children.text: nāstameti na codeti na śrānto na vikāravān |
children.translated_text: He neither sets nor rises, is neither weary nor subject to modification,
moving within all beings — the sun whose nature is <s>Śabda-brahman</s> (Word-Absolute). ||79||
Piercing whom with the sword of knowledge, [souls] go forth without hesitation.

children.text: yamenaṃ samyagjñānākhyena khaḍgena bhitvā vivicya yathāvad jñātvā
children.translated_text: Having pierced — that is, having discriminated and known properly — this [entity] called <s>Śabda-brahman</s> with the sword called right knowledge,

children.text: saṃsārānnirgacchantyātmānaḥ, so'yaṃ śabdabrahmākhyo ravirasmād ravervilakṣaṇa iti
children.translated_text: the souls go forth from <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). This sun called <s>Śabda-brahman</s> is different from [the physical] sun —
this is their error. ||78-79||

body.translated_text: Here he states the established doctrine —

children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) call that very speech by the name <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (subtle). ||80||
The word 'eva' is placed differently [than in the opponent's usage]. Those who know the true nature of the <s>Ātman</s> — the <s>Śaivas</s> — regard that [entity] called <s>Sūkṣmā</s>

children.text: bindukāryabhūtāṃ śabdavṛttimeva manyante, na tu puruṣasamavāyinīm, tasyāvikāritvena
children.translated_text: as merely a function of speech that is a product of <s>Bindu</s>, not as inherent in the <s>puruṣa</s>, since the [puruṣa] is non-modifiable,

being insentient [if it were], and because if it were inherent in the <s>puruṣa</s>, there would be the undesirable consequence of the <s>puruṣa</s> also being modifiable, insentient, and so forth. ||80||

body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the functions of speech as products of <s>Bindu</s>, he concludes —
These functions, confined to each individual soul, are of the nature of bondage.

children.text: āsāṃ ca kāryatvena jaḍatvānna citsamavāyo yujyate, api tu bandhanatvamevetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since these, being products, are insentient, union with consciousness is not possible; rather, they are only bondage — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Nevertheless —

children.translated_text: Individuals do not see the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as distinct from these. ||81||

'Individuals' means those whose selves are accompanied by <s>mala</s> (impurity). Due to the concealment by <s>mala</s>, because of the absence of discriminative knowledge regarding that [distinction], there is the delusion of selfhood in these [speech functions] — this is the import. ||81||

body.translated_text: Why do they have this error? — to this he says —
'The Supreme Self is the essence of speech' and 'Speech alone is the Self' — from [such] scriptural [statements].

body.text:
ātmano vākśaktyādisaṃbandhasyārthavādabhūtānāmāsāṃ 
śrutīnāmarthāparijñānādevaṃ te manyante pudgalāḥ, malayuktātmāna ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Due to not fully understanding the meaning of these scriptures — which are <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages) concerning the connection of the Self with the power of speech and the like — those individuals, whose selves are accompanied by <s>mala</s>, think thus — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: <s>Vaikharī</s> is perceived in auditory cognition; <s>Madhyamā</s> in determinate [cognition]; ||82||
<s>Paśyantī</s> is perceived in the impulses that give rise to <s>Madhyamā</s>.

children.text: vaikharī śrotragrāhyaiva | madhyamā parāmarśajñānarūpatvāt savikalpe lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikharī</s> is grasped by the ear alone. <s>Madhyamā</s> is perceived in the determinate [cognition] because it is of the nature of reflective knowledge.
The cause for the arising of that [Madhyamā] is <s>Paśyantī</s>. ||82||

body.translated_text: But the other [level] —

children.translated_text: When the function [of speech] has completely dissolved, resting in consciousness, ||83||

body.translated_text: then the <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (subtle [speech]), being pure, appears as [if it were] consciousness itself, due to non-discrimination.

children.text: sūkṣmā tvabhidheyabījatvena sarvabhūteṣvavasthitā paśyantyā api kāraṇabhūtā cidā
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, being the seed of the signified, established in all beings, and being the cause of <s>Paśyantī</s> as well, due to extreme proximity to consciousness (<s>cit</s>),
