appears as if of the nature of consciousness — thus it has been stated. ||83||

body.translated_text: And by the reasoning stated —

children.translated_text: There is no cognition of the <s>aṇus</s> (souls) that arises without the accompaniment of <s>śabda</s> (word). ||84||
All knowledge here arises pervaded by <s>śabda</s>.

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: This very fourfold <s>vṛtti</s> (function), due to resting upon <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>, ||85||
is further divided into five; those <s>kalās</s> are the functions of <s>Bindu</s>.

This very <s>vṛtti</s> of <s>Bindu</s>, whose nature is <s>śabda</s> (word), assists knowledge and the like in five ways, proportionately, for the souls who rest upon the <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s> — this is the meaning. But whence have the <s>Nivṛtti</s> and other [kalās] arisen? — to this he says —

children.text: pañcadhā jñānādyupakāriketyarthaḥ | nivṛttyā-dayaḥ punaḥ kuta utpannā ityatrāha-
children.translated_text: 'Those <s>kalās</s>' — they are functions in the form of <s>kalās</s>, which are states of <s>Bindu</s> itself.

children.text: kalāstā iti | bindorevāvasthā-bhūtāḥ kalākāravṛttayaḥ | tataḥ kalopādānatvenāpi
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Bindu</s> is established even as the material cause of the <s>kalās</s> — this is the import. ||85||

body.translated_text: He shows those very [kalās] by name —

children.text: nivṛttiśca pratiṣṭhā ca vidyā śāntiśca pañcamī || 86 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nivṛtti</s>, <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, and the fifth, ||86||
<s>Śāntyatītā</s> — these are the <s>kalās</s>, by which the fivefold <s>adhvan</s> (path) is pervaded.

children.text: etāśca sadāśivabhuvanordhvaṃ bhuvanatvena sthitā api śaktirūpeṇa
children.translated_text: And these, though situated as <s>bhuvanas</s> (worlds) above the world of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, are established as pervading
all the <s>adhvans</s> (paths) in the form of <s>śakti</s> (power) — he says: 'by which the fivefold <s>adhvan</s> is pervaded.' ||86||

children.text: tattvādhvā bhuvanādhvā ca varṇādhvā ca padātmakaḥ || 87 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tattva-adhvan</s> (path of principles), the <s>bhuvana-adhvan</s> (path of worlds), the <s>varṇa-adhvan</s> (path of phonemes), and that consisting of <s>padas</s> (words), ||87||
the <s>mantra-adhvan</s> (path of mantras) — the all-pervading among these is the <s>kalā-adhvan</s> (path of kalās), which depends on <s>Bindu</s>.
The <s>kalā-adhvan</s>, in the form described, pervading the five <s>adhvans</s> beginning with <s>tattva</s>, depends on <s>Bindu</s> as its material cause — this is the meaning.
Among these, the <s>tattva-adhvan</s> is in the form of the pure and impure <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth). The <s>bhuvana-adhvan</s>
consists of worlds from <s>Anāśrita</s> down to <s>Kālāgni</s>. The <s>varṇa-adhvan</s> is the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) itself. The <s>pada-adhvan</s>
is designated as <s>Vyomavyāpin</s> (space-pervading). The <s>mantra-adhvan</s> is the collected <s>mantras</s> themselves. ||87||

body.translated_text: But how do these come to be called <s>adhvans</s> (paths)? To this he says —

children.translated_text: Leaving one after another and reaching [the next], in the <s>kalās</s> and the rest, the imperishable and ageless ||88||
state is attained by souls; therefore the <s>kalās</s> and the rest are [called] <s>adhvans</s> (paths).

body.text:
yathā hi loke'dhvasu kramādekapadāvaṣṭabdhaṃ bhūpradeśaṃ 
muktvā'nyapadāvaṣṭabdhaṃ bhūpradeśamāsādya grāmādi prāpyate, tathā kalāsu tattveṣu 
varṇeṣu padeṣu mantreṣu vā'śuddhaviṣayeṣu
body.translated_text: Just as in the world, on paths, by leaving one area of ground where one foot is placed and reaching another area where the other foot is placed, a village and the like is reached, so too in the <s>kalās</s>, <s>tattvas</s>, <s>varṇas</s>, <s>padas</s>, and <s>mantras</s> — in their impure domains

children.translated_text: for the purpose of experiencing <s>karma</s>, and in their pure domains for the attainment of omniscience and the like, during <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation),

children.text: viśiṣṭasaṃbandhātmakaṃ yojanaṃ kriyate | tataḥ kalādivastupaddhatayo'dhvāna ityucyante || 88
children.translated_text: a conjunction in the form of a specific relationship is effected. Therefore, the systems of realities — <s>kalās</s> and the rest — are called <s>adhvans</s> (paths). ||88||

body.translated_text: And among those —

children.translated_text: The <s>kalā-adhvan</s> has been described previously with the divisions of <s>Nivṛtti</s> and the rest. ||89||
I shall describe its pervasion — together with its supports, emblems, and presiding deities,
resting upon <s>Ātman</s> (self), <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śakti</s> (power), and <s>Śiva</s>. ||90||

children.text: ādhārā hṛdayādayaḥ, aṅkāni cihnāni vajrādīni, adhidevatā adhiṣṭhātṛdevatāḥ
children.translated_text: The supports are the heart and the like; the emblems are the signs such as the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) and the like; the presiding deities are the governing deities
such as <s>Sadyojāta</s> and the rest; the form is quadrangular and the like; the causes are the lords such as <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest.
'Resting upon <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>' — here, the selves serve as the substrate for the experience of the souls. Moreover,

children.text: bindurupādānatayā, śaktiḥ karaṇatayā ādhārakatvena ca, śivaḥ kartṛtayā āśrayo yasyāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s> as the material cause, <s>Śakti</s> as the instrumental cause and support, and <s>Śiva</s> as the agent — [these constitute] the basis of
the pervasion of the <s>kalās</s>. ||89-90||

body.translated_text: Now, he describes the pervasion of <s>nivṛtti</s> [kalā] in the order of dissolution —

children.translated_text: In <s>nivṛtti</s> [kalā], the earth principle (<s>pārthiva tattva</s>) [has] one hundred and eight cities (<s>purāṇi</s>);
among them, six are outside the infinite cosmic egg (<s>anantāṇḍa</s>), [belonging to] <s>Kālānala</s> and others. ||91||
In the ten quarters beginning with the east, in each of the near regions, ten [cities each];
above the hundred <s>Rudras</s> and <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, ||92||
and of <s>Bhadrakālī</s> — in [these] worlds, the letter <s>kṣa</s> is proclaimed among the phonemes.
Here, the names of the <s>Rudras</s> are themselves the names of the worlds. The worlds and so forth
have been discriminately shown by us in the <s>paddhati</s> (manual). Due to fear of the text becoming too lengthy, and because they are
well known in many other <s>paddhati</s> texts, they are not written here. ||91-92||
The <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), having eighty-one <s>padas</s> (phonemic units), in the order of re-creation — ||93||
is established here with twenty-eight <s>padas</s>.

children.text: ekāśītipadā devī vyomavyāpilakṣaṇā śaktiḥ | sā ca pratisarga-padakramāt
children.translated_text: The <s>Devī</s>, having eighty-one <s>padas</s>, is the <s>Śakti</s> characterized as pervading space. She, in the order of re-creation
(i.e., the order of dissolution), beginning from the final <s>praṇava</s>, is established here in <s>nivṛtti kalā</s> with twenty-eight <s>padas</s>. ||93

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: mantrāvajātahṛdayau tatra sā tu parā kalā || 94 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> and <s>hṛdaya</s> born of <s>aja</s> (the unborn) — she is indeed the supreme <s>kalā</s>. ||94||
Pervading the worlds and other [paths], the five [kalās] abide in the five [paths].
The meaning is: pervading the five <s>adhvans</s> (paths), [the kalās] abide in them. ||94||

body.translated_text: Having thus described the pervasion of <s>nivṛtti</s>, he states its form and other characteristics —

children.translated_text: She is yellow, square in shape, hard, and marked with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt). ||95||

body.translated_text: She should be meditated upon as rising with manifold rays, full-bodied, in the lotus of the heart.
He states the reason for its name '<s>nivṛtti</s>' —

children.translated_text: The volition of the aggregate of atoms dissolved in that ceases. ||96||
Because it does not attain its fruit, therefore it is called <s>nivṛtti</s> (cessation).

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> is the cause here; the <s>mantra</s> is <s>Sadyojāta</s>; the presiding deity [is the same]. ||97||

body.translated_text: He also describes <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> [kalā] —

children.translated_text: In <s>pratiṣṭhā kalā</s>, excluding earth, there are four [elements];

children.text: bhūtāni pañca tanmātrāḥ pañca karmendriyāṇi ca || 98 ||
children.translated_text: the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>), five organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>), ||98||
five organs of knowledge (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect);
also <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), and the phonemes from <s>ha</s> to the end of <s>ṭa</s>-series, in reverse order; ||99||
twenty-three are declared, and fifty-six cities (<s>purāṇi</s>).
In water, fire, wind, space, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>avyakta</s>, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — ||100||
eight and eight <s>padas</s>, twenty-one in number there.

children.text: śiro vāmaśca mantrau dvau viṣṇuḥ kāraṇamucyate || 101 ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>mantras</s> are <s>Śiras</s> and <s>Vāma</s>; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is said to be the cause. ||101||
She is white, resembling the half-moon, adorned with [the hue of] blue lotus petals;
she should be meditated upon within the lotus of the throat, resplendent with abundant light. ||102||
The volition of the aggregate of atoms dissolved in that, for the accomplishment of its purpose,

children.text: pratiṣṭhito yatastena pratiṣṭhā nāma sā kalā || 103 ||
children.translated_text: is established; therefore that <s>kalā</s> is named <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment). ||103||
<s>Vāmadeva</s> indeed is the presiding [deity]; the speech-<s>mantra</s> form is accepted.
<s>Manana</s> (reflection) is omniscience; <s>trāṇa</s> (protection) is the grace toward beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Because of having the nature of <s>manana</s> and <s>trāṇa</s>,

children.text: ityabhidhīyate || iti nyāyāt śivaśaktitadanugṛhīteṣu mantraśabdo vartate, upacārāttu
children.translated_text: it is called <s>mantra</s> — by this reasoning, the word <s>mantra</s> applies to those favored by <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>Śakti</s>; but by figurative usage,
it is well known for the word that expresses [them]. Therefore here too, the divisions of <s>Śakti</s> — <s>Sadyojāta</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and others —

children.text: adhidevatātvenocyante | ata eva tāsu nivṛttyādiṣu bhuvanarūpāsu sadyojātādivigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: are spoken of as presiding deities. Hence, in those [kalās] — <s>nivṛtti</s> and others — which have the form of worlds, <s>Śiva</s> with the form of <s>Sadyojāta</s> and others
should be meditated upon by those desiring attainment of that state — so say the teachers. ||98-103||

body.translated_text: He describes <s>vidyā</s> [kalā] —

children.translated_text: In <s>vidyā</s> [kalā there are] seven [tattvas]: <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>rāga</s>, together with <s>niyati</s>, ||104||

children.text: vidyā kalā ca kālaśca māyātattvāni tatra tu |
children.translated_text: <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, and <s>kāla</s> — these are the <s>tattvas</s> (<s>māyā-tattvas</s>) there;
and the worlds beginning with <s>māyā</s> are to be known as twenty-seven. ||105||
Here the phonemes beginning with <s>ña</s> and ending with <s>gha</s>, seven in number, in reverse order;
the <s>padas</s> are twenty; the two <s>mantras</s> established are <s>Śikhā</s> and <s>Aghora</s>. ||106||
<s>Rudra</s> is the cause here; the <s>mantra</s> is <s>Bahurūpa</s> as the presiding deity.
She is blazing with manifold rays, triangular, marked with the <s>svastika</s>; ||107||
she should be meditated upon within the lotus of the palate, with a luster like dark collyrium.
The volition of the aggregate of atoms dissolved in that has all things as its domain; ||108||
because it illuminates all meanings, therefore it is called <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).

children.text: aśeṣagocaraḥ svabhuvanādhovartisamastādhvaviṣayaḥ, na tu sarvaviṣayaḥ, tasya
children.translated_text: 'All things as its domain' means: pertaining to the entire path below its own world, not to everything [universally], because
that [universal scope] is possible only in the absence of <s>mala</s> (impurity). ||104-108||

children.text: śāntau tu trīṇi tattvāni daśāṣṭau bhuvanāni ca || 109 ||
children.translated_text: In <s>śānti</s> [kalā] there are three <s>tattvas</s>, and eighteen worlds. ||109||
The phonemes stated here are three, from <s>ga</s> to <s>ka</s>;
the <s>padas</s> here are eleven; the two <s>mantras</s> are <s>Vaktra</s> and <s>Tanucchada</s>. ||110||
Pervading the worlds and other [paths], the five [kalās], marked with six <s>bindus</s>;
with the splendor of a thousand rays arising from a hexagon, ending subtly; ||111||
that supreme <s>Śakti</s> should be meditated upon in the interior of the lotus between the brows.
Due to the absence of hatred, attachment, and other [afflictions] in the aggregate of atoms dissolved in that — ||112||
because the volition becomes pacified, this is called <s>śānti</s> (peace).
<s>Īśvara</s> is the cause there; the <s>mantra</s> is named <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>. ||113||
He who presides over that should be known; <s>Puruṣa</s> is the presiding deity.

children.text: atra ca trīṇi tattvāni pañcamī tu parā kalā || 114 ||
children.translated_text: Here there are three <s>tattvas</s>; but the fifth is the supreme <s>kalā</s> — ||114||

children.text: śivatattvātmakaṃ tatra purāṇi daśa pañca ca |
children.translated_text: there, having the nature of <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, there are fifteen cities (<s>purāṇi</s>);
the phonemes preceded by <s>visarga</s>, sixteen in number, known as vowels (<s>svara</s>); ||115||
<s>Om</s> is the first <s>pada</s>; the <s>mantras</s> are designated <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Astra</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s>.
<s>Śāntyatītā</s> (that which transcends peace) is the supreme <s>kalā</s>, containing the five paths (<s>adhvans</s>) within herself. ||116||
She should be contemplated as having the nature of the great space (<s>mahākāśa</s>), in the lotus at the crown of the head.
<s>Īśāna</s>, the king of <s>mantras</s>, presides over this [kalā]; the cause ||117||
is the deity <s>Sadāśiva</s> there — this is proclaimed as the path of <s>kalās</s> (<s>kalādhvan</s>).
[It is] the pervader of the worlds and other [paths]; it is pervaded by <s>bindu</s>. ||118||

children.text: binduḥ śaktyā śivenaiṣā nānyena vyāpyate śivaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s> [is pervaded] by <s>Śakti</s>; this [<s>Śakti</s> is pervaded] by <s>Śiva</s>; <s>Śiva</s> is not pervaded by anything else.
'Three' means: those called <s>Vidyeśvara</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>. Therefore, considering the absorption of <s>Śakti-tattva</s>

children.text: śivatattve'ntarbhāvaṃ manyamānaḥ śāntyatītāvyāptimāha- pañcamī tviti | vyāpaka iti |
children.translated_text: into <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, he describes the pervasion of <s>śāntyatītā</s> — 'but the fifth' and so on. 'The pervader' —

children.text: uktaditarādhvanāṃ vyāpakaḥ kalādhvā bindūpādānaka ityuktaḥ | kartṛbhūtaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>kalādhvan</s> is said to be the pervader of the other previously mentioned paths, having <s>bindu</s> as its material [cause]. <s>Śiva</s>, who is the agent,

children.text: karaṇabhūtayā samavāyinyā śaktyā bindumadhitiṣṭhati, śivasya tu nādhiṣṭhātā'stītyarthaḥ
children.translated_text: presides over <s>bindu</s> through his inherent <s>Śakti</s> of the nature of action; but there is no one who presides over <s>Śiva</s> — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: He states this very [point] —

children.translated_text: For that Lord, having enveloped [all] by his own <s>Śakti</s>, which is non-different [from him], ||119||

children.text: sarvamākramya ca tayā vijānāti karoti ca |
children.translated_text: and pervading everything through her, he knows and acts.
From this, the nature of <s>Śakti</s> as all knowledge and all action is established. ||119||

body.translated_text: Now he examines the nature of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) —

children.translated_text: The existence of one thing in another, at all times without exception — ||120||
that is <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), [and it is] the basis of the arising and persistence of the obtained entity.

children.text: anyasya ākāśādeḥ, anyatra kuḍyādāvastitvaṃ sarvakālamavyabhicāriṇī vyāptiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Of one thing' — of space and so forth; 'in another' — the existence in a wall and so forth, at all times, without exception — that is <s>vyāpti</s>.

children.text: sā ca āptasya padārthasya ātmalābhanibandhamutpattinibandhanaṃ sthitinibandhanaṃ ca bhavati
children.translated_text: And that is the basis of the arising (<s>ātmalābha</s>) and the basis of the persistence of the obtained entity.

body.translated_text: Therefore —

children.translated_text: <s>Vyāpti</s> is twofold: one [operates] through mere proximity, [the other] through the agency of the Supreme Self. ||121||

body.translated_text: He demonstrates that very [point] —

children.translated_text: There, by mere proximity, <s>Citi</s> (Consciousness) brings about everything;
just as the sun is beneficial to the activities of the day through its proximity. ||122||

children.text: citiścaitanyātmikā śivasya samavāyinī śaktiḥ, saṃkalpamātreṇa sṛṣṭyādikṛtyaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Citi</s>, having the nature of consciousness, is <s>Śiva</s>'s inherent <s>Śakti</s>; by mere will, she accomplishes the function of creation and so forth,

children.text: vidadhāti, sūrya iva kamalavikāsādi | tathā hyātmano'pi svadehaspandanādau
children.translated_text: like the sun [accomplishes] the blooming of lotuses and so on. Likewise, for the self too, in the movement of one's own body and so on,
agency through mere will is observed. ||122||

body.translated_text: And thus, the pervasion in the form of the inert [being governed] within the self through the superintendence of <s>Cit</s> (Consciousness) — he states:

children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s>, within the Self, [produces] <s>nāda</s> and the other six paths (<s>adhvans</s>) in sequence,
through their various transformations, impelled by <s>Śiva</s>. ||123||
Just as clay [produces] pots and so forth when superintended by the potter.
'The six paths also' means: <s>Bindu</s> produces all [six paths] having the nature of <s>kalā</s>, <s>varṇa</s>, <s>pada</s>, <s>mantra</s>, <s>tattva</s>, and <s>bhuvana</s>.
The <s>tattva</s> and <s>bhuvana</s> paths are in their pure form only; but the impure <s>tattva</s> and <s>bhuvana</s> paths are produced from <s>Māyā</s>.

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yena yad vyāpyate vastu pariṇāmitayā svayam || 124 ||
children.translated_text: That entity which is pervaded by something through [the latter's] transformation — ||124||

children.text: sā tasya vikṛtiḥ proktā hemnastu makuṭo yathā |
children.translated_text: that is said to be the <s>vikṛti</s> (modification) of that [pervader]; just as a crown is [a modification] of gold.

body.translated_text: He applies this very meaning to the subject to be established —

children.translated_text: That sixfold path (<s>adhvan</s>) beginning with <s>kalā</s>, which is pervaded by <s>bindu</s> — ||125||
that is its modification; therefore, being pervaded, [it leads back to <s>bindu</s>] like <s>nāda</s> [leads to] <s>bindu</s>.
The sixfold path, excluding the impure <s>tattva</s> and <s>bhuvana</s> [paths], being an effect, like <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>, leads to
<s>bindu</s>, its own cause — this is the purport. ||125||

body.translated_text: Now he presents the view of those who hold <s>bindu</s> to be inherent [in <s>Śiva</s>] —

children.translated_text: Some say: <s>Bindu</s> is inherent in <s>Śiva</s>; therefore, ||126||
like the power of seeing (<s>dṛkśakti</s>), this supreme <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> is the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>).

children.text: jñānaśaktivadanyāpi bindvātmikā kriyāśaktiḥ śive samavaiti, na tu māyāvat tato
children.translated_text: Like the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), the other <s>Śakti</s> having the nature of <s>bindu</s>, i.e., <s>kriyāśakti</s>, is inherent in <s>Śiva</s> — not separate from him like <s>Māyā</s> —
this is the purport. ||126||

body.translated_text: And thus —

children.translated_text: Two <s>Śaktis</s> are inherent in <s>Śiva</s>: those having the nature of knowledge and action. ||127||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point]; therein —

body.text: ādyā tu saṃvid vijñānaṃ kriyā kuṇḍalinī parā |
body.translated_text: The first is <s>Saṃvid</s> (awareness), [also called] <s>Vijñāna</s> (knowledge); [the second,] action, is the supreme <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>.

children.text: ādyāyāḥ saṃvid vijñānamiti ca vyapadeśaḥ | anyasyāstu kriyā kuṇḍalinīti ca ||
children.translated_text: The first has the designations <s>Saṃvid</s> and <s>Vijñāna</s>; the other has [the designations] <s>Kriyā</s> and <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>.

body.translated_text: And of these two —

children.translated_text: Through the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), [<s>Śiva</s>] knows; through the power of action (<s>kriyā</s>), he creates the world. ||128||
'<s>Śiva</s>' should be supplied [as the subject]. ||128||

body.translated_text: 'Why?' — to this he answers:

body.text: kriyā hi phaladā puṃsāṃ na jñānaṃ syāt phalapradam |
body.translated_text: For indeed, action is fruit-giving for beings; knowledge is not fruit-giving.

children.translated_text: Because even for potters and others, the power of action alone, having the nature of effort,

children.text: phalamāvahati, jñānaśaktistu tattadarthaviṣayīkaraṇa eva caritārthā | tataḥ śivo'pi
children.translated_text: brings about the fruit in the form of producing pots and so on; but the power of knowledge is fulfilled merely in making the respective object its content. Therefore <s>Śiva</s> too,
knowing through the power of knowledge, creates everything through the power of action.

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.text: tābhyāṃ na virahastasya te ca na staḥ śivaṃ vinā || 129 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is never separated from these two [powers]; and they do not exist without <s>Śiva</s>. ||129||

body.text:
itthaṃ matāntareṇa bindoḥ śivasamavāyaṃ pradarśya tanmatenaiva 
sadāśivāditattvānyapi darśayati-
body.translated_text: Having thus shown the inherence of <s>bindu</s> in <s>Śiva</s> according to another view, he demonstrates the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> according to that very view —

children.text: tayoḥ prasaratoḥ sāmye tattvātmā syāt sadāśivaḥ |
children.translated_text: When those two [powers] proceed in equilibrium, [the result] is <s>Sadāśiva</s>, having the nature of a <s>tattva</s>;
when the power of action predominates over the power of knowledge in <s>Īśa</s> and <s>Vidyā</s> [tattvas respectively] — ||130||

children.text: tayoḥ kriyājñānayoḥ sāmyena prasaratoḥ satoḥ kriyāśakteriva
children.translated_text: When those two — action and knowledge — proceed in equilibrium,

the transformation having the nature of <s>Sadāśiva-tattva</s> occurs, as if from <s>kriyāśakti</s> [alone]; when <s>kriyāśakti</s> predominates, [the transformation] has the nature of <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>;
when <s>jñānaśakti</s> predominates, [it has] the nature of <s>Vidyā-tattva</s>. ||130||

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: In those <s>tattvas</s>, for the great souls who are <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (pure knowers),
varied worlds, consorts lovely by nature, ||131||
unfading enjoyments, and limbs and faculties —
<s>Śiva</s> creates [all these] through his <s>Śakti</s>, which is non-different [from him] and has the nature of action. ||132||
Through her, he also [creates] <s>nāda</s> and the rest; thus he is regarded as the creator of the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>).

body.translated_text: He summarizes the stated meaning —

children.text: ato nāyaṃ pṛthak śakteḥ śaktireva kriyātmikā || 133 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, this [<s>bindu</s>] is not separate from <s>Śakti</s>; <s>Śakti</s> herself, having the nature of action, ||133||
is inherent in <s>Śiva</s> — [and] <s>bindu</s> is spoken of there [as identical with her].

children.text: ato'yaṃ binduḥ śivasamavāyinyā jñānaśakternātyantaṃ pṛthagbhūto'pi tatsamavetā
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>bindu</s>, though not entirely separate from <s>jñānaśakti</s> which is inherent in <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: kriyāśaktireveti kecinmanyante | atha tannirāsāyāha- tatreti | siddhānto'bhidhīyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is actually <s>kriyāśakti</s> inherent in him — so some hold. Now, to refute that, he says 'there' — meaning: the established doctrine is stated. ||133||

body.translated_text: He states that very [doctrine] —

children.translated_text: This [<s>bindu</s>], within the Self, [producing] the multitude of <s>tattvas</s>, the series of numerous worlds, ||134||
creating various abundant bodies, enjoyments, faculties, and so forth —
<s>bindu</s> is rightly designated as transformative (<s>pariṇāmin</s>), like <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). ||135||
Since scripture declares <s>bindu</s> to be the material cause of <s>tattvas</s>, worlds, and so forth, its transformative nature,
like <s>Pradhāna</s> or like clay and so forth, must necessarily be accepted. ||134-135||

body.translated_text: 'What follows from that?' — to this he answers:

children.translated_text: That entity which is transformative is necessarily of inert nature;

children.text: yathā kṣīraṃ jaḍatve'sya samavāyaḥ kathaṃ śive || 136 ||
children.translated_text: just as milk [is inert]. If it is inert, how can it be inherent in <s>Śiva</s>? ||136||

children.text: pariṇāmitvāccāsya kṣīrādivajjaḍatvaṃ siddham | tataśca nāsya citsamavāyo yujyata
children.translated_text: And since it undergoes transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>), its insentience is established, like milk etc. Therefore, its conjunction with consciousness is not appropriate—
he says: 'Being insentient' (<s>jaḍatva</s>). || 136 ||

body.translated_text: If the conjunction with that [insentient Bindu] is accepted, then even <s>Śiva</s> would become insentient—he says—

children.translated_text: For that relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) with the insentient would bring insentience
to <s>Śiva</s>, whose sole nature is incomparable, undivided, and solidly conscious. || 137 ||

'Incomparable' because of being eternally liberated; 'undivided' because of being the object of all [knowledge]; 'solidly conscious' (<s>cidghana</s>) means a solid body consisting of knowledge and action—

children.text: ghanaṃ śarīramekameva svarūpaṃ yasya tasya śivasya | ayamarthaḥ- cetanātmikā śaktireva
children.translated_text: whose sole nature is that alone—of such <s>Śiva</s>. The meaning is this: the power (<s>śakti</s>) which is of the nature of consciousness alone

children.text: śivasya dehaḥ | sā caikā'pi jñeyakāryādyupādhibhedādupacāreṇa jñānakriyāśaktyā-
children.translated_text: is <s>Śiva</s>'s body. And although She is one, through the distinctions of conditions such as objects of knowledge, effects, etc., She is figuratively
designated as the power of knowledge, the power of action, etc. Through the states such as <s>Īśāna</s> etc. which assist in the five acts (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>),

children.text: kurvāṇopacāreṇa śarīratvenāpyupacaryata iti nāsyācetanabindusamavāyo yujyate, tatsamavāye
children.translated_text: performing the functions of a body, She is figuratively spoken of as a body as well. Therefore, conjunction of this [Śiva] with the insentient <s>Bindu</s> is not appropriate, for if such conjunction were accepted,
the fault of insentience and the like would follow. || 137 ||

body.translated_text: If one asks, 'Let Him be insentient—what is the fault?'—

children.translated_text: He who, deluded, with an inert intellect, considers the Lord to be inert—

children.text: na tasya yuktiḥ śāstraṃ vā nātmā nāsti ca devatā || 138 ||
children.translated_text: for him there is neither reasoning, nor scripture, nor Self, nor is there any deity. || 138 ||
If the insentience of the Lord is accepted, then there is contradiction by the inference that establishes the Lord through His being the creator of the world,
and by the <s>Āgamas</s> that teach His essential nature as consciousness, etc. Moreover, since the reasoning is
the same [for all conscious beings], the selves who are of the same class as <s>Śiva</s> would also become insentient. And since they [would be insentient],
deity too cannot be established, as [deity] is the agent of enjoyment and liberation [for souls]. || 138 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—
He [who holds such a view] is to be shunned by the learned, cast out from all systems of philosophy.

body.text:
nanu yuṣmatpakṣe'pi śivasya kartṛtvenābhyupagamāt kriyāveśena 
pariṇāmitāprasaṅgaḥ ? ata āha-
body.translated_text: But in your system too, since <s>Śiva</s> is accepted as the agent, does not the fault of transformation through engagement in action follow? To this he says—

children.translated_text: Because the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>), being the cause of action, is indeed consciousness (<s>cit</s>). || 139 ||

children.text: nātra kriyāveśaḥ, kartṛtvamapi tu kriyāyāṃ śaktatvameva |
children.translated_text: There is no engagement in action here; rather, agency is merely the capacity for action.

children.text: tataścāyaskāntaśakterivāyasi śivaśakteḥ sannidhimātreṇa bindāveva kriyāveśaḥ, ataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as the power of a magnet [acts] upon iron, so too the power of <s>Śiva</s>, by mere proximity alone, causes engagement in action in <s>Bindu</s> itself. Therefore,
since it is the cause of action, the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>) itself is called the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>)—thus there is no contradiction. || 139 ||

body.text:
atra parāśaṅkāpūrvakaṃ jāyate'dhvā yataḥ śuddhaḥ (ślo0 22) ityādi prāguktameva 
samarthayati-
body.translated_text: Here, prefaced by the opponent's doubt, he supports what was previously stated: 'From which the pure path arises' (verse 22) etc.—

children.translated_text: If it is held that there is no other insentient [reality] besides <s>Māyā</s> above [her level], and that <s>Bindu</s> [is identical with Māyā],

children.text: jāyate'dhvā kutaḥ śuddhaḥ kva vā līyeta kena vā || 140 ||
children.translated_text: then from what does the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>) arise? Where would it dissolve, and by what [cause]? || 140 ||
How would this [path] be sixfold, through the distinctions of <s>tattvas</s> (principles), <s>bhuvanas</s> (worlds), etc.?
And the <s>vijñānakevalas</s> (souls freed from <s>māyā</s> alone) are of three kinds—how, and from what cause? || 141 ||

body.translated_text: And how would they be liberated, without <s>Bindu</s> who brings about that diversity?

body.text: nanu cidrūpā śivaśaktireva tasya sarvasya heturata āha-
body.translated_text: But if [one says] the power of <s>Śiva</s>, which is of the nature of consciousness, is itself the cause of all that—to this he replies—

children.translated_text: For consciousness (<s>cit</s>) does not produce all of that through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). || 142 ||
'Because of the nature of consciousness' (<s>caitanyabhāvāt</s>)—this will be stated later in the determination of <s>Śakti</s>.
This was shown previously. And it has been established by us at length in the <s>Tattvaprakāśavṛtti</s>. || 142 ||

body.translated_text: Here the opponent's objection—

children.translated_text: This [Bindu] may be imagined to have manifold divisions due to the variety of effects. || 143 ||
If it is held that <s>Śiva</s> is one alone, possessing multiple powers—

children.text: nanūktavaccetanasya śivasya tattvādirūpeṇa pariṇāmo na yujyate, kintvekasyāpi
children.translated_text: as stated, transformation of the conscious <s>Śiva</s> into the form of <s>tattvas</s> etc. is not appropriate; but if the divisions into <s>Sadāśiva</s> and other <s>tattvas</s> are merely figurative,

children.text: śivasyānekaśakteḥ kāryabhedādaupacārikaḥ sadāśivāditattvabhedaḥ kālpanika eva, na tu
children.translated_text: due to the difference of effects, for the one <s>Śiva</s> who possesses multiple powers, being merely imagined and not

children.text: pāramārthika eveti yadyevaṃ bhavato'bhimatam, tatsatyameva, adhiṣṭhātṛviṣaye
children.translated_text: ultimately real—if this is your view, then that is indeed correct, with respect to the presiding [aspect], since
the distinction of states of <s>Śiva</s> as presider is figurative, being caused by the distinction in what is presided over. But the distinction of the presided-over
pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>) into <s>tattvas</s>, <s>bhuvanas</s>, etc. is indeed real; otherwise even figurative usage would be impossible. || 143 ||

body.translated_text: Now, if even that [pure path] is held to be unreal as a mere apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of consciousness, then—

children.translated_text: The path produced from <s>Māyā</s> too would likewise [be unreal], since there is no difference in reasoning. || 144 ||
Since the acceptance of apparent transformation is applicable to the impure path as well, that too would be reduced to unreality—that is the meaning. || 144

body.text: astu so'pyasatyaḥ, ko doṣa iti cet, tadayuktam, pramāṇabādhādityāha-
body.translated_text: If one says, 'Let that too be unreal—what is the fault?'—that is unjust, because it is contradicted by valid means of knowledge—he says—

children.translated_text: The pure paths, established by their respective causes, by scriptures, and even by the direct perception of <s>yogins</s>—
how could a wise person deny them? || 145 ||

children.text: atra ca śuddhādhvana ityupalakṣaṇamaśuddhānāmapi tattvādī-nām | tataśca
children.translated_text: Here, 'pure paths' is used by way of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) to include the <s>tattvas</s> etc. of the impure [path] as well. Therefore,
the acceptance of the unreality of the world in both its pure and impure forms is contradicted by all valid means of knowledge; hence the proponents of that view
are simply fools—that is the import. || 145 ||

body.translated_text: For indeed—

children.translated_text: Activity toward the distinguished Lord, the supremely generous giver, in accordance with scripture,
is declared to be for the sake of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and for liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). || 146 ||

children.text: śāstratastāvadbhogamokṣaprade śive siddhe sati śāstropadiṣṭakrameṇaiva bhogārthaṃ
children.translated_text: From scripture, first: when <s>Śiva</s> who bestows enjoyment and liberation is established, then in accordance with the procedure taught in scripture, the activity of souls for the sake of enjoyment
or for liberation is seen according to their respective qualifications. || 146 ||

body.text:
kiñca, bhogasthānamapi sākṣācchivakartṛkamatyantaśuddhaṃ śāstreṣu śrūyata iti 
darśayituṃ śrīmanmataṅgasūtraṃ (vi0 26|63) paṭhati-
body.translated_text: Moreover, to show that even the realm of enjoyment, being directly made by <s>Śiva</s>, is supremely pure as heard in the scriptures, he cites a <s>sūtra</s> from the blessed <s>Mataṅga</s> (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 26.63)—

children.translated_text: The station of <s>Sadāśiva</s> is attained through <s>yoga</s>, or through ritual practice (<s>caryā</s>), or through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>),
and through the distinction of consciousness, liberation [is attained]; or [these are attained] from the [combined] four. || 147 ||

children.text: cittabhedaśabdenātra jñānaṃ vivakṣitam | tataśca śuddhādhvani karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: By the word 'distinction of consciousness' (<s>cittabheda</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is intended here. And since in the pure path (<s>śuddhādhvan</s>), the operation of <s>karma</s>
is impossible, and since the enjoyment born from it, being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, is impure,

the pure enjoyment called 'non-ultimate liberation' (<s>aparamokṣa</s>), pertaining to the worlds of <s>Sadāśiva</s> etc., as well as the ultimate liberation (<s>paramokṣa</s>) consisting of equality with <s>Śiva</s>,

are attained through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) assisted by <s>yoga</s> etc. There, for those whose maturation of <s>mala</s> (impurity) is slow, who receive the elemental initiation (<s>bhautikadīkṣā</s>),
liberation is attained after enjoyment [in those worlds]; for those possessing advanced maturation of <s>mala</s>, who receive the final initiation (<s>naiṣṭhikadīkṣā</s>),

children.text: śarīrapātānantaram, sadyonirvāṇadīkṣābhājāṃ ca tadanantarameva mokṣaprāptiḥ | nanvasmin
children.translated_text: [liberation comes] immediately after the fall of the body; and for those receiving the initiation of immediate liberation (<s>sadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s>), liberation is attained immediately thereafter. Now, in this
<s>sūtra</s>, do not the four—initiation, ritual practice, knowledge, and <s>yoga</s>—appear as equally alternative means to enjoyment and liberation?

children.text: pratīyante ? naivam, vākyārthānabhijñānāt | evaṃ hi tatra vākyārthaḥ-
children.translated_text: Not so, due to ignorance of the sentence meaning. For the meaning of the sentence there is as follows:
Since '<s>Sadāśiva</s> station' is used here by way of indication [for all pure worlds], through <s>yoga</s> whose fruit is the direct realization of the respective world-lords,

children.text: tattadārādhanātmikayā vā caryayā, tattadbhuvanayojanātmikayā dīkṣayā ca,
children.translated_text: or through ritual practice (<s>caryā</s>) consisting of worship of those respective [lords], or through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) consisting of placing [the soul] in those respective worlds,

children.text: tattadbhuvaneśvarasvarūpa-niṣṭhena ca jñānena tattadbhuvaneṣu prāptirbhavatyeva, na tu
children.translated_text: or through knowledge established in the essential nature of those respective world-lords—attainment in those respective worlds indeed occurs; but not as equally alternative [means].

children.text: samavikalpatayā | jñānādiṣvapi dīkṣayā vinā'nadhikārāt tasyā eva prādhānyaṃ yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even among knowledge etc., since without initiation there is no qualification, initiation alone has primacy. Therefore:

children.text: mokṣo vā'tha catuṣṭayāt | asmāt samuccitān-naikasmād bhogo veti vāśabdārthaḥ | tathā
children.translated_text: 'Liberation, or from the [combined] four'—the meaning of the particle 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is: from this aggregate, not from just one, comes enjoyment [or liberation]. And

children.text: ca caryāyogayostāvaj-jñānaṃ vinānuṣṭhānameva nopapannam, nahyajñāte'rthe yogaś-caryā
children.translated_text: as for ritual practice (<s>caryā</s>) and <s>yoga</s>, without knowledge their very performance is impossible, for neither <s>yoga</s> nor ritual practice

children.text: vā saṃbhavati | jñānamapi dravyatvānmalādibandhānāṃ cakṣuṣaḥ paṭalānāmiva
children.translated_text: is possible regarding an unknown object. Knowledge too, since the bonds of <s>mala</s> etc. are substantial [realities],

children.text: cakṣurvaidyavyāpārād dīkṣākhyamīśvara-vyāpāraṃ vinā na tebhyaḥ puṃsāṃ mokṣaṃ
children.translated_text: like cataracts upon the eye, without the operation of the Lord called initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>)—like the operation of an eye-physician—cannot effect liberation for souls from those [bonds].

children.text: kartuṃ kṣamamityuktam | ato dīkṣaiva mokṣahetuḥ | uktaṃ ca tatraiva prakaraṇāntare-
children.translated_text: Therefore, initiation alone is the cause of liberation. As stated in another section of the same [text]:

children.text: tasmānmantrakriyā mukhyā seśvarī mukti muktidā (ma0 vi0 7|74) iti |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the ritual action involving <s>mantras</s>, presided over by the Lord, is the chief bestower of liberation' (<s>Mataṅga Vidyāpāda</s> 7.74).

children.text: śrīmatṣaṭsāhasrikāyāmapi- dīkṣaiva mokṣadā puṃsāṃ cidabhivyaktikāriṇī iti || 147 ||
children.translated_text: And in the blessed <s>Ṣaṭsāhasrikā</s> also: 'Initiation alone grants liberation to souls, being the cause of the manifestation of consciousness.' || 147 ||

body.text: atra ca sadāśivapadasya bhogādhikaraṇatvaṃ śrūyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: And here it is heard that the station of <s>Sadāśiva</s> is the locus of enjoyment—he says—
Thus enjoyment is declared [to be in] the great station of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.translated_text: By the word 'enjoyment,' figuratively, the locus of enjoyment is meant. And '<s>Sadāśiva</s> station' too
is used by way of indication for the worlds of the pure path—as stated.

body.text:
asya ca bhuvanarūpatvena kāryatvāt śuddhādhvatvācca bindurevopādānakāraṇatayā 
siddha ityuktamityabhiprāyeṇāha-
body.translated_text: And since this [pure path], being of the nature of worlds, is an effect, and since it belongs to the pure path, <s>Bindu</s> alone is established as the material cause—having stated this, with this intent he says—

children.translated_text: There, <s>Māyā</s> is not the material cause; the bodies and enjoyments etc. that arise [there are not from Māyā]. || 148 ||
Because of [its] supreme purity, therefore the pure path for the purpose of enjoyment is established,
there, in the station of <s>Sadāśiva</s>. || 148 ||

body.translated_text: He also establishes the pure path by another argument—

children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Māyā</s>, presided over by some agent who is directed [by Śiva], || 149 ||
is the material cause of the <s>kalās</s> (phases) etc., her nature being pervaded by the <s>kalās</s>.
Just as clay [is the material cause] of pots etc. through the potter, so indeed is she. || 150 ||
Adopting the <s>satkārya</s> (pre-existence of effect) position, the effects extending from <s>kalā</s> to earth are the <s>kalās</s>; by these,

children.text: śaktirūpābhirāśrayatvena vyāpyata iti kalāvyāptasvarūpiṇī māyā mṛdādivadaśuddhatvāt
children.translated_text: which are forms of <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Māyā</s> is pervaded as their substratum—hence she is 'of a nature pervaded by the <s>kalās</s>.' <s>Māyā</s>, being impure like clay etc.,

children.text: śivaprayojyena kartrā kṣobhyate, na tu binduvat sākṣācchivenetyuktam- śuddhe'dhvani śivaḥ
children.translated_text: is agitated by an agent directed by <s>Śiva</s>, not directly by <s>Śiva</s> as in the case of <s>Bindu</s>—as stated: 'In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is

children.text: kartā prokto'nanto'site prabhuḥ || (ki0 vi0 3|27) iti | kulālasyāpi śivaprayojyatvaṃ darśayati-
children.translated_text: declared the agent; <s>Ananta</s> is the lord in the impure [path]' (<s>Kiraṇa Vidyāpāda</s> 3.27). He shows that the potter too is directed by <s>Śiva</s>—
'Just as indeed' (<s>tathā hi</s>). || 149–150 ||

body.translated_text: The directed one, due to being a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), is the agent; the supreme Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) is the cause [behind him].

children.text: paśutvādeva kulālaḥ prayojyaḥ kartā, nirmalatvācchivaḥ prayojakakartetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Due to being a bound soul, the potter is a directed agent; due to being free from impurity, <s>Śiva</s> is the directing agent—that is the meaning.

body.translated_text: For indeed—

children.translated_text: This living being (<s>jantu</s>) is declared to be ignorant and powerless even in its own bodily activities. || 151 ||
Impelled by the Lord, it performs either auspicious or inauspicious [actions].

body.translated_text: Having thus established the illustration, he applies it to the thing illustrated—

children.translated_text: <s>Ananta</s>, being directed [by Śiva], endowed with body etc., is like the potter. || 152 ||
He by whom <s>Māyā</s> is agitated—with body, senses,
and location etc.—that pure path is established in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>. || 153 ||
'By whom' means 'made of which'—that is the meaning. 'With location etc.' means with a substratum in the form of worlds etc. By the word 'etc.' [is included]

children.text: prāguktena savikalpakajñānahetunā śabdena ca yukto'nantaḥ kartā | sa śuddho'dhvā
children.translated_text: the previously mentioned <s>śabda</s> (word) which is the cause of determinate knowledge; thus endowed, <s>Ananta</s> is the agent. That pure path
is established in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>. || 152–153 ||

body.text:
itthaṃ matāntaranirākaraṇena parigrahaśaktirūpāṃ 
śuddhādhvopādānabhūtāmacetanāṃ parabindusaṃjñāṃ mahāmāyāṃ prasādhya 
matāntareṇā'śuddhādhvano'pi bindūpādānatvaṃ māyāyāśca kāryatvamupanyasyati-
body.translated_text: Having thus established through the refutation of other views the insentient <s>Mahāmāyā</s> called <s>Parabindu</s>, which is in the form of the power of appropriation (<s>parigrahaśakti</s>) and is the material cause of the pure path, he now presents, according to another view, the material causality of <s>Bindu</s> for the impure path also, and the status of <s>Māyā</s> as an effect—

children.translated_text: Others, the learned, call <s>Māyā</s> a state of <s>Bindu</s>,
since she is of a nature pervaded by the <s>kalās</s> and is presided over by individual souls (<s>pudgala</s>). || 154 ||
Since—from the <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> <s>tattva</s> [downward]—<s>Māyā</s> too is pervaded by the <s>kalās</s> belonging to <s>Bindu</s>,

children.text: paścātmādhiṣṭhitā ca, tasmāt tāmapi bindorevāvasthāṃ kāryarūpāṃ sūkṣmāṃ
children.translated_text: and is presided over by bound souls, therefore they call her too a state of <s>Bindu</s> alone—a subtle form,
a transformation in the form of an effect. || 154 ||
Likewise, <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is [also a state] of that same [Bindu]: gross, subtle, and supreme—thus

children.text: mahāmāyā bhavet tredhā tatra sthūlā guṇātmikā || 155 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmāyā</s> is threefold. Among these, the gross one is of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). || 155 ||
<s>Prakṛti</s>, the generator of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and other objects of enjoyment, belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> (the individual soul).
They call <s>Prakṛti</s> also a gross state of that very same [Bindu]. Thus, for those

children.text: bindvekopādānavādināṃ sā mahāmāyā sthūlasūkṣmaparabhedena tridhā bhidyate |
children.translated_text: who hold the doctrine that <s>Bindu</s> alone is the material cause, that <s>Mahāmāyā</s> is divided into three through the distinctions of gross, subtle, and supreme.

children.text: sthūlā sā bindvavasthā sattvarajastamorūpā puruṣasya buddhyādīni bhogasādhanāni tattvāni
children.translated_text: The gross state of <s>Bindu</s>, of the nature of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, producing for <s>Puruṣa</s> the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) such as <s>buddhi</s> etc. which are the means of enjoyment,
and generating the objects of enjoyment successively, is called <s>Prakṛti</s>. || 155 ||
The subtle one is of the nature of non-differentiation of the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>kalā</s>. || 156 ||
The deluding <s>Māyā</s>, the generator [of those tattvas], is the cause of the entire impure path (<s>aśuddhādhva</s>).

children.text: sūkṣmā tu māyāsaṃjñā bhoktṛtvahetūnāṃ kalāditattvānāṃ sarvasya ca
children.translated_text: The subtle one, bearing the name <s>Māyā</s>, of the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>kalā</s> which are the causes of the state of being an enjoyer, and of all

children.text: prakṛtyāderapi tattvabhuvanātmanastadvartinaśca sākṣāt paramparayā ca kāraṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: the <s>tattvas</s>, <s>bhuvanas</s> etc. in the form of <s>Prakṛti</s> and their contents—is the cause, both directly and successively.

body.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: mantrayoniḥ parā māyā nityā kuṇḍalinī tu yā || 157 ||
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Māyā</s>, the source of <s>mantras</s>, eternal, which is <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, || 157 ||
is the material cause of the bodies of those who possess knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), lordship (<s>īśvara</s>), and selfhood (<s>ātman</s>).

children.text: parā tu māyopādānamiti | māyāyāścopādānabhūtā mahāmāyetyarthaḥ | sā ca
children.translated_text: But the supreme <s>Māyā</s> is the material cause — the meaning is that <s>Mahāmāyā</s> is the material cause (upādāna) of <s>Māyā</s>. And she is
eternal, because she is the supreme cause. || 157 ||

body.translated_text: And from that —

children.text: kāryātmikā sā māyeyaṃ pariṇāmavatī ca yat || 158 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Māyā</s>, whose nature is that of an effect, and which undergoes transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) — || 158 ||
produces the agent (soul) endowed with body and senses.

body.translated_text: And thus —

children.translated_text: The accomplishment of the purified path remains unobstructable. || 159 ||
For those in whose view <s>Māyā</s> is non-eternal and is the cause of <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, etc.,
for them, the impure path is not purified through the purification of <s>kalā</s>. || 160 ||

children.text: itthaṃ paramatena māyāyāḥ kāryatvaṃ prasādhya māyāyā anityatve
children.translated_text: Having thus established by the supreme doctrine that <s>Māyā</s> is an effect, he states the fault in <s>Māyā</s> being non-eternal —
'For those' etc. If the non-eternality of <s>Māyā</s> means one does not accept it as the material cause of the pure path,
then through the purification of the <s>kalā</s>-path, which is an effect of <s>bindu</s>, the purification of the impure path, which is an effect of <s>Māyā</s>, would not occur, since
the purification of one thing cannot bring about the purification of another. Therefore, since purification cannot be explained otherwise, the pure path too must be accepted as
an effect of <s>bindu</s> alone. || 159–160 ||

body.translated_text: He states this very point —

children.text: kalā hi śodhitāḥ pañca nivṛttyādyā viśuddhaye |
children.translated_text: For the five <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>nivṛtti</s> are purified for the sake of purification
of the <s>tattvas</s> and so forth; therefore the path is specifically an effect of <s>bindu</s>. || 161 ||

The purport is that if it is an effect of <s>bindu</s>, then through the purification of the <s>kalās</s> which serve as the material cause, the purification of all <s>tattvas</s> and the rest is unobstructable.

body.text:
nanu vyāpikānāṃ kalānāṃ śuddhyā vyāpyasya tattvādeḥ śuddhirbhaviṣyatītyata 
āha-
body.translated_text: Now, if one objects that through the purification of the <s>kalās</s>, which are pervaders, the purification of the pervaded — the <s>tattvas</s> and so forth — will follow, he says —

children.translated_text: But purification in the paths is not considered to result merely from the purification of pervaders;
of the <s>kalās</s>, which are not of the nature of material causes, being eternally pure, || 162 ||
the purification of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> alone would always absurdly follow.
Thus <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, the supreme source (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all paths, has been declared || 163 ||
by those <s>ācāryas</s> who are expert in the doctrine that all paths are effects.

body.text:
atra ca māyāyā anityatve pramāṇābhāvāt, śuddhasya 
bindoraśuddhopādānatvāyogāt, nityatvaśrutivirodhāccāyaṃ pakṣaḥ prayatnena nirākṛta iti 
matvā siddhāntajñānināmācāryāṇāṃ matena māyāyā nityatvasādhanāyāha-
body.translated_text: And here, since there is no evidence for the non-eternality of <s>Māyā</s>, since it is impossible for the pure <s>bindu</s> to be the material cause of the impure, and since it contradicts the scriptural statements of eternality — this position has been carefully refuted. Knowing this, in order to establish the eternality of <s>Māyā</s> according to the view of the <s>ācāryas</s> who know the <s>siddhānta</s>, he says —

children.translated_text: Others, however, declare <s>Māyā</s> here to be imperishable in the paths, || 164 ||
the material cause of <s>kalā</s> and the rest, and pervaded by <s>bindu</s>.
As stated in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and other texts: '<s>Māyā-tattva</s> is the seed of the world, indestructible and imperishable in nature,' and so on.
Also in the venerable <s>Raurava</s>: 'The lord of lords, sovereign of <s>vidyā</s>, the king of <s>mantras</s>, having agitated <s>Māyā</s>,
produced <s>kalā</s>' (1.6–7) and so on. || 164 ||

body.text:
nanu māyāyā akāryatve'pyaśuddhādhvano vyāpakamātrakalā-śuddhyā 
śuddhirbhavediti cedatiprasaṅgādityuktam, ata āha-
body.translated_text: Now, if one says that even though <s>Māyā</s> is not an effect, the impure path could be purified merely by the purification of the pervading <s>kalās</s> — since this leads to an absurd over-extension, as stated, therefore he says —

children.translated_text: And such purification should be understood by knowers of the <s>āgamas</s> as belonging to both. || 165 ||
By which the purification of the other (the pervaded) occurs through the purification of the pervader alone.
The purification of the pervaded path alone through the purification of the pervading <s>kalās</s> is established in <s>dīkṣā</s>

children.text: karmabhojanādidvāreṇopapadyata ityāgameṣu śrūyate | ayaṃ cātrābhiprāyaḥ- karmasadbhāve
children.translated_text: through the means of experiencing <s>karma</s> and so forth — thus it is heard in the <s>āgamas</s>. And the intention here is this: when <s>karma</s> exists,

children.text: hyātmanāṃ kalādiko'śuddhādhvā bandhatvenāvatiṣṭhate, tasya śuddhistān prati
children.translated_text: the impure path of <s>kalā</s> and the rest persists as bondage for the souls; its purification means

children.text: bandhakatvanivṛttirevābhimatā | sā ca malaparipākayuktasya dīkṣayā karmakṣayādupajāyate |
children.translated_text: the cessation of its nature as bondage with respect to them. And that arises through <s>dīkṣā</s> from the exhaustion of <s>karma</s> for one whose <s>mala</s> has matured.

children.text: taduktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇe- anekabhavikaṃ karma dagdhabījamivāṇubhiḥ | bhaviṣyadapi saṃruddhaṃ
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>: '<s>Karma</s> accumulated over many births, like seeds that have been burnt, and future [karma] too, being obstructed —

children.text: yenedaṃ taddhi bhogataḥ || (vi0 6|19) iti | śrīmatsvāyambhuve'pi- dharmādharmakṣaya-karī
children.translated_text: that [is destroyed] through experience' (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 6.19). Also in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s>: '<s>Dīkṣā</s> is the destroyer of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.'

children.text: dīkṣā iti | ataśca sarveṣvadhvasu pratyekamitarādhvāntarbhāvena bhogabhojanādirūpā
children.translated_text: And therefore, in all the paths, through the inclusion of each in the other paths, <s>dīkṣā</s> in the form of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and enjoyment is established,
and thus through the purification of the pervading <s>kalā</s>-path, the purification of the pervaded impure path of <s>tattvas</s>, <s>bhuvanas</s>, etc.,

children.text: sādhāraṇarūpasya taṃ prati bandhakatvanivṛttilakṣaṇā śuddhirupapadyata iti na kaściddoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: which has a common form, consisting in the cessation of its bondage-nature with respect to that [soul] — this purification is established, and so there is no fault. ||

body.text: itthaṃ māyāyā nityatve'pi doṣābhāvamuktvā punarapi bindumeva viśeṣayati-
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the absence of fault even when <s>Māyā</s> is eternal, he further specifies <s>bindu</s> —

children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, the womb of <s>mantras</s>, which abides as a possession [of <s>Śiva</s>], || 166 ||
the <s>śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, pervaded [by him], by whom all individual souls —
Since the denoted <s>mantras</s> cannot arise [without a cause], <s>Mahāmāyā</s> is the womb of the denoting <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: yonirmahāmāyā | sā ca śivasya parigrahaśaktirucyate, yayā sarve'pi paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: being the material cause of sound. And she is called the possessive <s>śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, by whom all <s>paśus</s> (bound souls)
are governed through <s>nāda</s> and other means as previously stated. || 166 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: This <s>śakti</s>, whose nature is action (<s>kriyā</s>), belonging to the sovereign Lord, is ever-arisen; || 167 ||
abiding in the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) alone, it is established as a bond (<s>pāśa</s>).
And since the Lord of all is governed by <s>kriyāśakti</s> (the power of action), for the purpose of producing pure effects, and since it abides

children.text: ca kriyāśaktyavivekena sthitatvācca kaiścid bhrāntyā kriyāśaktiraiśvarīti proktā, na tu
children.translated_text: in the souls without distinction from [their own] <s>kriyāśakti</s>, some, out of confusion, have called it the sovereign <s>kriyāśakti</s>; but in reality
it is not the <s>kriyāśakti</s> inherent in consciousness, because being a material cause, it is insentient — as has been stated. Therefore,

children.text: muktāṇuṣu na pravartate, paśuṣveva vartamānatvāt | iyamapi pāśatayaiva sthitā, na tu
children.translated_text: it does not operate in liberated souls, since it exists only in bound souls. This too is established only as a bond (<s>pāśa</s>), and not
as inhering in <s>Śiva</s> who transcends bonds. || 167 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: It perpetually causes the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls) to revolve in various wombs, without certainty. || 168 ||

children.text: seyaṃ kriyāśaktiravyatirekeṇa jñātā satī paśūnaśuddhāsu yoniṣu yojayati | tadviveke
children.translated_text: This <s>kriyāśakti</s>, when known without discrimination, yokes the <s>paśus</s> to impure wombs. But when there is discrimination,
there is no attainment of impure wombs — that is the meaning. || 168 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover —
By the power of its own reflective awareness, it bestows both enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).

children.text: svakīyena parāmarśajñānātmanā vīryeṇa bhogamokṣau prayacchati, bhogamokṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: By the power that has the nature of its own reflective knowledge, it bestows <s>bhoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s> — the meaning is that
it is indirectly instrumental to both <s>bhoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s>.

body.text:
māyā tu bhogopakārikā, anātmādiṣvātmādijñānahetutvāt, tatrāsya 
bhogopakāritvaṃ darśayati-
body.translated_text: But <s>Māyā</s> aids enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), because it causes the knowledge of self etc. in what is non-self etc. He shows its role in aiding enjoyment —

children.translated_text: She, by means of the arising of conditions that serve as instruments for the attainment of enjoyment, || 169 ||
through the accompaniment of words, always deludes [the souls] when not discriminated.
<s>Mahāmāyā</s>, whose nature is undiscriminated,

always deludes the <s>paśus</s> through the accompaniment of words, which is the cause of the arising of determinate cognition (<s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s>) that serves as the means for apprehending the instruments of enjoyment.

body.translated_text: And at that time —

children.translated_text: Effecting the separation from the attainment of immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) in every way, || 170 ||
then, for one whose mind is engrossed in the pleasure of sensory enjoyment —
For the person who has faith in sensory enjoyment, it at that time brings about in every way the state of being outside
the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> — that is the meaning. || 170 ||

body.translated_text: He also shows its instrumentality for liberation —

children.translated_text: Knowledge is the means to the attainment of supreme immortality, and is the instrument (<s>parikara</s>) of the bound soul. || 171 ||
The cause of the means called <s>dīkṣā</s> for attaining supreme liberation, and of the obligatory and other rites (<s>nityādi-karma</s>) to be performed after that,
is discriminative knowledge alone, since practice is impossible regarding an unknown object,
and even in <s>nirbīja-dīkṣā</s> (seedless initiation), knowledge is primary for the <s>ācārya</s>. || 171 ||

body.text: tasya ca śivādivastuviṣayakajñānasya śāstradvāreṇa bindureva saṃpādaka ityāha-
body.translated_text: And that knowledge concerning <s>Śiva</s> and other realities is produced by <s>bindu</s> alone through the medium of scripture — he says —

children.translated_text: And that [knowledge], through the accompaniment of words, arose from the mass of sounds; and the mass of sounds arose from <s>bindu</s>, and <s>bindu</s> too from <s>nāda</s>. || 172 ||
[Placeholder verse number integrated with next]
This <s>bindu</s>, [arising] from the unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>), is the cause of the pure path.

'<s>Anāhata-bindu</s>' is the designation of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, the source of the pure path. And it has been stated that the production of sound occurs through the sequence of <s>nāda</s>, <s>bindu</s>, etc. || 172 ||
[Continuation of commentary on verse 172.]
There, in the capacity of enjoyers, through enjoyments pertaining to body and senses, || 173 ||

children.text: malaḥ karma ca māyā ca viśuddhamanumīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>mala</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>māyā</s> are inferred to be pure.
And there, since the status of enjoyer is heard of for <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others, and since enjoyment is inseparable from body etc.,
and since <s>mala</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s>, which are the causes of impure body etc. that serve as instruments of impure enjoyment, are impossible there,
a pure <s>adhikāra-mala</s> (functional impurity), which is the cause of the status of enjoyer through pure body etc. that serve as instruments of pure enjoyment,

children.text: śuddhaṃ ceśvarasevātmakaṃ sahakāri karma, śuddhā ca māyā
children.translated_text: and pure cooperative <s>karma</s> consisting of service to the Lord, and pure <s>Māyā</s>
as the material cause of body etc. — these are inferred. And the attainment of the <s>bhuvanas</s> of <s>Mahāmāyā</s> for
that <s>adhikāra-mala</s> and <s>karma</s> consisting of service to the Lord, or <s>dīkṣā</s> which is the cause of that, is what produces [this], since
only for those who have transcended <s>Māyā</s> and whose obscuring <s>mala</s> has been severed is that possible. || 173 ||

body.translated_text: He states this very point —

children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> alone is the cause of both pure and impure <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>. || 174 ||

body.translated_text: Of the impure — namely, the impure <s>puṃstva-mala</s> (masculinity-impurity) which has the nature of false identification of self etc. in non-self etc. and is the cause of impure enjoyment, and of <s>karma</s> consisting of the performance of horse-sacrifices, brahmanicide, and the like — he says that contact with the effects of impure <s>Māyā</s> is the cause —
Of the two impure [mala and karma], impure <s>Māyā</s> alone [is the cause]; hence <s>Māyā</s> is considered twofold.

children.text: na tvāṇavamalasya sā heturiti vyākhyeyam, tasyānādyāvārakatvena śravaṇāt,
children.translated_text: But it should not be explained that she is the cause of <s>āṇava-mala</s>, since that is heard to be a beginningless obscurer,

children.text: ādimattve ca āvaraṇakāraṇāsaṃbhavāt | nanu karmāpyevamanādikam (ki0 vi0 3|7) iti śruteḥ,
children.translated_text: and if it had a beginning, the impossibility of there being a cause of obscuration [would follow]. Now, since it is heard that '<s>karma</s> too is beginningless in this way' (<s>Kiraṇa</s>, <s>Vidyāpāda</s> 3.7),

children.text: karmasadbhāva eva māyāpravṛtteśca kathaṃ karmaṇo māyā kāraṇamucyate, satyaṃ
children.translated_text: and since <s>Māyā</s> operates only when <s>karma</s> exists, how can <s>Māyā</s> be called the cause of <s>karma</s>? True,
the stream of <s>karma</s> and body is beginningless as a flow; and without <s>karma</s>, <s>Māyā</s> indeed does not operate. Nevertheless,

children.text: karmānuṣṭhānasya dehavatāmeva saṃbhavād vāsanārūpasya ca karmaṇo buddhidvāreṇa
children.translated_text: since the performance of <s>karma</s> is possible only for embodied beings, and since <s>karma</s> in the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) resides
in <s>Māyā</s> through the <s>buddhi</s>, it is stated thus — and there is no contradiction. <s>Karma</s> too, like agricultural work,

children.text: puruṣasaṃskārakatve tasya vikāritvaprasaṅgād buddhau guṇatvena vartata iyuktaṃ
children.translated_text: since it transforms <s>prakṛti</s>, if it were to transform the <s>puruṣa</s>, the absurd consequence of his being mutable would follow — it is fitting that it operates as a quality in the <s>buddhi</s>,

children.text: śrīmanmataṅgādau | ataśca māyāmahāmāyātmakadvayaṃ nityasiddhamityāha- māyā'ta iti |
children.translated_text: as stated in the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s> and other texts. And therefore, the dyad consisting of <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Mahāmāyā</s> is eternally established — he says 'Māyā therefore' etc.

children.text: evaṃ visadṛśakāryatvād māyāyā bindukāryatvaṃ na saṃbhavatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purport is that since the effects [of the two] are dissimilar, <s>Māyā</s> cannot be an effect of <s>bindu</s>. ||
Upon the discrimination of <s>bindu</s>, the sheath of <s>mala</s> is suddenly cut asunder. || 175 ||

children.text: malasya dravyatvena jñānānivartyatāyā uktatvāt, dīkṣayā kṣapitamalānāmeva
children.translated_text: Since it has been stated that <s>mala</s>, being a substance, cannot be removed by knowledge, and since only those whose <s>mala</s> has been destroyed by <s>dīkṣā</s>
attain the <s>bhuvanas</s> of the pure path, and since discriminative knowledge of <s>Mahāmāyā</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is possible
through scripture, the destruction of <s>adhikāra-mala</s> occurs upon that discrimination. || 175 ||

body.translated_text: But upon the discrimination of <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is the destruction of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and [their] husks.

children.text: yadāhuḥ- jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute (bha0 gī0 4|37) iti | tataśca
children.translated_text: As they say: 'The fire of knowledge reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes' (<s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> 4.37). And therefore,

children.text: karmakṣaye'pi pariṇatamalānāṃ vijñānakevalatva-meva | prakṛtipuruṣaviveke tu tadapi nāstyeva
children.translated_text: even upon the destruction of <s>karma</s>, for those whose <s>mala</s> has matured, there is only the state of <s>vijñāna-kevala</s>. But upon the discrimination of <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, even that does not exist.
As stated by the accomplished masters: 'Since enjoyment above <s>guṇa-tattva</s> and <s>karma</s> are not apprehended, even the <s>kaivalya</s>

children.text: sāṃkhyānāṃ naiva yuktamasaṃkṣayāt || (pa0 mo0 kā0 53) iti ||
children.translated_text: of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> is not tenable, due to the non-destruction [of mala]' (<s>Paramokṣa-nirāsa-kārikā</s> 53). ||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: Directing [its activity] toward the soul that has transcended <s>Māyā</s> but is still connected with <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, || 176 ||
the <s>śakti</s> of the Lord operates for the agitation of <s>bindu</s>.
Toward one who is a recipient of the <s>dīkṣā</s> of a <s>sādhaka</s> and desires pure enjoyment, the <s>śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s> produces body and other [instruments]
from the agitated <s>bindu</s> — that is the meaning. || 176 ||

body.translated_text: And that [bindu], agitated by <s>śakti</s> —

children.translated_text: Just as the ocean transforms only on its surface due to the impulsion of wind, || 177 ||
<s>bindu</s> transforms from one part [only] by the [impulsion] of <s>śakti</s>, and yet pervades all.

children.text: śakteḥ preraṇād ghṛtakīṭanyāyenaikadeśena bindurvikaroti, na tu kṣīradadhinyāyena
children.translated_text: By the impulsion of <s>śakti</s>, <s>bindu</s> transforms through one part according to the analogy of the insect in ghee, not by its entire nature as in the analogy of milk becoming curds,
because if it were so, the absurd consequence of non-eternality and infinite regress would follow — that is the meaning. Moreover,

children.text: svakāryarūpābhiḥ kalābhiḥ prāguktaṃ viśvaṃ vyāpnoti cetyarthaḥ || 177 ||
children.translated_text: through the <s>kalās</s> that constitute its own effects, it pervades the universe as previously described — that is the meaning. || 177 ||

body.translated_text: And this principle applies elsewhere as well — he says —

children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> too transforms from one part, and likewise pervades all || 178 ||
its own effects; similarly, <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest, i.e. <s>pradhāna</s>) is held [to function the same way].

children.text: ayamatra bindormāyāpradhānayorviśeṣo yat svakāryamevaite vyāpnuvataḥ, na tu
children.translated_text: The distinction here between <s>bindu</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>pradhāna</s> is that these pervade only their own effects, not

children.text: svasmādūrdhvam, tatra pragamāsaṃbhavāt | ataḥ śuddhasya tvaśuddhādhvanyapi vyāpakatvāt
children.translated_text: what is above them, since extension beyond [their domain] is impossible. But the pure [bindu], since it pervades even the impure path,
extension [beyond its own effects] is indeed possible. || 178 ||

body.text:
tatrānandarūpiṇi samantādvyāptisamṛddhibhāji bindāvakṣubdhe śivaśaktyā 
kṣobhanimitte viṣayīkṛte prasavaunmukhyabhāji sati śivaśakterudyogāt pālanātmako bhogo

children.text: yaduktam- adhikārī sa bhogī ca layī syādupacārataḥ iti | anena
atiśayāvadhibhūtā | parā sūkṣmā atyantasūkṣmā | atilālasā sarvānugrahaṇaśīlā ca
kartṛbhūtasya śivasya sannidhau karaṇabhūtayā śaktyā saṃbandhād binduḥ
kāryotpādaka ityāha- śivasyeti | binduḥ pratipuruṣaṃ bhinnairnādairātmanāṃ

body.text:
nanvindriyādirahitasya kartṛtvaṃ na yujyate ? tanna, svadehaspandādāvātmanaḥ 
śaktimātrasya karaṇasya darśanāt, asyāśca śivasamavāyena pariṇāmābhāvāt 
kāryabhedādaupacārika evecchājñānakriyādibheda ityāha-

children.text: anenāsyāḥ sarvādhiṣṭhānamuktam | yadāhuḥ- na sā bhāvakalā kācit
santānadvayavartinī | vyāptrī śivakalā yasyāmadhiṣṭhātrī na vidyate || iti |
na jāyate na mriyate kṣīyate na ca vardhate || 195 ||
tadaprakāśarūpaṃ vā jaḍaṃ vā dṛśyate yathā |
yato'sāvaprakāśarūpā jaḍā ca na bhavati, tato na vikāriṇītyarthaḥ || 196-197 ||

body.text:
evamasyāḥ kṣīradadhinyāyena sarvātmanā paraṃ vikāro nirākṛtaḥ, 
idānīmuktābhyāmeva hetubhyāmekadeśapariṇāmo'pi nāstītyāha-

children.text: tathāhi tāṃ samāśritya santo'nye śāśvatī satī |
tatsattā sādhyate kasya kena vā pratipādyate |
śuddhāśuddhamayasya kāryarūpasya jagataḥ siddhirnānyathā, tasyāḥ sattā kenānyena
vipaścita ityākṣepe | evaṃ hi te manyante- śaktireva cidrūpā satyabhūtā | sā ca

body.text: sā vidhātrī padārthānāṃ na niṣedhati kiñcana |

children.text: taduktam- āhurvidhātṛ pratyakṣaṃ na niṣedhṛ vipaścitaḥ (bra0 si0 2|1) iti | tataśca
tatastatpramāṇamiṣyate | yadāhuḥ- kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntaṃ pratyakṣam (nyā0 vi0 1|4) iti ||
grahaṇaṃ na saṃbhavatītyuktam, ataḥ svapnādijñānavadasatyabhūta evāyaṃ
mucyate tebhya evāyaṃ bandhamokṣau na vastutaḥ || 212 ||
sādhyeta taireva dṛḍhaṃ tasyāḥ syāt sadvitīyatā || 214 ||
yadi saṃvidaikyaṃ lokasya vyavahārasiddhaiḥ pramāṇairbhavadbhiḥ sādhyate, tatastaireva
sādhyadharmiṇi parvatādau dhūmavattvena hetunā prasiddho vahnimattvarūpadharmo'numīyate |
tataḥ pṛthageva bhedena dharmyādayaḥ siddhā abhyupagantavyāḥ || 215 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) and the other [components of inference] must be accepted as established separately, through difference. || 215 ||

body.translated_text: For indeed—

children.text: na siddhaḥ sādhyate dharmo nāsiddhairapi taistathā |
children.translated_text: An already-established property (<s>dharma</s>) is not [re-]proved; nor by those [components] which are themselves unestablished.
And establishment and non-establishment, being combined, cannot reside in one and the same [entity]. || 216 ||

children.text: nahi siddhasya sādhakāntarāpekṣā, nāpyasiddhā hetvādayaḥ siddhaṃ sādhayanti ||
children.translated_text: For what is already established has no need of another means of proof; nor do unestablished [components] such as the probans (<s>hetu</s>) prove what is established.

body.translated_text: And therefore—

body.text:
sapakṣapakṣayorbhede pramāṇamanumā bhavet |
	aikye hi na tayorhetusādharmya
body.translated_text: When the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) and the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) are different, inference can be a valid means of knowledge. For if the two were identical, the homogeneity of the probans (<s>hetu-sādharmya</s>)

children.translated_text: since, if the <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>sapakṣa</s> were identical, there would be no homogeneity of the probans—namely, the property of possessing smoke, established in the example,

children.text: sādhyadharmiṇi dhūmavattvasya sādharmyaṃ na bhavati, tasmāt tayoraikye nānumānāt
children.translated_text: with respect to the subject (<s>sādhya-dharmin</s>). Therefore, if the two were identical, the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) through inference
would not occur. || 217 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover, in the absence of an example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), even the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is not possible—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Due to its absence, || 217 ||
whose <s>vyāpti</s> with what, and how [could it be apprehended]?

body.translated_text: Thus, if inference is accepted for the purpose of proving non-duality, difference necessarily follows—he says—

children.translated_text: For establishing non-duality,
the inferential proof employed declares difference, for the establishment of its own components. || 218 ||
For the establishment of its own components such as the probans (<s>hetu</s>) and the like—this is the meaning. || 218 ||

body.text: kiñca, saṃvidekaiveti saṃvidviṣayabhedaniṣedhe jaṣaviṣayo bhedo na niṣiddhyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if one denies the difference of objects of consciousness while holding that consciousness is one alone, the difference pertaining to insentient objects is not negated—thus he says—

children.translated_text: 'Non-dual'—even such a negation would apply [only] to consciousness (<s>citi</s>), according to that doctrine.
Therefore, the state of duality would be established with respect to everything else; and even if [non-duality] were established [for consciousness], certainly || 219 ||
their thesis, which is a mere display of wishful thinking, would be broken.

body.translated_text: Even if the authority of scripture (<s>Āgama</s>) is accepted, non-duality is lost—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Scripture (<s>Āgama</s>) too, through the specific meanings recalled by those various [words], || 220 ||
how could it convey the collection of objects qualified by relation?
If this non-dual consciousness were intended to be expressed by their own [scripture], || 221 ||

body.text:
yadi svenāgamenādvayā saṃvittirabhidhitsitā syāt, kathamasau 
jātiguṇakriyādravyavācibhirgauriyaṃ śvetā gacchati grāmamityādibhiḥ padaiḥ 
smāritārthaviśeṣā padārthajātasaṃsargarūpāṃ viśiṣṭāṃ buddhiṃ janayet | etaduktaṃ 
bhavati- āgamasya satyabhūtasya pramāṇatayā'bhyupagame
body.translated_text: if non-dual consciousness were intended to be expressed by their own scripture, how could that [scripture], through words such as 'cow,' 'this [is] white,' 'goes to the village,' and so forth—which denote genus, quality, action, and substance—recalling specific meanings, generate a qualified cognition in the form of a connection of a collection of objects? What is being said is this: if scripture, being real, is accepted as a valid means of knowledge,

children.text: tena tadavayavaistadarthaiśca dravyādibhiḥ satyaiśca bhāvyam, ato'yamevādvaitavirodha iti
children.translated_text: then its parts, their meanings, and the categories such as substance and the rest must also be accepted as real; therefore this itself contradicts non-duality.

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: How can scripture establish non-duality, and how can inference [do so],
when [both are] obstructed by their own components that are capable of destroying non-duality? || 222 ||

body.translated_text: Now, in order to show the impossibility of the primary meaning of non-duality scriptures such as 'consciousness-power is one alone,' due to their conflict with other valid means of knowledge, he says—

children.translated_text: Moreover, words are seen to abandon their primary meaning due to conflict,
and to operate with a secondary (figurative) meaning, both in ordinary usage and in the <s>Vedas</s>. || 223 ||
'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is an ox,' 'the sacrificial post is the sun'—such [expressions] and the like.

body.translated_text: But inference, when <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance)—characterized by the relation of inseparable connection—has been apprehended, inevitably establishes its object as a valid means of knowledge—thus he says—

children.text: naivaṃ heturaduṣṭāyāṃ vyāptau sādhyaṃ na sādhayet || 224 ||
children.translated_text: It is not the case that a probans (<s>hetu</s>), when the <s>vyāpti</s> is unflawed, would fail to prove the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). || 224 ||

body.translated_text: Therefore, since the unity-scriptures are contradicted by inferences that establish difference, they are intended as praise (<s>stuti</s>) of the eternality, pervasiveness, and such similarities of consciousness—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Therefore, the scriptures, overwhelmed by the force of logical reasons, [which affirm] duality of the selves,
abandoning even the primary meaning, offer praise (<s>nuti</s>) of consciousness. || 225 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover—

children.translated_text: Even perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) apprehends, in an indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) manner,
difference of an object [from others], in the form of exclusion from others—which does not [merely] arise [spontaneously]. || 226 ||
The [subsequent cognition] that arises, preceded by the recollection of name and other specifics,
is determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>), free from doubt, and devoid of error— || 227 ||
this cognition is called perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).
Here indeed, the determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>) cognition too, arising preceded by the recollection of specifics such as name, valid means, and the like,
is accepted as a valid means of knowledge in the form of perception, because it is free from doubt and uncontradicted. As they say: 'Then subsequently,

children.text: paraṃ punarvastu dharmairjātyādibhiryayā | buddhyā'vasīyate sā'pi pratyakṣatvena sammatā ||
children.translated_text: that cognition by which the object is ascertained through properties such as genus—that too is accepted as perception'

children.text: (ślo0 vā0 pratyakṣa0 120) iti | tatastādṛśaṃ pratyakṣajñānaṃ yena jāyamānenotpadyate,
children.translated_text: (<s>Ślokavārttika</s>, Pratyakṣa section, 120). Therefore, even the indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) cognition, by which such determinate perception arises,

children.text: tadapi nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ vastunaḥ parebhyo vyāvṛttarūpaṃ bhedaṃ gṛhṇātyeva, kāryasya
children.translated_text: also apprehends the difference of the object in the form of exclusion from others, because the effect
