inherits the qualities of its cause, and because the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine of the pre-existence of the effect) is accepted. || 226-227 ||

body.text:
tasya tu bhedagrāhitvānabhyupagame taduttarakālaṃ savikalpakajñānaṃ notpadyata 
ityāha-
body.translated_text: If one does not accept that [indeterminate cognition] apprehends difference, then the subsequent determinate cognition would not arise—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Otherwise it is not tenable.
For one who has not apprehended the difference of the object, [there can be no cognition] possessing the specific name and the like of that [object]. || 228 ||
But [the opponent says]: since difference is preceded by the apprehension of mutual absence, it cannot be grasped by perception, which has a positive object

children.text: nopapadyata ityuktam, tadayuktam, siddhe hi bhede'sāvitaretarābhāvaḥ | anyathā payo'rthī
children.translated_text: —thus it was said. That is wrong, for when difference is established, that mutual absence [follows automatically]. Otherwise, one desiring milk
would pursue fire—and everything would be incoherent. || 228 ||

body.translated_text: The fruitfulness of inference also [depends] on the apprehension of difference. With regard to the apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance)—

children.translated_text: since the apprehension of difference is absolutely necessary for the cognition of <s>vyāpti</s>, inference operates
only when that [difference] exists—this is the meaning.

children.text: vastusāmānyamātragrahaṇe tu tasya prāgeva siddhatvād dharmiviśeṣaṇasya
children.translated_text: But if only the universal aspect of a thing is apprehended, since that is already established beforehand, inference, which [should serve] to prove a specific property (<s>dharma-viśeṣa</s>)
of a particular subject (<s>dharmi-viśeṣaṇa</s>), would not operate—thus he says—
Because in [the case of apprehending only] the universal, there would be the proving of what is already proved. || 229 ||

body.translated_text: He states the proof of difference in yet another way—

children.translated_text: Moreover, if one accepts that non-duality and difference are mutually other,
then difference is established. But if non-difference [between them] is maintained, then too it is proved. || 230 ||
If the otherness of non-duality from duality is accepted, then the two realities characterized as duality and non-duality are [themselves] not established [as non-dual].
But if oneness is maintained even for the pair consisting of the non-dual and the differentiated—the two realities of duality and non-duality—then if so,

children.text: bhedasyaivādvaitasaṃjñā bhavadbhirucyata iti na vo nāmni vivādaḥ | yato'smābhirapyevaṃ
children.translated_text: you are simply calling difference itself by the name 'non-duality'; then we have no quarrel about names. For even by us,
difference alone is what is being proved. || 230 ||

body.text:
nanvekasyāṃ rajjau sarpādibhramavadekasyāmeva saṃvidi satyabhūtāyāmasatyabhūto 
vastubhedapratibhāsa ityuktam ? ata āha-
body.translated_text: But has it not been said that, just as in a single rope there is the illusion of a snake and the like, so in a single real consciousness there is the unreal appearance of difference of objects? To this he says—

children.translated_text: A mere example cannot establish the thesis; therefore,
the rope illustration serves only to confuse the student. || 231 ||
Since a mere example, without a probans and the other [inferential components], cannot prove the thesis; and since if the example itself is real, it contradicts non-duality,
while if the example is unreal, there would be the unwanted consequence that the consciousness that is the analogandum (<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>) would also be unreal—
the rope illustration is entirely pointless—this is the meaning. || 231 ||

body.translated_text: Moreover—

children.translated_text: Nor is the rope comparable to consciousness, because no distinguishing features are perceived [to negate the objective world].
Those entities that merely negate knowledge do not cause [consciousness] to transform. || 232 ||

body.text:
rajjvādau hi sarpādibhramāḥ samyagjñānodayānnivartante | tato bādhitatvāt 
sarpādyavabhāsastimirādidoṣakṛto'satya eva | ghaṭapaṭādyarthaprakāśasya tu 
kālāntaradeśāntarayorapi
body.translated_text: In the case of a rope and the like, the illusions of snake and so forth cease upon the arising of correct knowledge. Therefore, being sublated, the appearance of snake and the like is indeed unreal, produced by defects such as dim light. But the manifestation of objects such as pots and cloths, since even at other times and in other places

children.translated_text: no distinguishing [counter-evidence] is observed, and since they appear beyond mere knowledge [itself], being unsublated,

these real entities such as pots, cloths, and the like, serving as limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), when [consciousness] transforms together with them, [consciousness] itself also appears as differentiated—
the self-awareness (<s>ātma-saṃvid</s>) does not bear similarity to a rope. What is being said is this:

children.text: ghaṭapaṭādibāhyārthabhedaḥ satya eva, ātmasaṃvidastu tattadarthasannidhau tattadākārāropo
children.translated_text: The difference of external objects such as pots, cloths, and the like is indeed real. But the superimposition of various forms upon self-awareness in the presence of various objects

children.text: buddhyadhyavasāyabheda upādhikṛta iti | etaccottaratra prapañcayiṣyate | ataśca
children.translated_text: is a difference of intellectual determination (<s>buddhy-adhyavasāya</s>), caused by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>). And this will be elaborated upon later. Therefore,
even though the intellectual (<s>bauddha</s>) cognition of the nature of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), arising in the form of various objects
in the presence of various objects, undergoes repeated differentiation, the apprehending consciousness (<s>grāhaka-saṃvid</s>), which always appears in one and the same form

children.text: grāhakasaṃvido na rūpāntaraparāvṛttiḥ, api tu nityatvameva, cetanatvenāvikāritvāt |
children.translated_text: as the determiner of each [object], does not undergo transformation into another form; rather, it is eternal, being unchangeable on account of its conscious nature.
Therefore, the self-awarenesses are not one alone; for if they were one,
there would be the unwanted consequences of uniformity of experience, liberation [for all], and other defects—this has been stated by us elsewhere. || 232 ||

body.translated_text: And the illusion of multiplicity of this self-awareness, due to non-discrimination from intellectual determination, is caused by <s>mala</s> (impurity) alone, for bound souls (<s>paśu</s>)—thus he says—

children.translated_text: But that consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), not [truly] knowing [itself], appears to transform with those various entities,
like the moon for one whose vision-power is obstructed by <s>mala</s> (impurity), for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). || 233 ||

children.text: yathā timiraruddhacakṣuṣa eko'pīnduraneka iva pratibhāti, evaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as for one whose vision is obstructed by an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>), even a single moon appears as if many, so too
for one whose power of knowledge is obstructed by <s>mala</s>, the one consciousness of the nature of awareness appears to transform as if into many forms. || 233 ||

body.text:
yathā ca pramāṇāntarasiddhaikyasyāpīndoranekatvapratyayastimira-hetukaḥ, evaṃ 
śāstrādisiddhaikyasya gṛhītṛrūpasya jñānasyānekākāratā-bhramaḥ svakāraṇaṃ malaṃ 
gamayatītyāha-
body.translated_text: And just as the perception of multiplicity regarding the moon—whose unity is established by other valid means—is caused by the eye-disease, so too the illusion of manifold forms regarding knowledge, whose unity as the cognizing subject is established by scripture and the like, points to <s>mala</s> as its cause—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Just as one suffering from eye-disease (<s>timira</s>), even reasoning a thousand times,
sees the one moon as many, again and again, || 234 ||
or just as one whose tongue is afflicted by bile, even reasoning [that milk is] sweet,
perceives even milk as bitter, due to a defect of the sense organ, || 235 ||
or just as when water mixed with collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) is being boiled,
even for the learned, the cognitions of 'blue' and 'hot' [arise] due to non-discrimination, || 236 ||
so too, consciousness, though properly examined through scriptures supported by reasoning,
appearing to transform as 'born,' 'destroyed,' 'manifold,' || 237 ||
would indicate a cause [for this error]—namely the non-cessation of [false] knowledge—like an eye-disease and the like.

body.text:
sa ca malo dravyatvāccakṣuṣaḥ paṭalādiriva na jñānamātrānnivartate, api tu cakṣuṣo 
vaidyavyāpāreṇa paṭalādiriveśvaravyāpāreṇa dīkṣākhyenaiva nivartata ityāha-
body.translated_text: And that <s>mala</s>, being a substance like the cataract (<s>paṭala</s>) of the eye, is not removed by knowledge alone; rather, just as a cataract of the eye [is removed] by the procedure of a physician, it is removed only by the procedure of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) called <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation)—thus he says—

children.translated_text: That [<s>mala</s>] is removed by meditation on <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śiva-praṇidhāna</s>), and by the ritual || 238 ||
prescribed in the <s>Śiva-śāstra</s> alone, not otherwise by any number of knowledge [practices],
just as an eye-disease [is cured] only by the treatment prescribed in the medical treatise. || 239 ||
That <s>mala</s> is removed only by the ritual action called <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), prescribed in the <s>Śiva-śāstra</s>, assisted by meditation on <s>Śiva</s> as an ancillary [practice].

children.text: kriyayaiva nivartate | yaduktaṃ śrīmatsvāyaṃbhuve- dīkṣaiva mocayatyūrdhvaṃ śaivaṃ dhāma
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s>: '<s>Dīkṣā</s> alone liberates [the soul] and leads it upward
to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.' Here is the formal proof:

children.text: malo jñānānivartyo bhavati, ātmakaraṇācchādakatvāt, timiravat | paramārtho malaḥ,
children.translated_text: <s>Mala</s> is not removable by knowledge, because it is a veil over the self's faculties, like an eye-disease. <s>Mala</s> is ultimately real,
because it produces the causal efficacy of contamination, just as the impurity in the form of a glass-cataract produces illusion. || 238-239 ||

children.text: itthaṃ grāhakasaṃvido nityatvaprasaṅgānmalaṃ tannivṛttihetuṃ coktvā grāhyasya
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the eternality of the apprehending consciousness and the <s>mala</s> and its cause of cessation, he says that the difference of the apprehended world (<s>prapañca</s>) is real—
Even in different places, times, and persons, [the world] appears no differently [than as differentiated],

children.text: abādhitaḥ pramāṇaiśca vivartaḥ syāt kathaṃ citeḥ || 240 ||
children.translated_text: and being uncontradicted by valid means of knowledge—how could [it] be a mere apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of consciousness? || 240 ||
Moreover, the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>), belonging to the domain of <s>Māyā</s>, is established by valid means of knowledge alone.

body.translated_text: But it was said that the manifold appearance of consciousness is due to error alone—thus he says—

children.translated_text: Therefore, consciousness appears to transform only due to the bondage of the souls (<s>aṇus</s>). || 241 ||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very point—

children.translated_text: An apparent transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of the consciousness-power (<s>cit-śakti</s>) is indeed a false modification by which
even what is not of that nature is experienced as if it were of that nature. || 242 ||

body.translated_text: And that <s>vivarta</s> occurs for the selves due to the non-discrimination of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>)—thus he says—

children.translated_text: That [<s>vivarta</s>], pertaining to both the sentient (<s>cit</s>) and the insentient (<s>acit</s>) domains, mutually connected,
arises from non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>), since it is accomplished through mutual superimposition (<s>anyonyādhyāsa</s>). || 243 ||

body.translated_text: He explains this very point—

children.translated_text: There, consciousness (<s>cit</s>), due to non-discrimination from the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> connected with itself,
superimposing upon itself the modifications of that [<s>buddhi's</s>] functions, though itself unmodifiable, || 244 ||
following birth and the rest, displays itself to the soul (<s>aṇu</s>) as 'born,' 'destroyed,' 'manifold,'
'accompanied by pleasure,' 'accompanied by pain.' || 245 ||
Likewise, the insentient [body's quality] and the quality of consciousness are superimposed upon the self;
through non-discrimination, one knows 'I am thin' — therefore: ||246||
This non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) of all <s>aṇus</s> (souls) is caused by <s>mala</s> (impurity);
it is the root of the continuum dominated by delusion, [arising from the confusion] of conscious and insentient entities. ||247||
This <s>aviveka</s> (non-discrimination) of persons, which takes the form of apprehending the impermanent, impure, painful, and non-self as permanent, pure, pleasant, and self,

children.text: na nirhetukaḥ, muktasyā'pi prasaṅgāt | atastasya kenāpi kāraṇenā'nādinā bhavitavyam |
children.translated_text: is not without cause — for otherwise, it would apply even to the liberated. Therefore, there must be some beginningless cause for it.

children.text: avivekasyānādisiddhatvād yastasya hetuḥ, sa mala iti bhāvaḥ || 244-247 ||
children.translated_text: Since <s>aviveka</s> is established as beginningless, that which is its cause is <s>mala</s> (impurity) — this is the import. ||244-247||

body.translated_text: He states the reason for this very [point] —

children.translated_text: For it would not be possible that the particular transformations of particular cognitions
with particular insentient objects [could occur] without a firm bond. ||248||

And the underlying intention here is: it is only because the selves are covered by <s>mala</s> that the manifestation of knowledge and the like occurs only through the medium of <s>kalās</s> and the rest.
And that [manifestation], because <s>Māyā</s> is a deluder, takes the form of the superimposition of selfhood upon the non-self and the like. ||248||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on bondage as the cause —

children.text: tathā hi dehe'haṃbuddhirna loṣṭe sā'pi kasyacit |
children.translated_text: For instance, the notion of 'I' in the body — that does not exist in a clod of earth for anyone;
it belongs to the <s>aṇu</s> (soul) alone, not to all [entities]; therefore, bondage between those two is accepted. ||249||

children.text: tayościjjaḍayoranyonyaguṇādhyāse bandha eva niyāmaka iti śeṣaḥ || 249 ||
children.translated_text: In the mutual superimposition of qualities between those two — consciousness and the insentient — bondage alone is the determining factor, this is the remainder. ||249||

body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: The sense organs of knowledge and action that belong to a particular person,
those do not become the instruments of another; between those two, similarly: ||250||
A specific intellect alone is precluded [from serving] for the transformation of a specific consciousness;
not every intellect [serves] all [souls]; therefore, bondage between those two is accepted. ||251||

children.text: buddhyārūḍhaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ kiñcit kenacideva yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever pleasure and pain, having risen to the intellect,
is experienced by a particular person alone — by that [fact], bondage between those two is the determining factor. ||252||

children.text: ayamarthaḥ- ātmanāṃ hi saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ sarvaviṣayasya jñānādeḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: since, in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the knowledge of all objects

children.text: svarūpatvena śāstreṣu śrūyamāṇasyādarśanāt tadāvārakeṇa tāvanmalena bhāvyam |
children.translated_text: that is described in the scriptures as the true nature of the selves is not observed, there must be <s>mala</s> that conceals it.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca kiñcijjñatvadarśanāt kalādidvāreṇa tajjanakena mohahetutvād viparītapratipattihetunā
children.translated_text: And since limited knowledge is observed in them, there must be bondage called <s>Māyā</s>, which, as the cause of delusion and the cause of erroneous apprehension, generates [limited knowledge] through the medium of the <s>kalās</s> and the like.

children.text: māyākhyena bandhena bhāvyam | bhogasya sukhaduḥkhāderbhogasādhanānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: And since experience — consisting of pleasure, pain, and the like — and the instruments of experience —
the body and sense organs — are diverse, being confined to each individual self,
<s>karma</s> as the cause of this diversity must also necessarily be accepted. ||250-252||

children.text: atra sāṃkhyacchāyayā viveka evātra niyāmako'stu, kiṃ malākhyenāprasiddhena
children.translated_text: Here, following the Sāṃkhya school's position, one might object: let non-discrimination itself be the determining factor here;
why posit bondage of the <s>puruṣa</s> by an unfamiliar [entity] called <s>mala</s>? — he raises this objection —

body.translated_text: If non-discrimination is the controller —
He answers —
By what is that [non-discrimination] between those two caused?

children.text: tayorbuddhisaṃvidoranyonyāvivekaḥ kena kṛtaḥ | nirhetukatve muktasyāpi bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By what is the mutual non-discrimination between intellect and consciousness caused? If it were causeless, it would also apply to the liberated.

body.text:
tatastatkāraṇatayā'nādyāvārako malo'bhyupagantavyaḥ, yadabhāve muktasya na 
punaraviveko bhavati, tata eva ca bandhavimocakasyeśvarasyāpi siddhiruktetyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, as its cause, <s>mala</s>, the beginningless concealer, must be accepted; in whose absence the liberated do not again have non-discrimination; and from that very [fact], the existence of the Lord who releases from bondage is also established — he says —

children.translated_text: Therefore, bondage exists; and bondage is considered to be separate from the Lord. ||253||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: A soul abiding in bondage is deluded; <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is the release from that bondage.

children.text: galite sarvathā bandhe vimukte cāṇave male || 254 ||
children.translated_text: When bondage has completely fallen away, and when the <s>āṇava-mala</s> (innate impurity) has been released, ||254||
the power that illuminates all things manifests, belonging to <s>Śiva</s> alone.
And bondage and liberation are from the grace of <s>Śiva</s> alone — this has been stated. ||254||
This great power, freed from all veils, ||255||

children.text: alpīyāṃsaṃ samāvṛtya viṣayaṃ sā tu darśayet |
children.translated_text: covering a lesser domain, reveals [only that much].

body.translated_text: How does it reveal? — to this he says —

children.translated_text: When there is no bondage for the <s>śakti</s> (power) whose nature is supreme consciousness, ||256||
only the mere existence of the supreme would shine forth for liberated <s>aṇus</s> (souls), unceasingly.

children.text: malarahitatvena svaparaprakāśikāyā muktātmasaṃvidaḥ paramātraṃ parasya vastunaḥ
children.translated_text: For the consciousness of the liberated self, which illuminates both itself and others due to being free from <s>mala</s>, only the mere existence of the supreme object

children.text: sattāmātraṃ prakāśate, na tu baddhātmavadasya viśeṣena bhogyatayā prakāśata ityarthaḥ,
children.translated_text: would shine forth, but not — as for the bound self — shine forth specifically as something to be enjoyed. This is the meaning,
for if it were so, even the liberated would have the undesirable consequence of being experiencers through the perception of pleasure, pain, and the like. ||256||

children.text: ato vimuktāḥ sarvajñā na tu cinmātravedinaḥ || 257 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the liberated are omniscient, not mere knowers of pure consciousness. ||257||

children.text: na tu svasaṃvedanamātraniṣṭhāḥ, api tu śivavat sarvajñā eveti || 257 ||
children.translated_text: Not established merely in self-awareness, but rather omniscient like <s>Śiva</s> — this is [the meaning]. ||257||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

body.text: sati bāhye tadajñānaṃ vastuni syāt tamaḥkṛtam |
body.translated_text: Even when an external object exists, ignorance of it would be caused by darkness (<s>tamas</s>).

body.text:
bāhye ca vastuni satyapi yadetadviṣayājñānamātraṃ baddhātmanāṃ dṛśyate, 
tanmalakṛtameva | tataśca asarvajñā na muktā ityāha-
body.translated_text: Even though external objects exist, the mere ignorance regarding them that is observed in bound souls is caused by <s>mala</s> alone. Therefore, those who are not omniscient are not liberated — he says —

children.text: tamasācchādyamānā hi na te muktā bhavanti ca || 258 ||
children.translated_text: For those who are veiled by darkness — they are not liberated. ||258||

body.translated_text: And the dependence [of knowledge] on the pervading of <s>śabda</s> (word) is the cause of bondage for <s>savikalpaka-jñāna</s> (determinate knowledge) — he says —

children.translated_text: <s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) arises from the agitation of <s>Bindu</s>, through the pervading of <s>śabda</s> in the cognitions
of <s>aṇus</s> (souls) obstructed by <s>mala</s>, in the perception of objects. ||259||
For those free from <s>mala</s>, since <s>Bindu</s> is not agitated, [there arises] cognition of objects that is <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual),
born of the release from that bondage — like a child born that very day. ||260||
For the liberated, since they have transcended the <s>Māyā</s>-based bondage of <s>Bindu</s>, the intellectual <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate)

children.text: savikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ na bhavet, kintu cicchaktirevānyānapekṣiṇī grāhyaṃ vastu viṣayīkaroti |
children.translated_text: knowledge assisted by the pervading of <s>śabda</s> does not arise; rather, the power of consciousness (<s>cit-śakti</s>) itself, independently, makes the object to be grasped its content.
The simile 'like a child born that very day' should be understood as illustrating only the absence of conceptual constructions such as <s>śabda</s>. ||259-260||

body.text:
vastuno bālasyāpi malāvṛtatvena vastūnāṃ yathāsvarūpānavabodhāt, muktānāṃ tu 
malarahitatvāt tacchaktiḥ samastaṃ vastu yathāvasthitameva gṛhṇātītyāha-
body.translated_text: Even for a child, due to being covered by <s>mala</s>, there is no apprehension of objects as they truly are; but for the liberated, being free from <s>mala</s>, that power grasps all objects just as they are — he says —

children.text: yo yadā vartate bhāvo bhūto bhāvi ca tat tadā |
children.translated_text: Whatever entity exists at whatever time — past, future, or present —
the imperishable consciousness, self-cognizing, grasps it according to the true state of that object. ||261||
As stated in the <s>Mokṣakārikā</s>: 'By the rays of <s>Śiva</s>'s power, with the vision of consciousness made capable,
the self, freed from obstruction, sees <s>Śiva</s> together with <s>Śakti</s> and the rest.' (verse 111) ||261||

body.translated_text: And even though omniscience and universal agency are possible for them, they do not act — he says —

body.text: na te viśvasya kartāraḥ kartā'sya śiva eva yat |
body.translated_text: They are not the creators of the universe, for <s>Śiva</s> alone is its creator.
Why? — to this he says —

children.translated_text: For there is nowhere any evidence for a multiplicity of agents. ||262||
For even in the case of chariots and the like, which have multiple makers, their production is never seen without following the will of one chief architect.

children.text: yaduktam- bahavo yatra netāraḥ sarve paṇḍitamāninaḥ | sarve mahattvamicchanti
children.translated_text: As it has been said: 'Where there are many leaders, all considering themselves wise, all desiring greatness,

children.text: tadvyaktamavasīdati || iti | anena pravāheśvarapakṣo'pi nirastaḥ, aiśvaryasya
children.translated_text: that undertaking clearly perishes.' By this, the view of a stream-lord (<s>pravāheśvara</s>) is also refuted, since lordship,

children.text: svarūpavyaktilābhātma-katvena vināśayogāt | tatastena nityamuktena śivenaiva kāryasya
children.translated_text: being of the nature of attaining the manifestation of one's true nature, is subject to destruction. Therefore, since the work is accomplished only by that eternally liberated <s>Śiva</s>,
and because [the liberated souls] are free from attachment, aversion, and the like, they do not act. ||262||

body.translated_text: He shows this very [point] —

children.translated_text: The eternally liberated, ever-risen, inconceivable power called <s>Śakti</s>,
the consciousness, perpetually rests upon <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause. ||263||

children.text: sa tayā jaḍamākramya sṛjatyavati hanti ca |
children.translated_text: With that [Śakti], pervading the insentient [world], he creates, preserves, and destroys;
the Lord conceals and also bestows grace upon the selves. ||264||

children.text: anena śaktivicāropasaṃhāreṇa tadāśrayabhūtasya śivasya vicāropakṣepo'pi kṛto
children.translated_text: By this conclusion of the investigation of <s>Śakti</s>, it should be understood that an introduction to the investigation of <s>Śiva</s>, who is the basis of that [Śakti], has also been made.

children.text: veditavyaḥ | tathāhi jagataḥ sanniveśādimattvena kāryatvāt tatkartṛtayā''tmanāṃ ca
children.translated_text: For indeed, since the universe, having orderly arrangement and the like, is an effect, <s>Śiva</s> is established as its maker; and since

children.text: malāvṛtatvāt tanmokṣakartṛtvena ca śivaḥ siddha eva | yaduktam- vivādādhyāsitaṃ viśvaṃ
children.translated_text: the selves are covered by <s>mala</s>, [Śiva] is established as the agent of their liberation. As it has been said: 'The universe, the subject of dispute,

children.text: viśvavitkartṛpūrvakam | kāryatvādāvayoḥ siddhaṃ kāryaṃ kumbhādikaṃ yathā || iti |
children.translated_text: must have an omniscient maker — being an effect, as established for both of us, like a pot and the like.'

body.translated_text: Now he states the [apparent] divisions [of Śiva] through the distinction of his functions (<s>kṛtya</s>) by way of figurative usage —
As the agent of those functions, he, though three[-fold], is indicated as five.
How? — to this he says —

children.translated_text: 'Endowed with power' (<s>śaktimān</s>), 'with effort aroused' (<s>udyukta</s>), and 'engaged' (<s>pravṛtta</s>) — thus by the teachers. ||265||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on this —

children.translated_text: Among these, the first is the potent one, without parts, designated as <s>Śiva</s>.
In him, the lordly power called <s>kriyā</s> (action) rests as if in a bud. ||266||
To show that, since <s>Śakti</s> is one, the distinction of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>kriyā</s> (action) is merely due to limiting adjuncts,
and since <s>jñāna</s> is invariably of the nature of <s>kriyā</s>, <s>Śakti</s> is designated by the word '<s>kriyā</s>.' When that <s>Śakti</s>, with all functions withdrawn,

children.text: svarūpamātrāvasthāne sati śivaḥ śaktādiśabdavācyo bhavati | saiva tasya
children.translated_text: rests in the state of mere essential nature, <s>Śiva</s> is denoted by the words '<s>śakta</s>' (potent) and the like. This is called
the dissolution state (<s>laya-avasthā</s>) of him who presides over <s>Para-bindu</s> (supreme seed-point). ||266||

body.translated_text: Now, in the state of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), he is denoted by the word '<s>udyukta</s>' (aroused) and the like — he says —

children.translated_text: That very [Śakti], beginning to unfold, heavy with the burden of <s>Bindu</s>'s embryo,
manifests to the Lord the uninterrupted flow of supreme bliss. ||267||

children.text: sā ca śaktirudyogena bindoḥ kāryasya prasavābhimukhyaṃ kurvāṇā yadā patyuḥ
children.translated_text: And that <s>Śakti</s>, through her effort directing <s>Bindu</s> toward the production of effects, when she

children.text: paramānandasantatiṃ jñānakriyāsamṛddhiṃ kāryotpādanenā''viṣkaroti, tadā tasya śivasya
children.translated_text: manifests to the Lord the flow of supreme bliss — the fullness of knowledge and action through the production of effects — then for that <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: bhogaḥ pālanātmako bhavatīti bhāvaḥ | na tu śivasya paramānandaḥ sukhātiśayo bhogaśca
children.translated_text: the state of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), consisting of preservation, occurs — this is the import. But <s>Śiva</s>'s supreme bliss should not be interpreted as an excess of pleasure, nor the enjoyment
as the experience of pleasure, because, due to his purity, those two — which would be limiting adjuncts — are not possible for <s>Śiva</s>. ||267||

body.text: tadānīṃ codyuktayā śaktyā sahā'yamudyuktādiśabdavācyaḥ prakāśata ityāha-
body.translated_text: At that time, together with the aroused <s>Śakti</s>, he is denoted by the words '<s>udyukta</s>' and the like — he says —

children.text: sa tayā ramate nityaṃ samudyuktaḥ sadāśivaḥ |
children.translated_text: With her he ever delights, fully aroused — <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
the glorious Lord whose body consists of the five <s>mantras</s>, both <s>sakala</s> (with parts) and <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts). ||268||

children.text: ataśca kāryopādhibhinnā īśānādipañcamantrātmikāḥ śaktaya eva tanukāryaṃ
children.translated_text: And therefore, the <s>śaktis</s> differentiated by the limiting adjuncts of effects, being of the nature of the five <s>mantras</s> — <s>Īśāna</s> and the rest —

children.text: kurvāṇāḥ śivasya tanurucyante, na tu pāramārthiketi bhāvaḥ | taduktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendre-
children.translated_text: are called the 'body' of <s>Śiva</s> as they perform the function of embodiment, not in the ultimate sense — this is the import. As stated in the glorious <s>Mṛgendra</s> [Āgama] —
'His body, through the five <s>mantras</s> employed for the five functions — <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, and <s>Aja</s> — [constitutes] the head and the rest.'
(vidyā 3.8-9). Therefore, the mention of form in the <s>Āgamas</s> is only for the purpose of meditation — as stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s> [Āgama] —

children.text: sādhakasya tu lakṣyārthaṃ tasya rūpamidaṃ smṛtam iti | atra ca śivaśaktyorlayādibhedasya
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of visualization by the practitioner, this form of his is taught.' And here, since the distinction of dissolution and other states of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is caused by the different states of <s>Bindu</s>,

children.text: bindvavasthābhedakṛtatvāt tasya ca śāntyatītakalārūpasya layāvasthātvena śruteḥ
children.translated_text: and since that [Bindu], being of the nature of the <s>Śāntyatītā-kalā</s>, is described as the dissolution state,
the substrate of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) is in the form of the transformation of the four <s>kalās</s> from <s>Śānti</s> onward. Through presiding over that,

children.text: bhogaḥ procyata ityuktaṃ śrīmanmataṅge- caturmūrtimayaṃ śubhraṃ yattatsakalaniṣkalam |
children.translated_text: the enjoyment of <s>Śiva</s> is also declared — as stated in the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> [Āgama]: 'That which consists of four forms, pure, both <s>sakala</s> and <s>niṣkala</s> —

children.text: tasmin bhogaḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ patyurviśvasya sarvadā || (vi0 3|34) iti | yadyevaṃ
children.translated_text: in that, the enjoyment of the Lord of the universe is always indicated.' (vidyā 3.34). If so,

children.text: sadāśivabhuvanādhiṣṭhāna eva devasya sadāśivatvāt tasyaiva pañcamantrarūpatvāt
children.translated_text: since the Lord's nature as <s>Sadāśiva</s> [resides] only in the <s>Sadāśiva-bhuvana</s> (world), and since it is that very [form] which has the nature of five <s>mantras</s>,
how is it described here in the state of enjoyment? It is stated thus because, in the <s>Nivṛtti</s> and other worlds, <s>Śiva</s> is to be meditated upon
merely in the form of the <s>Sadyojāta</s> and other <s>mantras</s>. The collective form of the five <s>mantras</s>

children.text: mūrtistasyādhikārāvasthasya pravṛttasya sadāśivabhuvana eveti vakṣyati- sa bindoḥ (ślo0 279)
children.translated_text: as his embodied form in the state of authority, of him who is engaged, is in the <s>Sadāśiva-bhuvana</s> alone — as will be stated [beginning with] 'He, of <s>Bindu</s>' (verse 279).

children.text: ityādinā | eṣo'rthaśca śrīmanmataṅge vistareṇa darśita iti tata evāvadhārayitavyaḥ || 268 ||
children.translated_text: And this meaning has been shown in detail in the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> [Āgama]; therefore, it should be ascertained from there. ||268||

body.translated_text: Now he states the <s>mantra</s>-nature of <s>Śakti</s> —

children.translated_text: Through reflecting (<s>manana</s>) on all entities, and through protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
that <s>Śakti</s> of his is in the form of <s>mantra</s>, possessing the properties of reflection and protection. ||269||
As it has been said: 'Reflection (<s>manana</s>) is omniscience; protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) is the grace toward those in <s>saṃsāra</s>;
because of possessing the properties of reflection and protection, it is called <s>mantra</s>.'

children.text: eṣā ca vyutpattiḥ śivasya śaktervidyeśvarādīnāṃ ca samānaiva, ataśca
children.translated_text: And this etymology applies equally to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>, and the rest; therefore,
the use of the word '<s>mantra</s>' for the signifying words is by way of figurative usage. ||269||

body.translated_text: And its division is only through limiting adjuncts — he says —

children.translated_text: Through the differentiation of effects and depending on the substrates, that one [Śakti] alone [appears] as five,
shining with <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, and the rest as the five domains to be presided over. ||270||

body.text:
binduśāntyādibhuvanādhiṣṭhānādasya īśānādibheda ityuktaṃ prāgeva | etadeva 
prapañcayati-
body.translated_text: The division [of Śiva] into <s>Īśāna</s> and the rest is due to presiding over the worlds of <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, and the rest — this has been stated previously. He elaborates on this —

children.text: binduḥ śāntiḥ kalā vidyā pratiṣṭhā sanivṛttikā |
children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s>, <s>śānti</s>, <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>pratiṣṭhā</s>, together with <s>nivṛtti</s> —
the places of enjoyment of these five; the name '<s>bindu</s>' is pronounced by <s>Śiva</s>. ||271||

Objection: Was it not said that only the four [sets of] worlds — <s>śānti</s> and the rest — are places of enjoyment? True, but even though the <s>parabindu</s>, which has the form of <s>śāntyatīta</s>,
exists in the state of dissolution, at the very beginning of creation the worlds belonging to it arise; therefore it too is included here
as a place of enjoyment — thus there is no contradiction. ||271||

body.text: ata evāsāṃ bindukalānāṃ kāraṇāvasthāyāṃ layarūpatvena parabindusaṃjñetyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, since these <s>bindu-kalās</s> have the form of dissolution in their causal state, they bear the name <s>parabindu</s> — he says:

children.translated_text: This undivided [state] of the five <s>kalās</s> is designated <s>bindu</s>;
the supreme form (<s>parā mūrti</s>) pertains to that [bindu]; the lower form pertains to effects. ||272||

children.text: parā mūrtirbindvadhiṣṭhātrī layāvasthā śaktiḥ, kāryādhiṣṭhātrī tvaparā śivasya
children.translated_text: The supreme form is the <s>Śakti</s> presiding over the state of dissolution, which is the <s>bindu</s>; but the lower form is <s>Śiva</s>'s
form that presides over effects — this is the meaning. ||272||

body.translated_text: And thus —

children.text: yā tasya vimalā śaktiḥ śivasya samavāyinī |
children.translated_text: That pure <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, which is inherent in him —
she herself is his form; due to the differentiation of action, she is called the body named <s>Sadā</s> (eternal). ||273||
The inherent <s>Śakti</s> herself, through the transformation of <s>bindu</s>, by presiding over
the <s>Sadāśiva-bhuvana</s> (world) that is below the <s>nivṛtti-bhuvanas</s>, and thus exercising authority, is figuratively called
the body named <s>Sadāśiva</s> — this is the meaning. ||273||

body.text:
dīkṣādinā tattadbhuvanaprāptānāṃ satya eva bhedaḥ, tadadhiṣṭhātryostu śivaśaktyoḥ 
kāryabhedād bheda ityuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: The differentiation of those who have attained their respective worlds through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and so forth is real; but the differentiation of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, who preside over them, is due to differentiation of effects — having stated this, he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, pervaded by the mighty <s>Śiva</s>,
for the pure souls of <s>Śiva</s>'s nature who are established in the places of enjoyment — ||274||
whatever bodies, enjoyments, faculties, abodes, knowledge, and so forth she creates —
that is her effect; she is the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action), and she is also called thus. ||275||

body.text:
śivaśaktikṣobhitā mahāmāyā yadyat kāryamutpādayati, tatra tadadhiṣṭhātryoḥ 
śivaśaktyoḥ kāryabhedena sthānabhedenopacārāt tattatsaṃjñā bhavati | yathā 
śāntibhuvanādhiṣṭhānena
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, agitated by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, whatever effect she produces — therein, <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, who preside over that, through differentiation of effects and figuratively through differentiation of stations, receive their respective names. Just as

children.text: tadutpāde ca śaktirapi śāntisaṃjñā, śivaśca śāntasaṃjñaḥ | ityevamanyatrāpi draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: when presiding over the <s>śānti-bhuvana</s> and producing it, <s>Śakti</s> too is called <s>Śānti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> is called <s>Śānta</s> — thus it should be understood for other [stations] as well.

children.text: | taduktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendre- kintu yaḥ patibhedo'smin sa śāstre śaktibhedavat |
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Mṛgendra</s>: 'But the differentiation of the Lord in this [system], like the differentiation of <s>Śakti</s>,
is figurative, through differentiation of functions and differentiation of stations.' (Vidyāpāda 13.164-165) ||274-275||

body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point] —

children.translated_text: The <s>Śakti</s> of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śūlin</s>) is indeed one, having the nature of all knowledge and action;
from which arise will, knowledge, action, and other states, which are the sources of effects. ||276||

children.text: yatprabhavā yadīyā icchājñānādyā avasthāḥ kāryayonayaḥ, kāryopādhikṛtā
children.translated_text: 'From which arise' means: the states of will, knowledge, and so forth, which are the sources of effects, are conditioned by effects —
this is the meaning. ||276||

body.text:
itthaṃ śaktireva śivasya mūrtistatkāryaviṣayetyuktam, idānīṃ 
bhogādhikāratattvavāsināmuktavad baindavānyeva śarīrādīnītyāha-
body.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that <s>Śakti</s> alone is <s>Śiva</s>'s form with respect to effects. Now he says that the bodies and so forth of those dwelling in the <s>tattvas</s> of enjoyment and authority are indeed of <s>bindu</s> —

children.translated_text: For <s>Īśvaras</s> (lords) and <s>Śivas</s>, their bodies, faculties, and so forth
are made of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, pure, auspicious, and appropriate to their respective domains of authority. ||277||

body.translated_text: And the agent of those [effects] —

children.translated_text: This <s>Śakti</s>, having the nature of action, is inseparable from <s>Śiva</s>;
through her connection with him, <s>Śiva</s> is said to be the cause of all effects. ||278||

body.translated_text: The state of authority is described —

children.translated_text: He, descending from <s>bindu</s>, enveloped by the atomic <s>Sadāśiva</s> [form],
dispatching <s>Sadāśivas</s> and <s>Maheśvaras</s> to the offices of lordly functions — ||279||
the Lord shines at the summit of all paths.
The 'descent' here means becoming active by abandoning the state of latent readiness; and 'activity' means empowering
the <s>Sadāśivas</s> and <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> to be initiated and appointed in sequence to the enjoyment of their respective worlds and to authority over the impure path.

children.text: niyojanam | ata eva prabhavanaśīlo'śeṣādhvādhiṣṭhātā bhrājate sadāśivākāreṇa
children.translated_text: Therefore, being of commanding nature, the presider over all paths shines forth in the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
attaining the status of being the object of meditation — this is the meaning. ||279||

body.translated_text: He shows the form of meditation and the presiding station —

children.translated_text: The Lord, having five streams as faces, peaceful, with <s>Śakti</s> as his head — <s>Śiva</s>; ||280||
with large eyes [representing] seeing, action, and will; endowed with the crescent moon of <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge);
with <s>Īśāna</s> as the crown, <s>Puruṣa</s> as the face, with a circle of arms [extending to] the ten directions; ||281||
<s>Aghora</s> as the heart, <s>Vāma</s> as the secret [part], radiant with a body born [of the five mantras];
this God, being active, complete (<s>sakala</s>), all-purifying. ||282||

children.text: atra ca pañcasrotaśśabdena mananatrāṇarūpāyāḥ śakteḥ pañcāvasthābhedā
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'five-streamed,' the five states of <s>Śakti</s>, whose nature is reflection and protection,
are spoken of. ||280-282||

body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the unity of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> despite the differentiation of <s>bindu</s>'s stations of presiding, he concludes —

children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is indeed one; likewise, <s>Śakti</s> too is without modification;
in the [three states of] dissolution, enjoyment, and authority, those two are of the nature of pure consciousness alone. ||283||

body.text:
idānīmanekatvamevaupacārikametayoḥ prakārāntareṇa darśayituṃ 
tattadavasthābhājāmātmanāṃ vāstavaṃ bhedamāha-
body.translated_text: Now, to show by another method that the multiplicity of these two is merely figurative, he states the real differentiation of souls who partake of the respective states —

children.translated_text: Indeed, in the pure, noble, and deep ocean of consciousness,
some, established by him, dissolve in their own Self. ||284||
Certain souls whose <s>mala</s> (impurity) has matured, being established by that <s>Śiva</s> as the gracious one — i.e., liberated by his power of grace —
dissolve in, i.e., abide in, their own essential nature, which has the form of a most pure, unsurpassed ocean of omniscience and omnipotence;

children.text: tiṣṭhanti, tadanugrahāt tatsāmyarūpaṃ mokṣaṃ bhajantītyarthaḥ | na tu śivātmanyaikyaṃ te
children.translated_text: through his grace, they attain <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) in the form of equality with him — this is the meaning. But it should not be interpreted as their merging into identity with <s>Śiva</s>'s self,

children.text: prayāntīti vyākhyeyam, advaitasya prāgeva niṣedhāt | ete ca
children.translated_text: since non-duality (<s>advaita</s>) has already been refuted. And these
are said to partake of the dissolution state, since they are equal to <s>Śiva</s> in the dissolution state. ||284||
The <s>vijñānakevalins</s> (pure knowers) too, since their <s>mala</s> has not matured, having transcended <s>Māyā</s>, taking shelter in <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, and being without enjoyment,
are said to partake of the dissolution state due to their inactivity — he says:

body.translated_text: Others, their powers restrained by <s>Śiva</s>, repose [in dissolution].
He describes those who partake of the enjoyment state —

children.translated_text: Others, embracing <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, which is active — ||285||
their minds focused solely on the bliss of contact with her, intent on enjoyment.
The meaning is: taking shelter in <s>Mahāmāyā</s> transformed into the form of worlds — <s>śānti</s> and others — they abide. ||285||
He also describes those who partake of the authority state —
Likewise, others, taking shelter in the supreme sky (<s>paravyoman</s>), at the summit of the paths, ||286||
perform the five functions, following the command of the Lord.
<s>Ananta</s> and others, taking shelter in the worlds of <s>Mahāmāyā</s> at the summit of the pure path, the supreme sky,
become performers of the five functions by <s>Śiva</s>'s command — this has been stated. ||286||
Therefore, he, though being one among those who partake of dissolution, enjoyment, and authority, ||287||
assumes figurative differentiation through the role of presider.
Similarly, <s>Śakti</s> is regarded [as one]; the differentiation of those two is now explained. ||288||
The mutual differentiation of those two — <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — is stated. ||287-288||

body.translated_text: He states that very differentiation —

children.translated_text: In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is the agent; <s>Śakti</s>, the instrument, is the one relied upon.
He should be known as the support [of all], self-established, of dense consciousness. ||289||
The differentiation of these two is precisely as property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). ||289||

body.text:
tatra ca dharmisvarūpaṃ jñānaṃ svaniṣṭhameva, viṣayagrahaṇasāmarthyarūpaṃ tu 
dharmatayocyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: And therein, the nature of the property-bearer, i.e., knowledge, is self-established; but the capacity for grasping objects is called the property — he says:

children.translated_text: She is <s>Saṃvid</s> (awareness), whose arising is [characterized by] eagerness in the apprehension of all objects;
and she is of the nature of supreme sovereignty (<s>mahimā</s>), having the form of pervasion. ||290||

body.translated_text: And therefore —
This great <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), the pervader of all objects, [is known] through those two [aspects].

children.translated_text: Due to being endowed with the capacity to pervade all objects, <s>Śiva</s> is the pervader of all meanings. He clarifies the stated meaning — 'through those two.'
That form of knowledge which is independent of anything external — that is designated <s>Śiva</s>. ||291||
The wise declare his <s>Śakti</s> to be the form that depends on the external.
'Depending on the external' means: depending on objects — this is the meaning. ||291||

body.text: kuta evaṃ kalpyata iti cedata āha-
body.translated_text: 'Why is it conceived thus?' — to this he answers:

children.translated_text: The awareness of every entity whatsoever has two aspects — ||292||
through that which depends on the external and that which is independent: <s>Śakti</s> exists, having <s>Śiva</s> as her ground.
In the domain of the inert: from observing that fire, which can burn, has the capacity to burn in the proximity of something combustible,

children.text: tadanabhivyakteḥ, cidviṣaye ca ātmani viṣayagrahaṇarūpasya svaniṣṭhasya grahītṛsvarūpasya
children.translated_text: and otherwise that [capacity] remains unmanifest; and in the domain of consciousness: since the self-established nature of the grasper, which is the form of grasping objects,
is established through self-awareness — this [dual nature] is proven. Therefore, <s>Śakti</s> exists. ||292||

body.translated_text: If so, what is the distinction between this <s>Śakti</s> of the self and this <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>? — to this he answers:

children.translated_text: For <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), whose glory is eternally manifest and unlimited, ||293||
with respect to objects to be known, things to be presided over, effects to be produced, and so on — nothing other [than <s>Śakti</s>], such as auxiliary causes, [is needed].
Therefore, <s>Śakti</s> — the form that depends on the external — befits the Lord. ||294||

body.text:
nityamuktvādīśvarasya jñeyādiviṣaye śaktivyatirekeṇa na buddhyādikaraṇāpekṣā, 
ālokādisahakāryapekṣā ca | ataḥ śaktireva tasya parāpekṣārūpaṃ nānyat | 
baddhātmanāṃ tu śaktyākhyaṃ viṣayāpekṣaṃ svarūpamātramevāsau kāryādiheturna 
bhavet, teṣāṃ kāryādau karaṇādyapekṣādarśanādityāha-
body.translated_text: For <s>Īśvara</s>, who is eternally liberated, with respect to objects to be known and so on, there is no dependence on instruments like <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) apart from <s>Śakti</s>, nor dependence on auxiliaries like light. Therefore, <s>Śakti</s> alone is his externally-dependent form, nothing else. But for bound souls, the form called <s>Śakti</s>, which depends on objects, is merely their essential nature and cannot be the cause of effects, since for them dependence on instruments and so on is observed in [producing] effects — he says:

children.translated_text: The externally-dependent form alone is not sufficient for everyone [to produce effects];
since effects such as sons and the like are observed [to arise] only otherwise [i.e., through instruments]. ||295||

children.text: śivasyeti pāṭhe kevalasya śambhorjñānaṃ na svarūpamātraniṣṭhameva, kintu
children.translated_text: In the reading '<s>Śivasya</s>' — the knowledge of <s>Śambhu</s> alone is not confined merely to his essential nature, but

children.text: viṣayāpekṣameva kāryādihetuḥ | na tu baddhātmanāṃ dṛṣṭakāryāṇāṃ putrādīnāṃ
children.translated_text: being object-dependent, it is the cause of effects. But for bound souls, of observed effects like sons and so on,
the arising through knowledge and so on that depends on objects, the father, and other [factors] is observed — this is the meaning. ||295||

body.text: ato neśvarasyāpi nirviṣayaṃ grahaṇātmakaṃ jñānaṃ saṃbhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: Therefore, even for <s>Īśvara</s>, knowledge having the nature of apprehension cannot be without objects — he says:

body.text: na tu nirviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tadeva viṣayagrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: Knowledge is never without an object; it is indeed the grasping of objects.

body.text:
yadyevaṃ viṣayasannidhāna eva grahaṇarūpasyotpattidarśanād 
dharmasvarūpasyānityatvaprasaṅgaḥ ? tanna, śivasya sarvadā bindvādernityasya viṣayasya 
grāhyatvāt, grahaṇasāmarthyasya grahītṛsamavetatvena sarvadā'vasthānācca |
body.translated_text: If so, since the arising of the grasping-form [of knowledge] is observed only in the proximity of objects, there would be the undesirable consequence of the impermanence of the property-nature? No, because for <s>Śiva</s>, <s>bindu</s> and the rest — which are eternal — always exist as objects to be grasped, and because the capacity for grasping, being inherent in the grasper, always persists.

body.text:
nanvātmanāṃ nīlādijñānavināśena pītādijñānasya krameṇotpattidarśanāt 
tatsāmarthyasyāpyanityatvaṃ lakṣyate ? ata āha-
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the destruction of knowledge of blue and the like and the sequential arising of knowledge of yellow and so on is observed in [ordinary] souls, the impermanence of that capacity too is inferred? To this he answers:

children.translated_text: Whether through opposition or in sequence — even so, that which is imperishable — ||296||
this is the characteristic of perishable [cognitions]: that which does not arise otherwise at that time.
Since intellectual (<s>bauddha</s>) knowledge — in the form of determination of yellow, which is different from the determination of blue and so on —
is perishable and mutually contradictory, even when arising in sequence, the capacity to grasp cognitions of pleasure and the like,
being always inherent in the grasper, is known [through self-awareness] to be imperishable. Therefore, it is only the intellectual [cognition] that undergoes otherwise —
i.e., transformation. ||296||

body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: That which is imperishable is eternal — this is accepted; from this, it differs. ||297||
<s>Śakti</s> belongs to <s>Śambhu</s> by way of substrate; and he to her — likewise.
That capacity of the self too, like <s>Śiva</s>'s capacity, must be accepted as eternal. And thus,

children.text: śivaśaktyorātmabhedābhāve'pi dharmidharmabhedaḥ satya evetyāha- asmāditi | tatastasmāt
children.translated_text: even though there is no real difference between <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, the differentiation of property-bearer and property is indeed real — he says: 'from this.' 'Likewise' means: from that
reason, <s>Śakti</s> is indeed of the nature of a property — this is the meaning. ||297||

body.translated_text: Here is an objection from the opponent —

children.translated_text: The designation '<s>Śakti</s>' may apply to the dense consciousness [i.e., <s>Śiva</s> himself] due to the conditioning adjunct of effects; ||298||

children.text: na tu śaktiḥ parāpekṣā vastuto'stīti kecana |
children.translated_text: but <s>Śakti</s> as externally-dependent does not truly exist — so say some.
The meaning is: only the property-bearer form is ultimately real, not the property form. ||298||

body.translated_text: The reply to this —

children.text: karaṇena vinā kāryaṃ kurvan kartā bhavediti || 299 ||
children.translated_text: That an agent could produce effects without an instrument — ||299||
this view of theirs is unjustified, being contradicted by both reasoning and direct perception.

children.text: kulālādīnāṃ hi kartṛṇāṃ karaṇena vinā kartṛtvādarśanāt śivasyā'pi kartṛtvāt
children.translated_text: For since agency without an instrument is not observed even for agents like potters, and since <s>Śiva</s> too is an agent,

children.text: kenāpi karaṇena bhavitavyam | tacchaktyātmakameva | yaduktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendre- karaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: there must be some instrument [for him]; and that is of the nature of <s>Śakti</s> itself. As stated in the venerable <s>Mṛgendra</s>: 'The instrument is none other than <s>Śakti</s>'

children.text: na śaktyanyat (vi0 3|4) iti | evamātmanāmapi dehaspandādau śaktireva karaṇamityuktam || 299 ||
children.translated_text: (Vidyāpāda 3.4). Thus for ordinary souls too, <s>Śakti</s> alone is the instrument in bodily movement and so on — this has been stated. ||299||

body.text:
kiñca, grahaṇarūpasya paramārthasyānabhyupagame 
sthitikāle'pyupādhibhūtasadāśivatattvādibindukāryaviṣayīkaraṇā-bhāvādasya 
sadāśivādibhedakalpanamayuktam | upādhyagrahaṇe'pyetadbhedopacārābhyupagame 
sarvadaivādhikārāvasthā bhavet, na tu layāvasthā, viśeṣābhāvādityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the apprehension which constitutes the ultimate reality is not accepted, then even during the period of cosmic maintenance, since [Śiva] would not have as His object the effects of <s>Bindu</s> such as <s>Sadāśiva</s> <s>tattva</s> etc. that serve as limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>), the imagining of [Śiva's] distinctions as <s>Sadāśiva</s> etc. would be unjustified. And even if the non-apprehension of the limiting conditions is accepted, if one accepts this figurative distinction, there would always be only the state of active governance, never a state of dissolution, since there would be no distinguishing factor—he says—

children.translated_text: Moreover, even if unapprehended, if the effect [of Bindu] is the limiting condition of the Lord, || 300 ||
since He would always be in a conditioned state, how could <s>Śiva</s> be unconditioned?

body.text: bindvādyagrahaṇe tatkṣobhādyapyasya na yuktam, ajñātasya karaṇāsaṃbhavāadityāha-
body.translated_text: If <s>Bindu</s> etc. are not apprehended [by Śiva], then His agitating them etc. would also be inappropriate, since it is impossible to act upon what is unknown—he says—

children.translated_text: How could He be an agent while lacking knowledge of His instrument (<s>kāraṇa</s>)? || 301 ||

body.text:
kiñcā''tmanāmapi śivasamānaguṇatvāddharmirūpatvād-
dharmarūpajñānānabhyupagame sukhādisaṃvedanarūpo bhogo na sambhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if knowledge in the form of a property (<s>dharma</s>) is not accepted for the selves too, who share the same qualities as <s>Śiva</s> and are in the form of property-bearers (<s>dharmin</s>), then enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) in the form of experience of pleasure etc. would be impossible—he says—

body.text: puruṣo vā kathaṃ buddhiṃ paśyet śaktyā tayā vinā |
body.translated_text: Or how could <s>Puruṣa</s> (the soul) perceive <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) without that <s>Śakti</s>?
And this being the case—

children.translated_text: This entire [universe] would be utter darkness without the lamp of <s>Śakti</s>. || 302 ||
What else would arise? And what could the Lord accomplish if He were powerless?
If <s>Śakti</s> is not accepted, the entire world would be devoid of all activity for the sake of enjoyment and liberation—that is the meaning. || 302

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: Although non-different [from <s>Śambhu</s>], <s>Śakti</s> is held to be distinct from <s>Śambhu</s>, being inherent [in Him]. || 303 ||
Just as [two varieties of] lentil—<s>masūra</s> and <s>aṅguṣṭha</s>—though [of the same species] are not [entirely] identical, for the stated reasons.
Just as a particular grain called <s>masūra</s> (lentil) and another of the same species called <s>aṅguṣṭha</s> differ from each other in some respect,

children.text: evaṃ śivaśaktyorvastvantaratvābhāve'pi dharmidharmatayā bhedaḥ siddhaḥ | atra ca
children.translated_text: so too, even though <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> are not different substances, their distinction as property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) and property (<s>dharma</s>) is established. And here,
having accepted their unity as belonging to the same class, the illustration is stated in this manner;
in reality, <s>aṅguṣṭha</s> and <s>masūra</s> lentils are [indeed] different. Thus, even though <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> are distinct as property-bearer and property,
due to the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), they are not separate like two different selves—he says: 'nor separate, as stated.' || 303 ||
Having thus established the distinction of <s>Śakti</s> and the possessor of <s>Śakti</s> as property and property-bearer, even though they are not different substances,
he concludes—
Though non-different, She is distinct; therefore She is inherent (<s>samavāyinī</s>) in <s>Śambhu</s>. || 304 ||
She is innate, rooted in Him, like the radiance of the sun—pure and stainless.

body.text: nanu bindvākhyayaiva śaktyā śivaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati, kimanayā ? ata āha-
body.translated_text: But [one might object:] <s>Śiva</s> could accomplish effects through <s>Śakti</s> called <s>Bindu</s> alone—what need is there for this [other Śakti]? To this he says—

children.translated_text: For this blessed Lord, by a <s>Śakti</s> that is utterly separate from His own Self, || 305 ||
never accomplishes anything, nor does He know anything.
Since <s>Bindu</s>, being a material cause, is external [to Śiva] and insentient, without [His own] inherent <s>Śakti</s> which is of the nature of consciousness,

children.text: vinā śivo na bindvādivastu viṣayīkartuṃ tatkṣobhādi cotpādayituṃ śaknoti, kumbhakārāderapi
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> cannot make <s>Bindu</s> and other realities His objects nor produce their agitation etc., since even a potter and the like
are seen [to act] only by virtue of possessing the power of consciousness. || 305 ||

body.text:
yadyevaṃ śaktyā vineśvarasyāpyakiñcitkaratvāt saiva jagatkāraṇatvenāstu | yadāhuḥ- 
yayā vinā na sarvajñaḥ so'pi tasyai namo'stu te iti, tanna, śakterdharmatvenāśrayaṃ 
vinā'vasthānāsaṃbhavāt | tadāśrayaḥ sa eṣa śaktimān saṅkalpamātreṇa viśvakartetyāha-
body.translated_text: If so, since even the Lord is incapable of doing anything without <s>Śakti</s>, let Her alone be the cause of the world. As they say: 'She without whom even the Omniscient [is powerless]—salutation to Her!' No, because <s>Śakti</s>, being a property, cannot exist without a substratum. That substratum is this very possessor of <s>Śakti</s>, who creates the universe by mere will—he says—

children.translated_text: Even without having applied [any] specific [effort], the God, the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), is the cause. || 306 ||

body.text: idānīṃ kartṛśaktyā bhedopacāre upādhibhūtaṃ pāramārthikaṃ kāryabhedamāha-
body.translated_text: Now he states the real distinction of effects that serves as the limiting condition for the figurative distinction of the agent's power—
The distinction of effects too would arise from the particular states of the effect.
He elaborates this very point—

children.translated_text: <s>Bindu</s>, whose effects have dissolved [into it], impelled by the <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, || 307 ||
for the sake of creation, maintenance, and the dissolution of the creator's manifestation,
it is <s>Bindu</s> alone, in whom the universe has been long sustained, that sets forth, || 308 ||
reaching a different state, just as [clay] begins [to become] a pot
through the transformation of clay into another state—so too does this [Bindu], previously [undifferentiated]. || 309 ||
Pervaded by the Lord's <s>Śakti</s>, through particular modes of activity,
it works toward the differentiation of effects, even though the Trident-bearer (<s>Śūlin</s>, i.e. <s>Śiva</s>) remains without modification. || 310 ||
Even without undergoing modification Himself, of the [stages of] splitting, drying, and powdering
which arise in the described sequence and are born from different states, || 311 ||
the hot-rayed [sun] would be the producer, as [it acts upon] the lotus; so too is <s>Śiva</s>,
the agent of creation and other effects, though without modification, possessing <s>Śakti</s>. || 312 ||

body.text:
nanu kimarthamasau sṛṣṭyādikāryaṃ karotīti cet, paśvanugrahāyeti brūmaḥ | yadyevaṃ 
sarvānugrāhakatve'pi śivaḥ kathaṃ keṣāñcideva mokṣaṃ karoti na sarveṣām, ayamevāsya 
svabhāvo vā tarhyantaḥ rāgadveṣayuktaḥ syāt | ata āha-
body.translated_text: Now, if one asks 'For what purpose does He perform the acts of creation etc.?'—we say: for the grace of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>). If so, even though He bestows grace upon all, why does <s>Śiva</s> grant liberation to some alone and not to all? Or if this is simply His nature, then He would be inwardly possessed of attachment and aversion. To this he says—

children.translated_text: Just as, without partiality (<s>anapekṣa</s>) and instantaneously,
the sun is the cause of melting [of wax] and drying [of clay], though itself without modification, || 313 ||
so too, of souls whose own <s>karmas</s> called merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and demerit (<s>apuṇya</s>) are equal and unequal,
<s>Śiva</s>, though without modification, is the agent of bondage and liberation. || 314 ||

children.text: satyaṃ sarvānugrāhakaḥ śivaḥ | na cāsya rāgādirvidyate, anādimalarahitatvāt |
children.translated_text: It is true that <s>Śiva</s> bestows grace upon all. And He possesses no attachment (<s>rāga</s>) etc., due to His being free from beginningless <s>mala</s> (impurity).

children.text: bandhamokṣakartṛtvaṃ cātmanāmeva, yogyatvādityuktam | tataśca yathaikākāra evārkaḥ
children.translated_text: The agency of bondage and liberation belongs to the souls themselves, due to their [differing] fitness—as stated. Therefore, just as the sun, being of one nature alone,

children.text: svasannidhānena dravatvayogyasya madhūcchiṣṭasya dravatāṃ śoṣatvayogyāyā mṛdaḥ
children.translated_text: by its mere proximity causes the melting of wax which is fit to melt, and the drying

children.text: śuṣkatāṃ ca karoti, tathā śivo'pi pakvamalānāṃ mokṣayogyānāṃ mokṣaṃ karoti,
children.translated_text: of clay which is fit to dry, so too <s>Śiva</s> grants liberation to those whose <s>mala</s> has matured and who are fit for liberation,

children.text: apakvamalānāṃ bandhayogyānāṃ tatpākārthaṃ bandhaṃ karotītyavirodhaḥ | ataścātra
children.translated_text: and produces bondage for those whose <s>mala</s> has not matured and who are fit for bondage, for the sake of ripening that [mala]—thus there is no contradiction. And here,

children.text: puṇyāpuṇyākhyaśabdena- na hṛṣyatyupakāreṇa nāpakāreṇa kupyati | yaḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: by the term 'merit and demerit' (<s>puṇyāpuṇya</s>)—'He who does not rejoice at kindness nor is angered by harm, who is equal

children.text: sarvabhūteṣu jīvanmuktaḥ sa ucyate || iti nyāyenopakārāpakārātmakaṃ
children.translated_text: toward all beings—he is called a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living)'—by this principle, the two kinds of <s>karma</s> consisting of

children.text: karmadvayamucyate | tayormalaparipākavaśāt sāmyabuddhau satyāṃ mokṣo bhavati, tadabhāve
children.translated_text: benefit and harm are meant. When, due to the maturation of <s>mala</s>, there is equanimity toward them, liberation occurs; in its absence,

children.text: tu bandha eva | na tvaścamedhabrahmahatyādi-rūpau puṇyāpuṇyau, tayoḥ sāmyaṃ
children.translated_text: there is bondage alone. But this should not be interpreted as meaning that the equality of merit and demerit in the form of horse-sacrifice and brahmin-murder etc.

children.text: mokṣaheturiti vyākhyeyam, śāstravirodhāt, tādṛśasya karmasāmyasya saṃsārāvasthāyāmapi
children.translated_text: is the cause of liberation, for that would contradict scripture, since such equality of <s>karma</s> is possible even in the state of
<s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), and since [such karmas] are fulfilled merely in their own destruction. Even the equality of all <s>karmas</s>
is a cause only of the state of <s>vijñānakevala</s> (a soul freed from <s>māyā</s> alone); since it cannot be the cause of liberation, and since the maturation of <s>mala</s> alone,
inferable through the sign of the described equality of <s>karma</s>, can be the cause of liberation through the means of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>)—this and more
has been stated by us at length in the <s>Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā</s>. And it has been established by the masters
in the commentaries on the blessed <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>, <s>Kiraṇa</s>, <s>Mataṅga</s>, etc.; therefore let it be ascertained from there. || 313–314 ||

body.translated_text: And therefore—

children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of two <s>karmas</s> whose ripening has been arrested by mutual opposition,
the <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s> descends upon the soul (<s>aṇu</s>). || 315 ||
Of the two [karmas] having opposed results—the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in the form of horse-sacrifice and brahmin-murder etc.,
or two <s>dharma</s>-[karmas] whose fruits are heaven and <s>Brahmaloka</s>, or two <s>adharma</s>-[karmas] whose fruits are <s>Avīci</s> and <s>Raurava</s> [hells]—when these <s>karmas</s>

children.text: sannipāte sati śaivī śivatvadāyikā'nugrāhikā śaktirātmani na patati, tasyā malaparipāka eva
children.translated_text: converge, the <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s> that bestows <s>Śivatva</s> (the state of Śiva), the <s>Śakti</s> of grace, does not descend upon the soul, since [its] descent is heard [in scripture to occur] only upon the maturation of <s>mala</s>.

children.text: pātaśravaṇāt | kintu rodhaśaktireva niyatidvāreṇa viruddhakarmakṣayārthaṃ patati | taduktaṃ
children.translated_text: Rather, it is the obstructing power (<s>rodhaśakti</s>) alone that descends through <s>niyati</s> (cosmic regulation) for the purpose of destroying the opposed <s>karmas</s>. As stated
in the blessed <s>Mataṅga</s>: 'In the ripening of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>...' (<s>Vidyāpāda</s> 13.15) etc.—initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) alone,
which is inseparable from the maturation of <s>mala</s>, is the cause of liberation through the destruction of <s>karma</s>. As stated in the blessed <s>Kiraṇa</s>:

children.text: anekabhavikaṃ karma dagdhabījamivāṇubhiḥ | bhaviṣyadapi saṃruddhaṃ yenedaṃ taddhi
children.translated_text: '<s>Karma</s> accumulated over many lives, like burnt seeds, for the souls; and future [karma] too is arrested—
that [existing karma is exhausted] through experience' (6.19). When <s>mala</s> has matured, the gracious [Śakti] descends. || 315 ||
The moment She descends, [the soul,] with its dense covering shaken off,
sees its own Self, with the defilement of <s>mala</s> pacified. || 316 ||
Due to the removal of the covering of <s>mala</s>, that which has been freed from it—[the Self's] nature consisting of omniscience etc.—shines forth—that is the meaning. || 316 ||

body.translated_text: For indeed, he is liberated at that very moment when he is 'smelled' (touched) by the will of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.translated_text: Touched by the <s>Śakti</s> of <s>Śiva</s> called initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), he is indeed liberated.

body.translated_text: And for the period after initiation, for the destruction of the bondage of <s>karmas</s> already commenced—

children.translated_text: He continues thereafter with regular (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) rituals. || 317 ||

body.translated_text: And even then—

children.translated_text: With this very body, the supreme, undivided pervasion
is attained by those great and steadfast ones, the fortunate <s>Śiva</s>-<s>yogins</s>. || 318 ||
Through the practice of <s>yoga</s>, omniscience etc. shine forth in this very [life]—that is the meaning. || 318 ||

body.translated_text: Incidentally, he speaks of the greatness of <s>Śiva</s>-<s>yogins</s>—

children.text: sa punāti dṛśā vācā caraṇena kareṇa ca |
children.translated_text: He purifies by his gaze, by his speech, by his feet, and by his hand,
rivers, communities, gardens, cities, and the like, through his mere play. || 319 ||

body.translated_text: How much more then this person who has taken refuge [in him], terrified of worldly existence!
Now the author of the treatise offers salutation to his own guru—

children.translated_text: Salutation to such a one, our guru, [who is] the splendor of <s>Śiva</s>, || 320 ||
the treasure of the jewels of <s>yoga</s> that bestow infinite fruits.

body.translated_text: By whom was this treatise composed? To this he says—

children.translated_text: By one whose mind was purified through the vision of what was composed by <s>Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, || 321 ||
this <s>Ratnatrayaparīkṣā</s> (Examination of the Three Jewels) was composed by <s>Śrīkaṇṭhasūri</s>.
By me, who follow the excellent commentary of the blessed <s>Rāmakaṇṭha</s>,
the meaning of the <s>Ratnatrayaparīkṣā</s> has been briefly illuminated. || 322 ||
|| The <s>Ratnatrayaparīkṣā</s> is complete. ||
By that lord among poets who composed the <s>Āścaryasāra</s>, rich in aesthetic savor (<s>rasa</s>),
the <s>Pāṣaṇḍāpajaya</s> (Defeat of Heretics), the <s>Kāvyatilaka</s> (Ornament of Poetry), and the <s>Bhaktaprakāśa</s> (Illumination of the Devotee),
and the <s>Abhyudaya</s> (Prosperity) among dramas, and the excellent commentaries on Śaiva [texts] with beautiful speech—
by that <s>Aghoraśiva</s>, the <s>Ratnatrayollekhinī</s> (Illumination of the Three Jewels) has been well composed.
Thus the <s>Ratnatrayollekhinī</s> composed by <s>Aghoraśivācārya</s> is complete. ||
